title: Angular signals do not work in Vitest (NG0303)
body:
### Describe the bug

I'll preface this by saying I'm not entirely sure if this is a Vitest issue or `@analogjs/vitest-angular` issue, as I'm confused as to how they work together.

Basically signals in an Angular component are ignored, and the error `NG0303: Can't set value of the 'x' input on the 'Y' component. Make sure that the 'Z' property is declared as an input using the input() or model() function or the @Input() decorator.` is logged to stderr.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/Ehesp/angular-testing-library-repro/tree/main

```
npm i
npm test
```

A simple component like so:

```ts
@Component()
export class DividerComponent {
  name = input<string>();
}
```

A simple test:


```ts
it.only('renders a divider with text', async () => {
    const { container } = await render(DividerComponent, {
      imports: [DividerComponent],
      inputs: {
        name: 'hello',
      },
    });

    screen.debug();

    const textContainer = container.querySelector('.fui-divider__text');
    expect(textContainer).toBeTruthy();
  });
```

The test runs fine, but the signal is set to `undefined` on the component.

Note, this is using `angular-testing-library`, where I originally thought the issue lay (see https://github.com/testing-library/angular-testing-library/issues/548), however it turns out this happens without that library, just using Vitest.

It could well be https://www.npmjs.com/package/@analogjs/vitest-angular though!

title: `vitest run | head -3` leaves orphaned workers consuming memory (SIGPIPE)
body:
Vitest's default fork pool has a bug where worker processes become orphaned when the parent process receives SIGPIPE. This commonly occurs with `npx vitest run 2>&1 | head -10`, which is frequently used by AI coding assistants to limit output and conserve context window space. This can quickly, silently, and indefinitely consume all your computer's RAM.

### Reproduction

**Repository:** https://github.com/davidbludlow/vitest-orphaned-workers-bug-reproduction

```bash
git clone https://github.com/davidbludlow/vitest-orphaned-workers-bug-reproduction
cd vitest-orphaned-workers-bug-reproduction  
npm install
npx vitest run 2>&1 | head -3
ps aux | grep 'node (vitest'  # Shows orphaned workers
# Then after you are convinced that this is a bug, you can forcefully kill the processes, before
# they crash your system. I basically have to completely reboot WSL Ubuntu if I let the orphaned
# vitest processes run free for about 5 minutes, they consume so many resources.
pkill -f vitest
```

### Expected vs Actual

**Expected:** All processes terminate when parent receives SIGPIPE  
**Actual:** Workers remain orphaned, consume ~3.6GB RAM each, can crash system at ~7GB total

### Impact

- **Common trigger:** AI agents frequently use `| head` to limit output for context conservation
- **Shell patterns:** Also probably affects other early-exit pipes
- **Silent failure:** Initial output appears normal, workers orphaned in background. You might not notice it until after Linux becomes almost entirely unresponsive.

### Workaround

```javascript
// vitest.config.js
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    pool: 'threads',  // Instead of default 'forks'
  },
});
```

### System Info

- **Vitest:** 3.2.4
- **Node:** 22.14.0 (via Volta node version manager)
- **OS:** Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS, run on WSL 2 on Windows 11 64-bit, but my guess is that the bug affects all Linux/Unix

npm

title: Performance regression when upgrading from Vitest v3 to v4 with single worker thread
body:
### Describe the bug

After upgrading from Vitest v3 to v4, I’m seeing a consistent ~2× slowdown in our test suite when running with a single worker thread.

**Prior behavior (v3)**
Using the following config:
```js
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    globals: true,
    environment: 'node',
    pool: 'threads',
    poolOptions: { threads: { singleThread: true } },
  },
})
```
Execution time:
```
Duration 846ms
(transform 137ms, setup 0ms, collect 153ms, tests 9ms, environment 0ms, prepare 193ms)
```

**After upgrade (v4)**
Updated config per migration guide, replacing deprecated poolOptions:
```js
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    globals: true,
    environment: 'node',
    pool: 'threads',
    maxWorkers: 1,
  },
})
```

Execution time:
```
Duration 1.79s
(transform 122ms, setup 0ms, collect 193ms, tests 15ms, environment 0ms, prepare 35ms)
```

**Observations**
- Test execution time is nearly doubled from 846ms to 1.79s. (results from the minimal reproductions on StackBlitz)
- On my main project, I have almost the same difference (from 54s to 138s)

Thanks for vitest, it is awesome 😊

### Reproduction

title: .locator() method missing from TypeScript types for page and Locator
body:
### Describe the bug

The `.locator()` method works at runtime but is missing from TypeScript type definitions, causing the error:

```
Property 'locator' does not exist on type 'Locator'.
```

This occurs for both `page.locator()` and `locator.locator()` (chaining).

**Use case:**
Testing component loading states where skeleton elements are rendered with `data-slot` attributes:

```typescript
const table = page.getByRole("table");
const skeleton = table.locator('[data-slot="skeleton"]').first();
await expect.element(skeleton).toBeVisible();
```

**Question:**
What's the recommended way to query elements by CSS selector (e.g., `[data-slot="skeleton"]`) in vitest browser mode? If `.locator()` isn't part of the public API, is there an alternative approach that doesn't require `data-testid` attributes? Are we supposed to define [Custom Locators](https://vitest.dev/guide/browser/locators.html#custom-locators) for these cases? That seems like a lot of overhead for general cases.

title: vitest@4: Non-deterministic module mocking behavior
body:
### Describe the bug

I've been upgrading a sizable TS codebase (~400 test files, ~4000 test cases)  to vite 7 and vitest 4. I'm nearly done, but a very strange problem that I am running into is that I sometimes get this following error:

```
Error: [vitest] There was an error when mocking a module. If you are using "vi.mock" factory, make sure there are no top level variables inside, since this call is hoisted to top of the file. Read more: https://vitest.dev/api/vi.html#vi-mock
...
Caused by: Error: Module "/path/to/internal/fileModule.ts" was mistakenly invalidated during fetch phase.
```

This is happening with 2 different reusable component files (let's just call them `fileModule.ts`), and in a non-deterministic set of test files (which import and test functions that themselves import the problematic invalidated module files). 

In some cases, I am mocking the internals of `fileModule.ts` with a factory `vi.mock`, spreading the results of `importOriginal`. And I also have actual test files that test the contents of `fileModule.ts`

Digging in, it seems to possibly be related to vite's module caching (https://github.com/vitejs/vite/blob/bb85bd751e4568c707612b708deaba67f8af4ca3/packages/vite/src/module-runner/runner.ts#L293). 

I've tried a number of things, including messing with the vitest config settings, vite config settings, `vi.hoisted` on some of the mocked functions. 

~50% of the time, running the test suite passes all tests. ~50% of the time there are >1 of these `mistakenly invalidated during fetch phase` errors (often 1 or 2, sometimes up to 4).

We never experienced these issues in `vitest@3`

I thought that this could be some sort of race condition, but I also tried using `maxWorkers: 1` and the problem was still present.

Any ideas what might be going on here?

unknown

title: Enhance Chai assertions
body:
### Clear and concise description of the problem

Following [this discussion](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/discussions/8789#discussioncomment-14771676), I think it would be good to provide Chai-like assertions for all Jest-like assertions.

Especially in the case of spies/mocks, the assertions could be similar to [sinon-chai](https://github.com/chaijs/sinon-chai) or consistent with the existing Jest assertions.

For examples:
- `toHaveBeenCalled()` -> `to.have.been.called` or `to.have.been.called()`
- `toHaveBeenCalledTimes(n)` -> `to.have.callCount(n)` or `to.have.been.calledTimes(n)`
- `toHaveBeenCalledWith(args)` ->  `to.have.been.calledWith(args)`
- ...



### Suggested solution

Assuming the new assertions should be consistent with the existing ones, the changes could be just adding new assertion names in [jest-expect.ts](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/main/packages/expect/src/jest-expect.ts). For example: 
```ts
def(['toHaveBeenCalled', 'toBeCalled', 'called'], function () { ...}
```

However, the file might have to be renamed to something like `jest-chai-expect.ts`, because it's not only about Jest anymore.


### Alternative

If we don't want to mix the the Jest and Chai assertions in the same file, another solution could be moving the assertion functions to a new shared module, then defining the Jest assertions in `jest-expect.ts` and the Chai assertions in `chai-expect.ts`.


### Additional context

I'd be glad to create a PR, once this feature request is accepted and an implementation is recommended.

title: v4 coverage include/exclude logic breaks advanced use cases
body:
### Describe the bug

The refactor introduced in v4 to move away from `test-exclude`, while a significant improvement to on-disk package size, also introduced a change in behavior by performing direct filesystem access within the replacement.  The previous v3 `test-exclude` behavior operated solely on the path strings and matched them to include/exclude patterns.  The introduction of the direct file system access is problematic for several use cases such as:
* Vite plugins that provided load hooks for virtual files that may need to be processed for coverage.  (virtual files may contain relevant code from actual application files.  Source maps can map back to the files)
* Reporting coverage of node package/libraries that contain source maps. (first-party libraries being common but analysis of third-party package usage is also a possibility)

Additionally, there is the potential for performance degradation due to a synchronous file system operation being performed in a loop over every file included in the coverage.  For large projects this may be problematic.

Relevant `existsSync` call: https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/9b75ec5f2fa46daaaa649493eb7f643a1cc9f51a/packages/vitest/src/node/coverage.ts#L175


### Reproduction

For the first above use case:
1) Create a new Angular application for next version: `npx @angular/cli@next new vitest-coverage --defaults`
2) Change into directory and install coverage: `npm i @vitest/coverage-v8`
3) Run tests via `ng test --coverage --no-watch` and note no coverage report information.
4) Force install vitest 3: `npm i --force vitest@3 @vitest/coverage-v8@3`
5) Re-run tests and note coverage report with files.
6) Reinstall vitest 4: `npm i vitest@4 @vitest/coverage-v8@4`
7) Manually edit the vitest package to remove the `existsSync` call here: `node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/coverage.CSfvENE1.js` (line 2784)
8) Re-run tests and note coverage report with files.

### System Info

```shell
npmPackages:

  vitest: ^4.0.4 => 4.0.4
```

title: Project order changed with v4
body:
### Describe the bug

We're using Vitest at MUI and have 23 packages in our mui-x monorepo. 

In Vitest v3, projects ran sequentially, as you can see [here](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/mui/mui-x/108325/workflows/73b7d9c6-c400-40ff-9846-3081f4136e13/jobs/665288). The next project only started when the previous had finished.

It seems in Vitest v4 this is no longer true. [Projects are interleaved](https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/mui/mui-x/108187/workflows/df70b3d0-2460-43bc-9263-a28ff8e65710/jobs/664225) automatically, which is an issue for us since we use `isolate: false` to speed up tests, which causes the tests to fail. We're also setting `fileParallelism` to false, restricting the maximum number of workers to 1 and defining the projects using the glob syntax (e.g., `projects: 'packages/*/vitest.config.jsdom.mts'`).

I know there's `sequence.groupOrder`, but it is impractical to use when there's 23 packages. We need to ensure numbers don't collide and if we add or remove a new package we'll need to again ensure these numbers are defined as expected. 

Plus, I don't see any mention of a change of behavior in this regard in the migration guide, so I'm unsure whether this change is intended or accidental. 

Ideally, we'd either have the old behavior back or, if not possible, a flag (e.g., `projectParallelism: false`) that we could use to disable project running in parallel. 

### Reproduction

[Here's](https://github.com/mui/mui-x/pull/20102/files/9195b06aa1494f06db986a61fd2f8029338b4208) on our commits that attempt to fix it.

title: expect.toThrow doesn't work correctly if actual is an error from another realm
body:
### Describe the bug

If function throws an error which is instance of another realm, `expect.toThrow` will pass with any expected error instance.

With the given setup: 

```js
import vm from 'node:vm'
const script = new vm.Script('fn = () => { throw new TypeError("oops") }')
const context = {}
vm.createContext(context)
script.runInContext(context)
const { fn } = context
```

all of the following assertions will pass at the same time (!):

```js
expect(fn).toThrow(new TypeError('oops'))
expect(fn).toThrow(new TypeError('message'))
expect(fn).toThrow(new ReferenceError('oops'))
expect(fn).toThrow(new EvalError('no way'))

title: Global setup/teardown that works with Pinia
body:
### Clear and concise description of the problem

I have tests where I want to initialise global state once, then run all tests using that global state. I use Pinia library to store my global state.
My tests essentially look like this all in a single file:
`AllTests.test.ts`
```ts
describe.sequential('Tests', () => {
  beforeAll(async () => {
    setActivePinia(createPinia())
    initialiseStateInPiniaOnceForAllTests()
  })
  describe.sequential('test category A', () => {
    test('a1', async () => {})
    test('a2', async () => {})
  })
  describe.sequential('test category B', () => {
    test('b1', async () => {})
    test('b2', async () => {})
  })
})
```

This works all well and good.
However, since I have multiple categories of tests, this single file starts to get difficult to navigate.
I searched for ways to split up test categories (for ex.: `'test category A'` and `'test category B'`) into their own files.
However I could not find ways to do what I currently do in `beforeAll`.

I saw someone running into similar issue, and they got around it by implementing CustomReporter:
https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/discussions/6719#discussioncomment-10950374

I suppose that works fine for initialising something external like DB, but I could not seem to get it to work with Pinia (I kept getting error, that I forgot to do `setActivePinia`).

### Suggested solution

It would be nice if I could get something similar to this working, that would be equivalent to snippet I've shared in `AllTests.test.ts` above, but split into multiple files:

`RunOnceBeforeAllTests.ts`
```
runOnceBeforeAllTests(() =>{
    setActivePinia(createPinia())
    initialiseStateInPiniaOnceForAllTests()
})
```

`CategoryA.test.ts`
```
describe.sequential('test category A', () => {
    test('a1', async () => {})
    test('a2', async () => {})
  })
```

`CategoryB.test.ts`
```
describe.sequential('test category B', () => {
    test('b1', async () => {})
    test('b2', async () => {})
  })
```

title: browser: dynamicImportPlugin breaks dynamic imports in web workers
body:

`dynamicImportPlugin`, which is added by default by vitest when using the browser runner, transforms dynamic imports into code that references `globalThis["__vitest_browser_runner__"]`. Vitest is throwing an error when a test contains expect calls within a Promise.all call

### Reproduction

```ts
it('ticks all checkbox', async () => {

it('ticks all checkbox', async () => {

body:
### Describe the bug

After upgrading from v3 to v4, we started seeing sourcemap warnings when running tests.

These warnings come from libraries in `node_modules`, and as far as I can see, point to _existing_ sourcemap files on disk, such as this:

```shell
Sourcemap for "/Users/fotis/oss/vitest-optimizer-sourcemap/node_modules/.pnpm/domutils@3.2.2/node_modules/domutils/lib/esm/feeds.js" points to missing source files
```

I have narrowed this down to the use of `deps.optimizer.ssr.enabled`, but these warnings are emitted even for packages unrelated to those being optimized. I am including more info in the reproduction step below 😌 

(I vaguely remember seeing these warnings in past Vitest versions, but they had gone away for a while 💭 )

### Reproduction

I have a reproduction at https://github.com/fpapado/vitest-optimizer-ssr-sourcemap-warning, simply:

```shell
nvm use
corepack enable

pnpm install

- Using vitest v3 (`pnpm add -DE vitest@3`) shows no such warnings
- In v4, if `deps.optimize.ssr.enabled` is `true`, but `include` is empty or not defined, then there are no warnings

title: `@vitest/coverage-istanbul` returns the combined sourcemap where it should be returning the non-combined sourcemap
body:
### Describe the bug

Rollup's transform hook expects `map` to be the sourcemap mapped from the `code` passed to the hook to the `code` returned from the hook.

This `onFileTransform` hook instead returns the `map` from the original `code` (because it passes the result of `getCombinedSourcemap()` to `instrumentSync` and that returns the combined source map)
https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/353ee5bbcb9e1fad3147e067cd8ba1b10ba71da2/packages/coverage-istanbul/src/provider.ts#L65-L83

This causes the sourcemap generated by Vite to be wrong.

### Reproduction

Add
```js
    if (id.endsWith('/math.ts')) {
      console.log(`${code}//# sourceMappingURL=data:application/json;base64,${btoa(JSON.stringify(map))}`)
    }
```
after this line:
https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/353ee5bbcb9e1fad3147e067cd8ba1b10ba71da2/packages/coverage-istanbul/src/provider.ts#L81

This is the result I got locally: [sourcemap visualizer](https://evanw.github.io/source-map-visualization/#)
The input TS file is shown as the original file. But the JS file should be shown here as it is already transformed to JS by Vite.

title: Subpath import conditions are not processed
body:
### Describe the bug

If we have a [package subpath imports](https://nodejs.org/api/packages.html#subpath-imports) defined with custom conditions, vitest always runs resolve to `import` and `default` condition. 

Say we have sub path import with conditions. If we run the scripts in general with `bun`, `nodejs` etc the import conditions are respected.

resolve:  {

title: DevTools: Preserve devtools settings between sessions
body:
### Clear and concise description of the problem

Preserve Playwright Chrome DevTools settings between vitest browser mode sessions.

Use cases:
- remember ignore listing settings
- remember source maps settings
- remember ui preferences (close needless side panels, resize)

Without it, each browser run requires 15sec of manual adjusting devtools settings. For example, I have to disable ignore listing as I debug node_modules code often.

### Suggested solution

Chrome user data dir is stored in a cache directory, persisted between browser runs.

---

Chrome has --user-data-dir option for storing persistent user data.
I tried this in vitest 4:

```ts
      provider: playwright({
        launchOptions: {
          args: [
            `--user-data-dir=${process.cwd()}/node_modules/.cache/playwright-user-data-dir`,
          ],
        },
      }),
```

But it errors, and suggests using API I am not sure is public for vitest users:
> error during close browserType.launch: Pass userDataDir parameter to 'browserType.launchPersistentContext(userDataDir, options)' instead of specifying '--user-data-dir' argument

Even if there is a way to hack it on my side, I feel like persistent devtools settings is a useful feature that should be on by default.

### Alternative

_No response_

await expect(JSON.stringify(['foo', 'bar'], null, 2)).toMatchFileSnapshot("demo.json");
```

title: toMatchScreenshot should not generate screenshots if they pass the comparator
body:
### Describe the bug

When vitest is run with `--update`, `toMatchScreenshot` unconditionally emits new screenshots (even when the test would otherwise pass). This means that if you have a non-deterministic UI element, every run with `--update` produces a new screenshot.

This causes problems when used in CI (where it's recommended to run with `--update`). The presence of updated screenshots does not indicate the *need* to update the screenshots. This means we have to run CI twice:

- First, to see if we need to update the screenshot files
- Second, to get those updates. Even then, we have to be clever not to include unecessary changes.

It seems that `--update` shouldn't unconditionally update. If you want unconditional updates, it's easy enough to wipe the `__screenshots__` directory and run the tests.

### Reproduction

1. Clone the example repo: `git clone https://github.com/djrenren/vitestScreenshotTestFailure`
2. Run tests (successfully) `cd vitestScreenshotTestFailure && npm test:browser`
3. Observe the screenshots have changed: `git status` 

The example repo renders a single random pixel on a canvas. Enough to differ but not enough to fail the test.

title: `task` fixture is undefined in file-scoped fixtures
body:
### Describe the bug

When using test.extend() with scope: "file", the task fixture is undefined. The same fixture definition works correctly without the file scope.

### Expected behavior
task should be defined and accessible in file-scoped fixtures, at minimum providing task.file so fixtures can access file-level metadata like the filepath.

### Actual behavior
task is undefined when the fixture has scope: "file".

Apologies if this is intentional, I couldn't find anything in the docs that suggests the built-in task fixture should ever be undefined.

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitest-dev-vitest-ggimrrx6?file=test%2Frepro.test.ts

```typescript
import { it as vitestIt, describe, expect } from "vitest"

const itFails = vitestIt.extend<{ foobar: string }>({
  foobar: [
    async ({ task }, use) => {
      // Worth noting that `expect` when taken from the dependencies is also undefined, so this uses global expect
      expect(task).toBeDefined()
      await use("foobar")
    },
    { scope: "file", auto: true },
  ]
})

const itWorks = vitestIt.extend<{ foobar: string }>({
  foobar: async ({ task, expect }, use) => {
    // But here expect is defined and works
    expect(task).toBeDefined()
    await use("foobar")
  }
})

describe("file-scope-fixture-repro", () => {
  itFails("should work", async ({ foobar, expect }) => {
    expect(foobar).toBe("foobar")
  })

  itWorks("should work", async ({ foobar, expect }) => {
    expect(foobar).toBe("foobar")
  })
})
```

title: setupFile dependencies cached when isolate: false
body:
### Describe the bug

This happens when run with `isolate: false` and `maxWorkers: 1`. At MUI we use this mode because our suite runs twice as fast under it. It also allows us to control parallelism more optimally across projects using sharding. However, it has some strange behaviors when it comes to setup/teardown hooks being removed and setup files not always being cleared from cache.

An `afterEach` hook that is being set up in a dependency of a setup file gets cleared after the suite runs. The setup file seems to get cleared from module cache between each suite, but its dependencies don't. 


### Reproduction

title: The `coverage.autoUpdate` rewrite strips intended newlines from config files
body:
### Describe the bug

Using `coverage.autoUpdate` in a configuration to update the thresholds will strip intended whitespace/newlines from the bottom of configuration files.

This goes against common linting rules like `eslint/prettier-prettier` that enforce newlines at the end of files, meaning that on-update the build will generally fail CI builds, if linting is enabled there.

The workaround is to ignore the role in the second-to-last line:
```ts
import { configDefaults, defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    globals: true,

    coverage: {
      enabled: true,
      provider: 'istanbul',
      thresholds: {
        autoUpdate: (newThreshold: number): number =>
          newThreshold >= Math.floor(newThreshold) + 0.2 ? Math.floor(newThreshold) : Math.floor(newThreshold) - 1,
        statements: 56,
        branches: 47,
        functions: 58,
        lines: 56,
      },
      reporter: ['json', 'json-summary', 'text', 'cobertura', 'html'],
      include: ['lib/**/*.ts'],
    },

    exclude: [...configDefaults.exclude, '**/dist/**/*'],
  },
  // eslint-disable-next-line prettier/prettier
});
```

but it'd be nice if only the `thresholds` part of the file was replaced, preferably just the numbers. In general it's hard to conform to all linters, since something like `56.<many digits>1` may want to wrap to a new line:
```
lines:
  56.0000000000000000000000000000000000001
```

so maybe the real solution is to offer a post-update script that could be run to format. Appending to our "test" script to format is ugly and also doesn't work in Monorepos that lint/format from the top-level, not individually in each package.

### Reproduction

Configure eslint with the `prettier` plugin.

Run tests, the coverage doesn't even have to change.

See that the newline is stripped off of `vitest.config.ts`.

title: Inconsistent Test Behavior Due to Module Caching
body:
### Describe the bug

When running tests with `sequence.concurrent` set to true. Results in tests sharing module state between tests resulting in unexpectedly flaky tests not actually failing regardless of if shuffle is set or not.

The example snippet:
```ts
let driver: ExternalLibrary | undefined;

const externalDriver: ExampleDriver = {
  init: (config) => {
    driver = ExternalLibrary.load(config);
  },

  track: (event, properties) => {
    void driver?.track(event, properties);
  },
};
```

The expected flaky test:
```ts
  it('example driver calls internal track with expected values', async ({
    expect,
  }) => {
    const exampleDriver = (await import('./externalDriver')).default;

    exampleDriver.track(exampleEvent, exampleProperties);

    expect(mockedLibraryMethods.track).toHaveBeenCalledWith(
      exampleEvent,
      exampleProperties
    );
  });
```

The expectation that a test that calls `externalDriver.track` without `externalDriver.init` called first would fail if we check if the external library's `track` method is called with the same arguments as the internal track function.


### Reproduction

With `sequence.concurrent` set to `true` the tests always pass. This is unexpected due to `init` needing to be called before the track function for the internal driver to actually be set. My expectation is that these tests should be flaky and fail 50% of the time.

With `sequence.concurrent` set to `false` the second test always fails. Which matches the expected behavior.

maintainer_reply:
Can you explain which Vitest feature is not working as intended for you?

There seem many factors (e.g. concurrent, shuffle, beforeEach, vi.mock, vi.resetModules, etc.) and overall the behavior seems working expected. From what I tested, `concurrent` tests would run two `beforeEach + reset modules` before starting neither of imports, so these two tests end up importing same module.

For example, this is what I see with debug logging https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitest-inconsistent-module-caching-plp6h8ds?file=src%2FexternalDriver.test.ts

```js
[reset] example driver loads the internal client on init
[reset] example driver calls internal track with expected values
[import-1]
[import-2]
[init]
[track]
```

Maybe one thing could be said that, `shuffle` should reverse `init` and `track` to fail test by 50% of chance, but this shouldn't practically matter in general since `concurrent + shuffle` spawns both test at the same time anyways.

For now, let me flag this as "needs reproduction" as I couldn't see anything actionable from the current reproduction.

maintainer_reply:
The image without browser and OS information is the screenshot that's captured automatically when tests fail.

The CLI output looks like this (using `diff` just to highlight the important bit):
```diff
 FAIL   chromium  button.test.ts > button visual regression
Error: expect(element).toMatchScreenshot()

No existing reference screenshot found; a new one was created. Review it before running tests again.

Reference screenshot:
  <path>/__screenshots__/button.test.ts/button-visual-regression-1-chromium-darwin.png


+ Failure screenshot:
+  - __screenshots__/button.test.ts/button-visual-regression-1.png
```

You can disable automatic screenshot captures by setting `test.browser.screenshotFailures` to `false`, its default value is `!browser.ui` so that's why it gets generated when running in headless mode and without the `--update` flag (when `toMatchScreenshot` creates a reference for the first time, the test fails).

The folder those screenshots are saved in is configurable with `test.browser.screenshotDirectory`, but that's also the default folder `toMatchScreenshot` saves screenshots to:
```
`${root}/${testFileDirectory}/${screenshotDirectory}/${testFileName}/${arg}-${browserName}-${platform}${ext}`
```

title: relative benchmark.compare
body:
### Clear and concise description of the problem

When using benchmark.compare you must use it on the same system with the same load. This makes it hard to identify regressions in CI environments.

### Suggested solution

Run a mini benchmark that tests some generic things, like some math that will likely never be optimized and some memory copying.

Then use the result of that mini benchmark to scale the results of the actual benchmark. That way it's more likely that different systems will still get the same results.

### Alternative

When comparing in CI, first checkout and build the main branch, run the benchmark, then checkout the PR branch, and run benchmark.compare.

This is most accurate but also costly in terms of CI compute, elapsed time, and setup work for the CI of the project.

### Additional context

_No response_

title: Circular ESM imports fail with "Cannot read properties of undefined" during module initialization
body:
### Describe the bug

When ESM modules have circular dependencies, Vitest doesn't handle them correctly during initialization, causing imported modules to be `undefined` even though they should be partially available as per ESM specification.

This appears to be a regression or incomplete fix of #4143 that supposedly fixed circular import handling

### Reproduction

Repository: https://github.com/lehni/vitest-circular-import-repro

```bash
git clone https://github.com/lehni/vitest-circular-import-repro.git
cd vitest-circular-import-repro
npm install
npm test

The Issue

The reproduction demonstrates a realistic scenario: a centralized logging utility that accesses the app instance.

Circular dependency chain:
1. app.js imports models/index.js
2. models/model-b.js imports utils.js (to use the log() utility)
3. utils.js imports app.js (to access app.log()) ← circular!

Error:
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'log')
  at log utils.js:6:14
  at Function.configure models/model-b.js:6:8
  at App.addModels app.js:24:18
  at new App app.js:6:10

Expected Behavior

In native Node ESM, circular imports result in partially initialized modules being available. When utils.js imports app.js during the circular reference, it should receive the module namespace object (even though the default export may be undefined initially).

The test should:
1. Successfully import all modules
2. Execute the model configuration
3. Verify that '[APP] Configuring ModelB' was logged

Actual Behavior

The module import fails with Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'log') because app is completely undefined in utils.js, preventing the test from even running.

title: Global `vi.mock()` inside root `setupFiles` is not executed for workspace library imports in Nx + pnpm monorepo
body:
### Describe the bug

**Environment**

- Vitest version: v3.x
- pnpm: 9.x
- Node: 22
- Workspace tool: Nx monorepo (21+)
- Package layout: pnpm workspaces
- Test runner invoked via Nx or pnpm command 
- Root-level vitest.config.ts defining global setupFiles

**Note**:
Previously these shared libraries were consumed using TypeScript path aliases, and the same global mock pattern worked correctly. After migrating to pnpm workspaces ("name": "@shared/ui" etc.), the issue appeared.

**Problem summary**

In a large Nx + pnpm workspace monorepo, I have a shared testing utility library with a global setup file:
```
libs/shared/testing/src/setupTests.tsx
```

It contains a global mock for a module from another workspace package:

```
import { ComponentType } from 'react';

const withI18n = (Component: ComponentType<any>) => {
  // custom HOC logic...
};

vi.mock('@shared/ui/src/i18n-context', async () => {
  console.log('[setupTests] vi.mock callback executed');
  const actual = await vi.importActual('@shared/ui/src/i18n-context');
  return { ...actual, withI18n };
});
```

Root-level config:

```
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    ...
    globals: true,
    setupFiles: [
      path.resolve(__dirname, './libs/shared/testing/src/setupTests.tsx'),
    ],
  },
});

```

**Expected behavior**

- The setup file should run.
- The vi.mock() callback should be executed.
- All imports of @shared/ui/src/i18n-context should use the mocked implementation.

This previously worked when resolving these modules through TypeScript path aliases.

**Actual behavior**

After switching these libraries to pnpm workspace packages:

- The setup file runs (verified with logs).
- The vi.mock callback never executes.
- The debug console.log inside the callback never appears.
- Tests load the unmocked implementation.
- Tests depending on the mocked withI18n fail.

So the issue is not simply “mock not applied” — the mock factory function is never invoked at all.

**Monorepo structure**

```
libs/
  shared/
    testing/
      src/setupTests.tsx
    ui/
      src/i18n-context.tsx

```

Both `@shared/ui` and `@shared/testing` are pnpm workspace packages with a `package.json` containing their `"name"` fields.
User code imports:
```
import { withI18n } from '@shared/ui/src/i18n-context';
```

With TypeScript path aliases → mock applied correctly.
With pnpm workspace packages → mock callback not executed.

**Why this appears to be a Vitest issue**

- The setup file executes normally.
- The vi.mock() statement is registered.
- The callback never executes.
The module specifier matches exactly.

The only difference between working and not working setups is the switch from TS path aliases → pnpm workspace packages.

### Reproduction

I can provide a minimal public repo demonstrating:

- Nx + pnpm workspace
- libs/shared/ui
- libs/shared/testing containing setupTests.tsx
- Root vitest.config.ts
- A test showing:
   - The setup file runs
   - The vi.mock callback does not run
   - The workspace module is not mocked

### System Info

```shell
irrelevant
```

### Used Package Manager

title: Code coverage file overmatching
body:
### Describe the bug

Vitest coverage will overmatch files if you run vitest in a monorepo where one package path is a substring of another package path.

e.g. `my-repo/packages/app` and `my-repo/packages/app-utils`

coverage include glob is set to something like `src/**/*.ts`

when running the tests in `packages/app-utils` everything is normal

when running the tests in `packages/app` the coverage calculation is including everything both in `packages/app/src/` and `packages/app-utils/src`

a naive solution would be to adjust this section of the vitest node coverage:
```javascript
    // File outside project root with default allowExternal
    if (this.options.allowExternal === false && roots.every(root => !filename.startsWith(root))) {

...
```

to check root as a complete path
```javascript
    // File outside project root with default allowExternal
    if (this.options.allowExternal === false && roots.every(root => !filename.startsWith(root + '/'))) {

...
```

title: html reporter not working when metadata served with content-encoding of 'gzip'
author: dezsiszabi
maintainer_reply:
I agree the current Vitest side trick is brittle, but I think technically your server responding with
- content-encoding: gzip
- content-type: application/gzip

is incorrect. content-type should be `application/json` since that's the result when browser natively handles decompression. That's what Vitest client assumes around the code of `registerMetadata`.

body:
### Describe the bug

I'm in the process of migrating some tests in a project to run in browser mode. I currently have 507 tests and I started by migrating 3 of those to browser mode. I have made the following changes to my config:

title: expect(object).toBeUndefined causes memory leak
body:
### Describe the bug

Expecting an object to be undefined causes a memory leak that results in the test executing infinitely until the heap runs out of memory. This happens regardless of whether expect(object).toBeUndefined() or expect(object).toBe(undefined) is called.

### Reproduction

Code: https://github.com/LavCorps/Alter-Ego/blob/1937ee589d1855d6dafa43a1369bad43cf539c2f/Test/Classes/GameEntityFinder.test.js#L161

The test itself is actually incorrect here, as the function *does* return a value, but that shouldn't cause a memory leak.

EDIT: Upon further inspection, I suspect it has to do with pretty-format attempting to display circular references, as RoomItem contains a reference to Game, which itself contains references to RoomItems, and so on. This has been mended in newer commits to make game a private field accessible with a getter, but I imagine pretty-format being unable to display circular references without looping infinitely will be a problem for others.

title: Options coverage.include and coverage.exclude do not work as expected
body:
### Describe the bug

Hello! I am migrating from v3 to v4 and found that new coverage include/exclude logic in v4 does not quite match what was working in v3 and seems like a bug.

### Case 1: I want to include all files, but exclude files from top-level

**Coverage options**:
```ts
coverage: {
      include: [
        // all .js,.ts,.tsx files
        '**/*.ts',
      ],
      exclude: [
        // exclude .ts files for top-level
        '*.ts',
      ],
}
```

**Expected behavior**: files inside folders are included in coverage and files on top-level - are not

**Actual behavior**: all files are not included

**Potential fix**: Do not use [`contains` options for `picomatch.isMatch`](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/v4.0.16/packages/vitest/src/node/coverage.ts#L165). When I remove it, I achieve expected behavior.

### Case 2: I want to exclude all dirs with some particular name even if it happens that CWD already includes such name

**Ignore Name**: foo

**CWD**: /Users/iam/code/foo

**Coverage options**:
```ts
coverage: {
      include: [
        // all .js,.ts,.tsx files
        '**/*.ts',
      ],
      exclude: [
        // exclude files in any "foo" folders 
        '**/foo/**',
      ],
}
```

**Expected behavior**: all .ts files inside CWD are included in coverage, except files that are under folders with name "foo"

**Actual behavior**: all files are not included, because CWD is ignored

**Potential fix**: Use [relative filename with `picomatch.isMatch`](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/v4.0.16/packages/vitest/src/node/coverage.ts#L164). When I use `path.relative(process.cwd(), filename)` instead of `filename`, I achieve expected behavior.

### Reproduction

title: `RollupError: Parse failure` when environment is jsdom
body:
### Describe the bug

Unorthodox uses of `vi.hoisted()` cause invalid code to be generated during the [`vitest:mocks` transform](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/59f92d403bf97b3145911aaeffbae36b465284c7/packages/mocker/src/node/hoistMocksPlugin.ts#L75), for example:

```js
const mock = (await $.track_reactivity_loss(vi.hoisted(() => import("vitest-mock-extended").then((m) => m.mock))))();
const toaster = vi.hoisted(() => mock());
```

becomes

```js
vi.hoisted(() => import("vitest-mock-extended").then((m) => m.mock))const toaster = vi.hoisted(() => mock());

const mock = (await __vi_import_0__.track_reactivity_loss())();
```

The unorthodox code is initially just a normal

```js
const mock = await vi.hoisted(() => import("vitest-mock-extended").then((m) => m.mock))
const toaster = vi.hoisted(() => mock<Toaster>())
```

but top-level awaits are wrapped by Svelte in `$.track_reactivity_loss` in a previous transform.

Ensure Svelte is setup/configured for the project. Run a test file named `whatever.svelte.test.ts` containing:

import { vi } from "vitest";

const path = await vi.hoisted(() => import("node:path"));

title: Intermittent unhandled rejections: [vitest-worker]: Closing rpc while "fetch" was pending (tests pass, run ends with errors)
body:
### Describe the bug

I’m occasionally seeing Vitest report **unhandled promise rejections** during a test run with the error:

`Error: [vitest-worker]: Closing rpc while "fetch" was pending`

This happens **intermittently** both **locally** and in **CI**, sometimes without any apparent change in the code or environment. The test run still reports all test files and tests as passing, but the run ends with **“Vitest caught N unhandled errors”** and exits with errors.

From what I can tell, the error is raised while Vitest/Vite is importing modules during the test execution (module runner), and the stack trace points to a component barrel export file, but the error message suggests a worker RPC shutdown while a “fetch” is still pending.

## Expected behavior

* No unhandled rejections during the run.
* If a worker is closing while something is pending, I’d expect a clearer actionable message (or a deterministic failure pointing at the underlying cause).
* Test runs that pass should not randomly end with “unhandled errors” without a clear failing file/root cause.

## Actual behavior

* Tests report as passing, but Vitest prints **Unhandled Errors / Unhandled Rejection** and finishes with **Errors > 0**.
* The stack trace often references module imports (Vite module runner) rather than a specific failing assertion.
* Occurs sporadically (hard to reproduce deterministically).

### Reproduction

Unfortunately I don’t have a minimal reproduction yet because it’s intermittent:

title: Misleading error messages relating to spyOn modules. - "Cannot spy on export  "[X]". Module namespace is not configurable in ESM"
body:
### Describe the bug

If I write some code like this: 

```
// main.test.ts
import { vi } from "vitest";
import * as lodash from "lodash";
vi.spyOn(lodash, "after");


```

Then this code will error with 

```typescript
TypeError: Cannot spy on export "after". Module namespace is not configurable in ESM. See: https://vitest.dev/guide/browser/#limitations
 ❯ src/main.test.ts:3:4
      1| import { vi } from "vitest";
      2| import * as lodash from "lodash";
      3| vi.spyOn(lodash, "after");
       |    ^
      4| 

Caused by: TypeError: Cannot redefine property: after
```


This links us to this documentation: 

https://vitest.dev/guide/browser/#limitations

This documentation appears to relate to browser mode specifically. 

However this error occurs whether we are using browser mode or not.* 
This causes some confusion when encountering this error. 

Furthermore - this kind of code _is_ valid in vitest v3. This breaking change is not reflected in in the migration guide. 


https://vitest.dev/guide/migration.html#vitest-4

If I'm understanding it right vitest v4 changes the way spys are applied, and directly use of spyon against external modules is no longer supported at all. 

*Note that we can reproduce a similar error that _does_ only occur in browser mode. 

```typescript
import { vi, describe, it, expect } from "vitest";
import * as foo from "./main";
vi.spyOn(foo, "foo");
```

title: Memory leak in 4.0.18 causing OOM when running multiple tests
body:
## Describe the bug

vitest 4.0.18 has a memory leak when running multiple tests in sequence, causing OOM (Out of Memory) errors. Downgrading to 4.0.4 resolves the issue.

## Reproduction

The tamagui monorepo has a reproduction of this issue:
- Commit with fix (pinning to 4.0.4): https://github.com/tamagui/tamagui/commit/9a8381a175
- Commit before fix (4.0.18): https://github.com/tamagui/tamagui/commit/3ac968be38

Steps to reproduce:
1. Clone https://github.com/tamagui/tamagui at commit `3ac968be38` (using vitest ^4.0.18)
2. Run `bun install && bun run build:js`
3. Run `cd code/compiler/static-tests && bun run test:babel:web`
4. Observe OOM error after running 27 tests

With vitest 4.0.4 (commit `9a8381a175`), the same tests pass in ~1 second without any memory issues.

## System Info

```
Node.js v24.3.0
macOS Darwin 25.2.0
vitest 4.0.18 (broken)
vitest 4.0.4 (working)
```

## Used Package Manager

bun

## Expected behavior

Tests should run without OOM errors regardless of the number of tests being run.

## Actual behavior

After running ~20+ tests, the process runs out of memory and crashes with:

```
FATAL ERROR: Reached heap limit Allocation failed - JavaScript heap out of memory
```

## Additional context

- This only occurs when running multiple tests in the same session
- Individual tests pass fine
- Memory accumulates across tests, suggesting workers/processes aren't being cleaned up properly
- Adding `--max-old-space-size=8192` or `--no-file-parallelism` doesn't help
- The issue appeared after upgrading from 4.0.4 to 4.0.18

## Validations

- [x] The provided reproduction is minimal and self-contained

title: `hideSkippedTests` removes `it.todo` tests from reports, does not affect test summary
body: ### Describe the bug Currently, our codebase uses both `it.todo` (to signify unimplemented behaviors still needing tests) as well as `it.skipIf`/`it.runIf` to skip certain test cases inside certain entries of `describe.each` table-driven tests. This results in numerous extra test cases that will literally never run under any circumstances and clog up summaries. I was looking into using `hideSkippedTests` to remove all skipped entries from test reports, but realized that it would also remove mention of `it.todo`s as well. (Given the test summary distinguishes between `todo` and `skip`, I'd assume the two would be treated differently here, or at least have the option to do so.) Moreover, the skipped test count inside the test summary remained the same with the option enabled and disabled, meaning it doesn't _truly_ hide all skipped tests as it claims to be the case. #### Notes This can be circumvented by wrapping test cases inside `if` blocks to avoid them being collected altogether, though significantly less ergonomic. This occurs with every single reporter I checked that has a summary, so it's probably not a reporter issue. ### Reproduction https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitest-dev-vitest-hhsxu2z2?file=vite.config.ts `hideSkippedTests` on: `hideSkippedTests` off: ### System Info From Stackblitz: ```shell System: OS: Linux 5.0 undefined CPU: (8) x64 Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-9880H CPU @ 2.30GHz Memory: 0 Bytes / 0 Bytes Shell: 1.0 - /bin/jsh Binaries: Node: 20.19.1 - /usr/local/bin/node Yarn: 1.22.19 - /usr/local/bin/yarn npm: 10.8.2 - /usr/local/bin/npm pnpm: 8.15.6 - /usr/local/bin/pnpm npmPackages: @vitest/ui: latest => 4.0.18 vite: latest => 7.3.1 vitest: latest => 4.0.18 ``` ### Used Package Manager `pnpm` (also happens with `npm` on stackblitz) ### Validations - [x] Follow our [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) - [x] Read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Read the [docs](https://vitest.dev/guide/). - [x] Check that there isn't [already an issue](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues) that reports the same bug to avoid creating a duplicate. - [x] Check that this is a concrete bug. author: developer239
maintainer_reply:
Whole concept of built-in `poolOptions` was removed in
- https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/8705

We were planning that change over a year - pushing it later and later due to the complexity. I've written some of this reasoning in the PR:

> Vitest uses [`tinypool`](https://github.com/tinylibs/tinypool) for orchestrating how test files are run. Originally Tinypool was a fork of [`piscina`](https://github.com/piscinajs/piscina) which implemented `node:worker_threads` pooling only. Codebase of Piscina is very complex. It has features Vitest users do not need or cannot even use. When ever we add new features to Tinypool, we need to make sure we don't break those unused features that some other dependent package might be using.
> 
> Tinypool has some flaws that are making it hard to use in Vitest. When user is running Vitest workspaces with multiple pools, we easily end up in a situation where we allocate too many resources at the same time. For example in a 4 core CPU we may end up spinning 4 threads AND 4 processes at the same time. This is twice the amount of resources we intended to use. Tinypool does not support splitting resourceses across `runtime`. Also mixing `isolate: false` with `isolate: true` is very complex from Vitest's point of view - and not supported properly at the moment.
> 
> Originally Tinypool did not support `node:child_process` runtime. That was added for Vitest in https://github.com/tinylibs/tinypool/pull/65. While this feature works fine, there's still some overhead that the original `node:worker_threads` runtime required. I think there's room for some optimization and performance gains. Note that adding this feature to Piscina's codebase was unnecessarily difficult.
> 
> For the past 1-2 years, whenever we've seen Tinypool related weird errors in Vitest I've thought about rewriting Tinypool completely. However Tinypool is nowadays used by large packages like `facebook/docusaurus`, `jest-light-runner` and `@rstest/core`. Rewriting Tinypool just for Vitest's needs might break other's use cases. It would also be better if we could make changes to Vitest's pool implementation quickly, without any major releases.
> 
> We should replace Tinypool usage in Vitest with a custom internal pool implementation that lives in Vitest monorepo.

Any suggestions how we could do better? This was introduced as breaking change so I'm a bit surprised of your tone. 🤷

title: Provide an explicit way to pass through context to test sub functions
body:
### Clear and concise description of the problem

I'm creating some wrappers around tests (mostly using `test.extend()` and want to do something like this:

```javascript
myTest('...', (context) => {
  for (const subFn of testSubFns) {
    testSubFn(context);
  }
});
```

This isn't permitted, the first argument has to destructure, but I don't necessarily know which things each test sub function will need. I'm sure there's a good reason for this, but it feels very restrictive.

### Suggested solution

Having tried a few workarounds (like rest/spreads), I guessed that Vitest must be parsing the function source code to see which params it's using. I don't know the rationale for this and looking at the source didn't offer any explanation. If it has to be this way, maybe there are one or two options that could be implemented:

* Allow an array of test functions as the second argument of `test()`, e.g. `test('...', [fn1, fn2, ...fns]);`
* Export a helper function that collects the dependencies of test functions, e.g. `test('...', chainTestFunctions([fn1, fn2, ...fns]))`

### Alternative

Right now it seems like my only option would be to reimplement Vitest's dependency detection, run it on my functions and change the `toString()` output of my function to represent the concatenated list of dependencies across all of them. That doesn't sound much like fun to me!

### Additional context

My main reason for doing this is I have a library for declarative testing of Svelte components. The component looks like this:

```svelte
<Test it="opens the menu when the button is clicked">
  <Check fn={...} /> <!-- fn may need access to context -->
  <Check fn={...} /> <!-- fn may need access to context -->
</Test>
```

The reason for allowing multiple `<Check>`  functions is that I am exploring the idea of providing off-the-shelf actions and assertions to simplify test writing.

### Validations

- [x] Read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Read the [docs](https://vitest.dev/guide/).

maintainer_reply:
> I guessed that Vitest must be parsing the function source code to see which params it's using. I don't know the rationale for this and looking at the source didn't offer any explanation.

This is because fixture happens lazily depending on detecting the destructured argument `test("...", { myData } => ...)`. If such laziness is not required, there is `{ auto: true }` https://vitest.dev/guide/test-context.html#automatic-fixture and I think technically it can work by `test("...", context => context.myData)`, but I suppose there might be still a validation error for this case. If that's the case, it might make sense to relax that on Vitest side. Would that suffice for your use case?

Create a Chrome extension project with a content script ```typescript console.log('[CRXJS] Hello world from content script!') function changeAppContent() { const appElement = document.getElementById('app') if (appElement) { appElement.innerHTML = 'crxjs' } } changeAppContent() ``` 2. Original Content

author: joeyslater
maintainer_reply:
This looks like a mix of bug and new feature. Probably the current intent of `sequence` config is actually root-only config, but that doesn't surface in the project type due to a typo here: https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/a60ded0fb1a15a5bc2eb6c26681d9e934d3e17eb/packages/vitest/src/node/types/config.ts#L1296-L1305

That said, limiting `sequence` to root doesn't seem like a hard limitation, and we can technically relax it to support at least `concurrent`, `hooks`, `setupFiles` (and the test-level `shuffle`) per project. That should be possible by tweaking how the serialized config is derived here: https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/a60ded0fb1a15a5bc2eb6c26681d9e934d3e17eb/packages/vitest/src/node/config/serializeConfig.ts#L89-L95

And here comes accompanying AI review:

<details><summary>🤖</summary>

## Root cause

When Vitest builds the per-worker config, the entire `sequence` block is read from the **root** config, so anything set on an individual project is silently dropped:

https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/a60ded0fb1a15a5bc2eb6c26681d9e934d3e17eb/packages/vitest/src/node/config/serializeConfig.ts#L89-L95

```ts
sequence: {
  shuffle: globalConfig.sequence.shuffle,
  concurrent: globalConfig.sequence.concurrent,
  seed: globalConfig.sequence.seed,
  hooks: globalConfig.sequence.hooks,
  setupFiles: globalConfig.sequence.setupFiles,
},
```

The runtime only ever sees this serialized config (e.g. `runner.config.sequence.concurrent` in the test runner), so the project-level value never reaches the code that consumes it.

## What the behavior should be

Rather than patching just `concurrent` — which would leave `sequence` with a confusing surface where some subkeys respect project config and others silently don't — I think this should be decided for the whole block. Sorting each field by where it's actually consumed:

| field | consumed | proposed scope |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| `concurrent` | runtime only | **per-project** |
| `hooks` | runtime only | **per-project** |
| `setupFiles` | runtime only | **per-project** |
| `shuffle` (tests) | runtime only after resolution* | **per-project** |
| `groupOrder` | node, per spec | **per-project** (already is) |
| `seed` | node (file order) + runtime (test shuffle) | **global** |
| `sequencer` / `shuffle.files` | node, cross-project file ordering | **global** |

\* `sequence.shuffle` (`boolean | { files, tests }`) is split during config resolution: the `files` part becomes `sequence.sequencer` (cross-project file ordering, inherently global), and the resolved `shuffle` boolean is just the `tests` dimension — purely runtime. So the serialized `shuffle` is unambiguously per-project.

Encouragingly, this split is **already the documented type intent**. The project config type tries to strip exactly `sequencer` and `seed`:

https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/a60ded0fb1a15a5bc2eb6c26681d9e934d3e17eb/packages/vitest/src/node/types/config.ts#L1296-L1305

```ts
export type ProjectConfig = Omit<
  InlineConfig,
  NonProjectOptions
  | 'sequencer'   // bug: InlineConfig has no `sequencer` key (it's `sequence`)
  | 'deps'
> & {
  mode?: string
  sequencer?: Omit<SequenceOptions, 'sequencer' | 'seed'>   // bug: should be `sequence`
  deps?: Omit<DepsOptions, 'moduleDirectories'>
}
```

Because of the `sequencer`/`sequence` typo, the `Omit` is a no-op and the full `sequence` (including `seed`/`sequencer`) is still type-accepted on projects, plus a phantom top-level `sequencer` option leaks in. So the *intent* — "`sequencer` and `seed` are root-only; the rest of `sequence` is per-project" — matches the proposed behavior; the runtime just never implemented it and the type that meant to express it is broken.

## Proposed changes

1. **Behavior**: serialize `concurrent`, `hooks`, `setupFiles`, and `shuffle` from the project config (`config.sequence.*`) instead of `globalConfig.sequence.*`. Keep `seed` and `sequencer` global.
2. **Types**: fix the project-config typo so `seed`/`sequencer` are genuinely project-hidden:
   ```ts
   export type ProjectConfig = Omit<
     InlineConfig,
     NonProjectOptions | 'sequence' | 'deps'
   > & {
     mode?: string
     sequence?: Omit<SequenceOptions, 'sequencer' | 'seed'>
     deps?: Omit<DepsOptions, 'moduleDirectories'>
   }
   ```
   Optionally also narrow project `shuffle` to drop `files` (`boolean | { tests?: boolean }`), since `shuffle.files` only affects cross-project file ordering and is a no-op per project.
3. **Docs**: document that within a project, `sequence` controls per-project test behavior, while `sequence.sequencer`, `sequence.seed`, and `sequence.shuffle.files` are honored only from the root config (cross-project file ordering / shared reproducibility seed). Note that `sequence.shuffle: true` on a project means "shuffle this project's tests," not files.
4. **Minor**: the "Running tests with seed …" log only fires when the *root* shuffles; once per-project `shuffle` lands, it should also print when any project shuffles.

## Follow-up (separate)

Per-project `sequence.seed` override. This needs the project seed to *inherit* the resolved root seed (rather than generate its own `Date.now()`) plus per-project seed reporting, so it's better as its own change. Until then, `seed` stays global and documented as such.

## Repro confirmation

Confirmed on vitest 4.1.9 with a minimal project setup (root `sequence.concurrent: false`, project `suite-1` `sequence.concurrent: true`, two ~150ms tests): with the setting on the **project** the tests run sequentially (~306ms); moving the same setting to the **root** makes them run concurrently (~152ms). Only the root value reaches the runtime.

Happy to open a PR for items 1–4 (per-project fields + type fix + docs) and leave per-project `seed` as a separate issue, if this split sounds right.

</details>

2) Upon building the application we had a blank screen with a `tslib` error in the console. 

This seems to be because we are on `"vite": "^5.4.8"` which is not supported but annoyingly I only spotted this after migrating fully, and then facing issues after building - and the only place I could find this information is on the GitHub repo's `[README.md](https://github.com/AidanDaniel97/vitest/blob/main/README.md)` and _[not in the migration guide](https://vitest.dev/guide/migration.html)_


I'm happy to submit a PR for this, I think it's a necesarry addition for some clarity on what has changed. It may also be worth doing the same for the Vitest 3 migration guide.

### Your Suggestion for Changes

Ideally if we can add warning banner at the top of the migration guide 

```
::: warning Prerequisites
Vitest 4.0 requires **Vite >= 6.0.0** and **Node >= 20.0.0**. 
:::
```

or more detailed 

```
::: warning Prerequisites
Vitest 4.0 requires **Vite >= 6.0.0** and **Node >= 20.0.0**. Before proceeding
with any other migration steps, ensure your environment meets these requirements.
Running Vitest 4.0 on older versions of Vite or Node is not supported and will
likely result in unexpected errors.
:::
```

https://vitest.dev/guide/migration.html

title: merge-reports produces empty output (tests="0") for reporters relying on onFinished (e.g., JUnit)
body:
### Describe the bug

When using `--merge-reports` with `--reporter=junit`, the resulting XML file contains 0 tests, even if the blobs contain valid test results. 

While coverage reporters (like `cobertura`) work correctly because they are handled separately via `coverageProvider`, standard reporters like JUnit rely on the `onFinished` hook receiving a populated list of files. Currently, `mergeReports` does not correctly populate the internal state or pass the merged files to the `_testRun.end` cycle, causing reporters to see an empty test suite.

### Reproduction

1. Generate blob reports on shards:
   `vitest run --shard=1/2 --reporter=blob --outputFile=.vitest-reports/1.blob`
2. Merge reports with JUnit reporter:
   `vitest --merge-reports=.vitest-reports --reporter=junit --outputFile=junit.xml`

**Expected Behavior:**
`junit.xml` should contain aggregated test results from all blobs.

**Actual Behavior:**
`junit.xml` is generated but indicates 0 tests:
```xml
<testsuites name="vitest tests" tests="0" failures="0" errors="0" time="0">
</testsuites>
```

In `Vitest.prototype.mergeReports` (packages/vitest/src/node/core.ts), the `_testRun.end()` method is called to finalize the run. However, since no actual tests were executed in this process, the `state` passed to reporters is empty (or the files are filtered out).

I have confirmed locally that:
1. `this.state.collectFiles(files)` needs to be called to populate the global state.
2. Reporters need to be manually triggered with the merged `files` array, or `_testRun.end` needs to be aware of these files.



### System Info

```shell
Vitest version: 3.2.4
```

npm

title: Vitest config `benchmark.reporters` has incorrect type; forbids passing arbitrary file paths
body:
### Describe the bug

Currently, `benchmark.reporters` has the type `Arrayable<"default" | "verbose" | Reporter>`, meaning the only strings it can accept without type errors are those of the built-in bench reporters. 

This goes directly against its documentation ("... one or more built-in report names, reporter instances, and/or **paths to custom reporters**"[^1]), as well as Vitest's runtime behavior of using the reporter as normal.

https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/4d7938a567d4afb16ed793fe1ac34b7b9880f06e/packages/vitest/src/node/types/benchmark.ts#L27-L33

A solution would be adding `string & {}` to the type signature; this would allow arbitrary strings while preserving IDE autocomplete for the default types.

[^1]: Bolded for emphasis

title: `getCurrentInstance()` returns `null` in browser mode when using custom `resolve.conditions` in a monorepo
body:
### Describe the bug

**AI notice**: AI has been used to extrapolate from a large monorepo that can't be shared. The workaround suggested works and solves the issue. I am uncertain about further details as the AI has done the digging to find a workaround.

## Related issues

- https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/5301 - Also concerns `resolve.conditions` but I am not sure it is the same issue or not. 

--- 
When using `vitest-browser-vue`'s `render()` in browser mode, `getCurrentInstance()` returns `null` inside a component's `render()` function. This also breaks `withDirectives()`:

```
[Vue warn]: withDirectives can only be used inside render functions.
```

## Trigger conditions

npm workspaces + custom `resolve.conditions` (e.g. `['source']`), a common monorepo pattern for resolving TypeScript sources directly.

## Root cause

**NOTE:** This is an AI conclussion:

> The `test-utils-rewrite` esbuild plugin in `@vitest/browser` resolves `@vue/test-utils` to its **CJS entry**, which `require('vue')`s a separate CJS Vue runtime. With workspaces + custom conditions, esbuild fails to deduplicate this CJS copy against the ESM Vue used by test code, resulting in two independent Vue instances with separate `currentInstance` state.

## Expected

`@vue/test-utils` should be resolved to its ESM bundler entry (`vue-test-utils.esm-bundler.mjs`) so it shares the same Vue runtime as test code.

## Reproduce

```bash
npm install
npm test --ws
```



### Reproduction

A reproduction repo can be found here:

https://github.com/filimon-danopoulos-stratsys/vite-custom-condition-repro

**NOTE** AI has been used to to simplify the reproduction. The README contains the AI summary of the issue.

title: docs: Add JSDocs to reporter functions and methods for downstream use
body: ### Describe the bug As it stands, virtually **NONE** of the methods and properties inside `BaseReporter` or `DefaultReporter` have any JSDoc comments at all. Aside from making the experience inside modern IDEs _not good_, this notably obfuscates what different methods do for anyone attempting to write a custom reporter themselves. Knowing the difference between `getTestName` and `getFullName` (or one of the other 25+ methods in that class) can be painfully vague at times given the spa. Yes, `vitest.dev` does document some methods inside the API section, but... 1. It only mentions the ~16 or so methods related to test cycle lifespan, meaning methods like `onUserConsoleLog` or `printTestSummary` have no information aside from the function signature itself. 2. People tend to prefer staying in an IDE over reading documentation[^1]. Even for those who don't hate reading the docs, the existence of documentation pages is not always made clear. Doc comments are just as (if not even more important) for external users as internal ones. Ideally, I'd like to see the external API documented inside my IDE alongside the website docs. Perhaps one could provide a short overview and the other a more in-depth explanation? (Either way, something would be better than nothing, especially when these methods are exported for external use.) ### Reproduction 1. Attempt to make a new reporter that has custom logging 2. Get confused because of the lack of docs 3. Waste 5 hours running in circles 4. Realize that `vitest.dev` has docs for some methods 5. Realize that the methods you are confused about are not on that page 6. title: Allow to configure fixture scope test/worker
body:
### Clear and concise description of the problem

In the #4165 a decision was made to make all fixtures test-scoped, so that they are recreated again for each test. However there are cases where performance-wise it will be better to have a fixture initialized again and then reused across tests in same spec. This also make it more aligned with how playwright handles this.

### Suggested solution

Let to pass additional argument when declaring the fixture, like
```
test.extend({
  usualFixture: () => {...} // test scope by default
  sharedFixture: [() => {}, { scope: 'worker'}] // shared across all tests in the worker
})
```

### Alternative

I see no viable alternative with current fixtures api

### Additional context

https://playwright.dev/docs/test-fixtures#worker-scoped-fixtures

title: MSW handler disabled just before call
body:
### Describe the bug

I am using Vitest browser mode with Vue, with MSW to mock api calls. 

I'm using a simple setup file, as suggested by [MSW](https://mswjs.io/docs/recipes/vitest-browser-mode/#example) : 
```ts
import { setupWorker } from 'msw/browser'
import type { SetupWorker } from 'msw/browser'
import { it as testBase } from 'vitest'

export const worker = setupWorker()

export const it = testBase.extend<{ worker: SetupWorker }>({
  worker: [
    // eslint-disable-next-line no-empty-pattern
    async ({}, use) => {
      // Start the worker before the test.
      await worker.start({ quiet: false, onUnhandledRequest: 'warn' })

      // Expose the worker object on the test's context.
      await use(worker)

      // Remove any request handlers added in individual test cases.
      // This prevents them from affecting unrelated tests.
      worker.resetHandlers()

      // Stop the worker after the test.
      worker.stop()
    },
    {
      auto: true,
    },
  ],
})
```

And in my test:
```ts
import { describe } from 'vitest'
import { it } from '@/msw'
import { render } from 'vitest-browser-vue'
import { http, HttpResponse } from 'msw'
import HelloWorld from '../HelloWorld.vue'

describe('HelloWorld', () => {
  it('renders properly', ({ worker }) => {
    worker.use(
      http.get('https://httpbin.org/status/401', () => {
        return new HttpResponse(null, { status: 401 })
      }),
    )

    render(HelloWorld, {props: {msg: 'Hello Vitest'}})
  })
})
```

title: `@vitest/coverage-v8` v4 produces `NaN` in BRDA entries of lcov reports, breaking Codecov integration
body:
### Describe the bug After upgrading from Vitest v3 to v4.0.18 in a Vue 3 component library monorepo, the lcov coverage reporter generates invalid `BRDA` (branch data) entries containing `NaN` instead of integer hit counts. `NaN` is not a valid value per the [lcov specification](https://ltp.sourceforge.net/coverage/lcov/geninfo.1.php), which expects a non-negative integer or `-`. This produces corrupt lcov reports that may cause issues with coverage tools relying on strict lcov parsing. The migration PR is public and can be reviewed here: https://github.com/LouisMazel/maz-ui/pull/1473 ### Affected files The issue only affects **Vue Single File Components** (`.vue` files). Plain `.ts`/`.js` files produce valid lcov output. The `NaN` always appears in the **4th field** (execution count) of `BRDA` entries, and always on **branch index `1`** (the "else" / falsy path of a conditional). In our project ([maz-ui](https://github.com/LouisMazel/maz-ui), 50+ Vue components), **77 `NaN` entries** are produced across **36 `.vue` files**. Here is the full list of affected components:
36 affected files (click to expand) - `src/components/MazAlert.vue` - `src/components/MazAnimatedText.vue` - `src/components/MazAvatar.vue` - `src/components/MazBackdrop.vue` - `src/components/MazBottomSheet.vue` - `src/components/MazBtn.vue` - `src/components/MazCard.vue` - `src/components/MazCarousel.vue` - `src/components/MazCheckbox.vue` - `src/components/MazChecklist.vue` - `src/components/MazCircularProgressBar.vue` - `src/components/MazContainer.vue` - `src/components/MazDatePicker/MazPickerCalendar.vue` - `src/components/MazDatePicker/MazPickerHeader.vue` - `src/components/MazDialog.vue` - `src/components/MazDialogConfirm.vue` - `src/components/MazDrawer.vue` - `src/components/MazDropdown.vue` - `src/components/MazDropzone.vue` - `src/components/MazGallery.vue` - `src/components/MazInput.vue` - `src/components/MazInputNumber.vue` - `src/components/MazInputPhoneNumber.vue` - `src/components/MazPagination.vue` - `src/components/MazPopover.vue` - `src/components/MazPullToRefresh.vue` - `src/components/MazRadioButtons.vue` - `src/components/MazReadMore.vue` - `src/components/MazSelect.vue` - `src/components/MazSelectCountry.vue` - `src/components/MazStepper.vue` - `src/components/MazSwitch.vue` - `src/components/MazTable.vue` - `src/components/MazTabsBar.vue` - `src/components/MazTextarea.vue` - `src/plugins/toast/MazToast.vue`
### Reproduction ### Minimal `vitest.config.ts` ```ts import Vue from '@vitejs/plugin-vue' import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config' export default defineConfig({ plugins: [Vue()], test: { environment: 'jsdom', coverage: { provider: 'v8', reporter: ['lcov'], include: ['src/**/*.vue'], }, }, }) ``` ### Minimal Vue component (`src/Example.vue`) ```vue ``` ### Minimal test ```ts import { mount } from '@vue/test-utils' import Example from '../src/Example.vue' test('renders', () => { mount(Example, { props: { title: 'Hello' } }) }) ``` ### Run ```bash vitest run --coverage ``` ### Inspect `coverage/lcov.info` You will find entries like: ``` BRDA:9,0,1,NaN ``` The 4th field should be a non-negative integer (`0`, `1`, `42`, ...) or `-` per the [lcov specification](https://ltp.sourceforge.net/coverage/lcov/geninfo.1.php), never `NaN`. ## Actual behavior The generated `lcov.info` contains invalid branch data. Example from `MazContainer.vue` (line 97 is a `
` in the template): ``` BRDA:97,1,0,1 BRDA:97,1,1,NaN ← invalid: should be 0 or a positive integer BRDA:97,2,0,3 BRDA:97,2,1,3 ``` The pattern is consistent across all 77 occurrences: - **Always branch index `1`** (3rd field) — the else/falsy path of the conditional - **Always on lines corresponding to Vue template conditionals** (`v-if`, ternary expressions in templates) - **Only in `.vue` files** — `.ts` and `.js` files in the same project produce perfectly valid lcov output - **The `clover` reporter is NOT affected** — only the `lcov` reporter produces `NaN` ### Impact on external tools The `NaN` values produce invalid lcov output that may cause issues with coverage tools expecting strict lcov compliance (e.g., Codecov, SonarQube, Coveralls). In our case, we initially observed Codecov failing to process the report, though we do not exclude a separate Codecov-side issue as a contributing factor. ## Expected behavior All `BRDA` entries should contain valid integer execution counts. A branch that was never taken should be `0`, not `NaN`. ## Versions | Package | Version | | --------------------- | ------------------------------------ | | `vitest` | 4.0.18 | | `@vitest/coverage-v8` | 4.0.18 | | `ast-v8-to-istanbul` | 0.3.11 | | `@vitejs/plugin-vue` | 6.0.4 | | `vue` | 3.5+ | | Node.js | 22 | | OS | Ubuntu 24.04 (CI) / macOS 15 (local) | ## Additional context - **Regression from Vitest v3**: the same project with the same test suite produces valid lcov output on Vitest v3. The migration PR (linked above) only bumps Vitest dependencies and adapts configs to v4 breaking changes. - **Root cause hypothesis**: the bug is likely in `ast-v8-to-istanbul` (the AST-based V8 remapping that replaced `v8-to-istanbul` in Vitest v4). When Vue SFC template conditionals are compiled to JavaScript, they produce branches that the V8 engine reports coverage for. The AST remapping appears to produce `NaN` when computing hit counts for certain branch paths in the remapped source. - **`@vitest/coverage-istanbul` is NOT affected**: switching from `provider: 'v8'` to `provider: 'istanbul'` on the exact same codebase and test suite produces **0 `NaN`** across 4269 BRDA entries. This confirms the bug is specifically in the V8 provider's AST remapping layer (`ast-v8-to-istanbul`), not in the lcov reporter itself. | Provider | NaN count | Total BRDA entries | |------------|-----------|--------------------| | `v8` | 77 | ~850 | | `istanbul` | **0** | 4269 | - **Workaround 1**: use `provider: 'istanbul'` instead of `provider: 'v8'` — this fully avoids the bug. - **Workaround 2**: patching `NaN` to `0` in lcov files before uploading to Codecov (`sed -i 's/,NaN$/,0/g' coverage/lcov.info`) restores Codecov processing, but this is not a real fix. ### System Info ```shell System: OS: macOS 26.3 CPU: (10) arm64 Apple M1 Pro Memory: 101.30 MB / 16.00 GB Shell: 5.9 - /bin/zsh Binaries: Node: 22.15.1 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.15.1/bin/node Yarn: 1.22.19 - ~/.yarn/bin/yarn npm: 10.9.2 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.15.1/bin/npm pnpm: 10.28.1 - ~/.nvm/versions/node/v22.15.1/bin/pnpm bun: 1.3.2 - ~/.bun/bin/bun Browsers: Chrome: 143.0.7499.41 Safari: 26.3 npmPackages: @vitest/coverage-v8: ^4.0.18 => 4.0.18 vite: ^7.3.0 => 7.3.1 vitest: ^4.0.18 => 4.0.18 ``` ### Used Package Manager pnpm ### Validations - [x] Follow our [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) - [x] Read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Read the [docs](https://vitest.dev/guide/). - [x] Check that there isn't [already an issue](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues) that reports the same bug to avoid creating a duplicate. - [x] Check that this is a concrete bug.
