title: docs: clarify allowed characters in config file name pattern
body:
> **Note:** This issue was written with the help of translation tools. I apologize if there are any unnatural expressions.

### Description

In the [Test Projects documentation](https://vitest.dev/guide/projects.html#defining-projects), the config file naming pattern is described as:

> matches `(vite|vitest).*.config.*` pattern

This notation is ambiguous — users may interpret `*` as a shell glob (any character), but the actual implementation uses `\w+` (regex word characters: `[a-zA-Z0-9_]`):

```ts
const CONFIG_REGEXP = /^vite(?:st)?(?:\.\w+)?\.config\./
```

This means names like `vitest.my-project.config.ts` silently fail to be detected, which can be confusing.

### Suggested Change

Make the pattern description more explicit. For example:

- Show the actual regex or clarify that only word characters (`a-z`, `A-Z`, `0-9`, `_`) are allowed
- Add an "invalid" example (e.g. `vitest.my-project.config.ts`) alongside the valid ones

### Additional context

- Source: [`packages/vitest/src/node/projects/resolveProjects.ts#L25`](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/main/packages/vitest/src/node/projects/resolveProjects.ts#L25)
author: Koutaro-Hanabusa
maintainer_reply: It looks reasonable to support hyphen `-` . I don't think limiting to `\w` was intended specifically.

title: Virtual module mocking issue in Vitest 4
body:
### Describe the bug

_This discussion is a follow-up to [this discussion](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/discussions/9734) that I initially opened before this issue.__

In a test file, I have different `describe` blocks where in each of them, I mock a virtual module, e.g. using `vi.doMock()` and mock a function from that virtual module making it return different values.

The behavior seems to be different between Vitest 3 and Vitest 4:

- Vitest 3: everything seems to work as expected, and calling some code that uses that virtual module returns the mocked value.
- Vitest 4: the first mocked value seems to be returned for all tests.

### Reproduction

I've setup a minimal repro available here: https://github.com/HiDeoo/vitest-4-mock-repro

1. Clone the repository
1. Run `pnpm install`
1. Run `pnpm test`

Some tests that are checking that the expected returned mocked value is correct will fail.

A few extra notes:

- Running `pnpm add vitest@3` and `pnpm test` will make the test pass
- I tried swapping the order of `vi.resetModules()` and `vi.doMock()` as [suggested](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/discussions/9734#discussioncomment-15917711) but this didn't change the behavior

### System Info

```shell
System:
```

title: `vi.importActual()` issue with virtual modules in Vitest 4

### Describe the bug

In a test file, I mock a virtual module, e.g. using `vi.mock()` and try to import the original module using either [`vi.importActual()`](https://vitest.dev/api/vi.html#vi-importactual) or the [`importOriginal()`](https://vitest.dev/api/vi.html#vi-mock) helper.

```ts
vi.mock("virtual:test", async (importOriginal) => {
```

title: Add built-in matcher: expect(...).toBeValidUUID() (or similar)
body:
### Clear and concise description of the problem

As a developer using Vitest t would be useful if Vitest shipped with a built-in matcher to assert that a value is a valid UUID, 
In many tests, after creating an entity (DB insert, API call, domain factory, etc.), we don’t care about the exact UUID value, only that it is a valid UUID.

Today, users have to:

- write regex assertions repeatedly (error-prone and noisy), or
- add a custom matcher via expect.extend, which works but is boilerplate that many projects will duplicate.
Having a built-in matcher would improve readability and encourage consistent assertions across projects.

### Suggested solution

Add a built-in matcher that validates UUID strings, ideally supporting common versions:

- expect(value).toBeValidUUID()
  - Fails if value is not a string (or optionally accepts string | undefined?).
  - Validates canonical UUID format (xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx).
  - Optionally validates UUID version and variant properly.

### Alternative

- Keep it as user-land custom matcher via expect.extend (current approach)
- Encourage a recipe in docs (copy/paste matcher) instead of bundling it
- Use regex inline:
  - expect(id).toMatch(/[0-9a-fA-F-]{36}/)
  - (but this is usually too permissive and harms readability)

### Additional context

I already use a custom matcher in my project and it works well; I’m proposing adding it to Vitest by default since UUID checks are a common need.

Example custom matcher I currently use:
```Typescript
import { expect } from 'vitest'

const UUID_REGEX =
  /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[1-5][0-9a-f]{3}-[89ab][0-9a-f]{3}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i

expect.extend({
  toBeValidUUID(received: unknown) {
    const pass = typeof received === 'string' && UUID_REGEX.test(received)
    return {
      pass,
      message: () =>
        pass
          ? `expected ${received} not to be a valid UUID`
          : `expected ${received} to be a valid UUID`,
    }
  },
})
```

### Validations

- [x] Follow our [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)
- [x] Read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md).
- [x] Read the [docs](https://vitest.dev/guide/).
- [x] Check that there isn't already an issue that requests the same feature to avoid creating a duplicate.
author: ET-TOUNANI
maintainer_reply: I think this is a better fit as outside of core. I'd imagine similar needs arise from other string format regex needs e.g. email, timestamp, etc. For reference, zod has quite a bit https://zod.dev/api#string-formats (I'd imagine it's not easy for them to decide what to include and not) and you could still integrate them with `schemaMatching` https://main.vitest.dev/api/expect.html#expect-schemamatching e.g. `expect(value).schemaMatching(z.uuid())`.

title: Feature Request: Extensible VCS Adapter System for Changed Test Detection
body:
### Clear and concise description of the problem

**Summary:**  
Add a plugin/extension point system to Vitest to support custom VCS (Version Control System) commands for detecting changed files. This is essential for efficiently running tests in large monorepos that use VCS systems other than Git (e.g., Mercurial, SVN) or require custom change-detection logic.

**Problem:**  
Currently, Vitest's `--changed` flag and related functionality rely on Git to determine which files have been modified. This creates limitations for developers in enterprise environments where:
-  Legacy codebases use Mercurial (hg), Subversion (svn), or other VCS systems
-  Custom version control systems or proprietary solutions are in use
-  The default Git-based change detection doesn't work with alternative VCS workflows
-  Large monorepos require specialized change detection logic for optimal performance

### Suggested solution

**Implementation Details:**  
1. **Configuration Option:** Add a `vcsCommand` field in Vitest configuration:
```typescript
export default defineConfig({
  vcsCommand: 'hg status --modified --added --no-status --print0 | xargs -0'
})
```

2. **Standard Interface**: The custom command should output changed file paths (relative to project root), one per line, to stdout. 
3. **Fallback Behavior**: Maintain current Git-based detection as default when no custom command is specified.
4. **Environment Variables**: Support dynamic command configuration through environment variables for CI/CD flexibility.

**Example Usage:**

**For Mercurial users:**
```
export default defineConfig({
  vcsCommand: 'hg status --modified --added --no-status'
})
```

### Alternative

title: @vitest/mocker 4.1.0: vite declared as optional peer dependency but imported unconditionally in dist/node.js
body:
### Describe the bug

Starting with `@vitest/mocker` 4.1.0, running vitest with `@vitest/browser-playwright` fails with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` if `vite` is not explicitly installed in the project, even though `vite` is declared as an optional peer dependency.

**Expected:** Tests run (or a graceful error if vite is required)

**Actual:**
```
Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'vite' imported from /path/to/node_modules/@vitest/browser-playwright/node_modules/@vitest/mocker/dist/node.js
```

## Root cause

In `@vitest/mocker/package.json`, vite is declared as optional:

```json
"peerDependencies": {
  "vite": "^6.0.0 || ^7.0.0 || ^8.0.0-0"
},
"peerDependenciesMeta": {
  "vite": {
    "optional": true
  }
}
```

However, `dist/node.js` appears to have an unconditional static import of `vite`, causing Node.js module resolution to fail immediately at load time when vite is not present.

This worked in 4.0.18

## Workaround

Explicitly install `vite` as a devDependency:

```bash
npm install vite --save-dev
```



### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitest-dev-vitest-bjtmmvai?file=package.json&initialPath=__vitest__/

1. Create a project with the following devDependencies:
   ```json
   {
     "devDependencies": {
       "@vitest/browser-playwright": "4.1.0",
       "vitest": "4.1.0"
     }
   }
   ```
2. Run `npm install`
3. Run `vitest`

title: Vitest 4 & Vite 8 - Consistent CommonJS Interop
body:
### Describe the bug

I've upgraded my stack to Vite 8 & have hit the breaking change [Consistent CommonJS Interop](https://vite.dev/guide/migration#consistent-commonjs-interop).
Vite expose a `legacy.inconsistentCjsInterop: true` option to work around this. Let's imagine I don't want to use this option - it's deprecated - so I find that there's an inconsistency between vite & vitest.

My specific case uses `@twemoji/parser` [here](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@twemoji/parser).

When using vite 7 - both vitest & vite behave the same.
When using vite 8 - I'm required to use `legacy.inconsistentCjsInterop: true` to revert to the legacy behavior to keep the same test vs browser behaviour. If I fix the issue without using this option - vitest does not recognize imports the same way as vite.

In my head, vite has changed how he sees certain cjs imports in vite 8. And vitest does not yet follow suit?

### Reproduction

### Vite 7
👇  Well imported ✅ 
`import twemojiRegex from '@twemoji/parser/dist/lib/regex';` 

[In the browser](https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-sykiynnh?file=src%2Fmain.ts&terminal=dev)
[In vitest](https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitest-dev-vitest-siydnoym?file=src%2FisEmoji.ts)

### Vite 8
👇  Not well imported 🔴 
`import twemojiRegex from '@twemoji/parser/dist/lib/regex';` 

👇  Changed to this to be well imported ✅ 
```
import twemojiRegex from '@twemoji/parser/dist/lib/regex';
const twemojiRegexDefault = twemojiRegex.default;
``` 

[In the browser](https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-b4xsy8or?file=src%2Fmain.ts&terminal=dev)

title: vitest/coverage-istanbul crashes with TypeError: template is not a function when used with cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers
body:
### Describe the bug

When using `vitest/coverage-istanbul@4.1.0` with `cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers@0.13.0`, running tests with coverage fails immediately with:

```
TypeError: template is not a function
 ❯ requireVisitor node_modules/@vitest/coverage-istanbul/dist/provider.js:1024:40
 ❯ VitestModuleEvaluator._runInlinedModule node_modules/vitest/dist/module-evaluator.js:206:4
 ❯ ServerModuleRunner.directRequest node_modules/vite/dist/node/module-runner.js:1243:59
The error does not occur in a plain Vitest setup (without the Cloudflare Workers pool).
```

Root cause
The bundled **provider.js** imports **babel/core** via a default ESM import (`import require$$0$3 from '@babel/core'`), generated by rollup/plugin-commonjs during the build. When this import is resolved by Vite's `ServerModuleRunner` (used by `cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers`), it only detects CJS named exports declared via direct exports.X = ... assignments.

`babel/core` declares most of its exports (including `template`, `parseSync`, `traverse`) using `Object.defineProperty(exports, ...)` with lazy getters. These are invisible to Vite's CJS static analysis. Only 7 out of 34 exports are detected — the ones using direct assignment patterns.

The result: template is undefined on the imported object, and provider.js crashes when it tries to call it.

Used Package Manager
npm


### Reproduction

Repo: [temp-vitest-istanbul-repro](https://github.com/mictian/temp-vitest-istanbul-repro)


```bash
git clone https://github.com/mictian/temp-vitest-istanbul-repro
cd vitest-istanbul-repro
npm install
npm test
```

The repro contains:

* vitest.config.ts — uses cloudflareTest plugin + istanbul coverage
* wrangler.jsonc — minimal Cloudflare Workers config
* src/sum.ts + src/sum.test.ts — trivial test file


**Suggested fix**

In packages/coverage-istanbul/rollup.config.js, replace the ESM default import of babel/core with a createRequire call so it loads via Node's native CJS loader (which correctly handles Object.defineProperty exports).

I verified this locally by patching dist/provider.js:

```diff
- import require$$0$3 from '@babel/core';
+ import { createRequire as __createRequire } from 'node:module';
+ const __require = __createRequire(import.meta.url);
+ const require$$0$3 = __require('@babel/core');
```
After patching, the coverage provider loads successfully with all 34 babel/core exports present.

A possible implementation in the rollup config would be a renderChunk plugin that rewrites the babel/core import to use createRequire.

### System Info

```shell
System Info
- vitest: 4.1.0
- @vitest/coverage-istanbul: 4.1.0
- @cloudflare/vitest-pool-workers: 0.13.0
- Node: v22.x
- OS: macOS
```

npm

title: Playwright: logs causes timeouts across parallel tests and across browsers
body:
### Describe the bug While debugging an issue in a React [lib](https://github.com/Comcast/react-data-grid), React started spamming the console with logs like this one:
Example log ``` Encountered two children with the same key, `0`. Keys should be unique so that components maintain their identity across updates. Non-unique keys may cause children to be duplicated and/or omitted — the behavior is unsupported and could change in a future version. ❯ console.error test/failOnConsole.ts:13:12 ❯ require_react_dom_client_development That in itself is not an issue with Vitest whatsoever. What is an issue on the other hand, is that the one test that triggered the logs made unrelated tests running in parallel time out, for example: ``` TimeoutError: locator.click: Timeout 2000ms exceeded. Call log: - waiting for locator('[data-vitest="true"]').contentFrame().getByTestId('__vitest_0__') - locator resolved to ↵ ↵↵ - attempting click action - waiting for element to be visible, enabled and stable ❯ test/setupBrowser.ts:87:18 85| // 1. reset cursor position to avoid hover issues 86| // 2. force focus to be on the page 87| await userEvent.click(document.body, { position: { x: 0, y: 0 } }); | ^ 88| }); 89| ``` If I `.skip` the test causing the logs, then the other tests pass as expected. It seems like the test runner/nodejs process/orchestrator can become too busy to execute browser interactions in a timely manner. I wonder if tasks other than console logs can overwork the nodejs process. Should the nodejs process [`yield`](https://nodejs.org/api/timers.html#timerspromisesschedulerwaitdelay-options) to higher-priority tasks? Should there be 1 nodejs worker per test suite? Either way, interaction latency is definitely affected by low-priority tasks. ### Reproduction https://github.com/nstepien/vitest-bug 1. `npm ci` 2. `npx playwright install` 3. Run tests - `npm test` - all browsers spamming the console while running all the tests - `npm run test:across` - one browser spamming the console, other browsers run the tests 4. Comment out the `console.log();` line in `test/spam.test.ts` and run the tests again: - Actions do not timeout anymore With `npm run test:across`: - `chromium` runs a test that spams console logs - `firefox` and `webkit` run interaction tests - the chromium logs cause firefox and webkit tests to time out! Example logs: ### System Info ```shell System: OS: Windows 11 10.0.26200 CPU: (32) x64 AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D 16-Core Processor Memory: 34.28 GB / 63.58 GB Binaries: Node: 25.8.1 - C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.EXE npm: 11.11.1 - C:\Program Files\nodejs\npm.CMD pnpm: 10.30.3 - C:\Users\Stepi\AppData\Roaming\npm\pnpm.CMD Browsers: Chrome: 146.0.7680.154 Edge: Chromium (146.0.3856.59) Firefox: 148.0.2 - C:\Program Files\Mozilla Firefox\firefox.exe npmPackages: @vitest/browser-playwright: ^4.1.0 => 4.1.0 playwright: ^1.58.2 => 1.58.2 vitest: ^4.1.0 => 4.1.0 ``` ### Used Package Manager npm ### Validations - [x] Follow our [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) - [x] Read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Read the [docs](https://vitest.dev/guide/). - [x] Check that there isn't [already an issue](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues) that reports the same bug to avoid creating a duplicate. - [x] Check that this is a concrete bug. For Q&A open a [GitHub Discussion](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/discussions) or join our [Discord Chat Server](https://chat.vitest.dev). - [x] The provided reproduction is a [minimal reproducible example](https://stackoverflow.com/help/minimal-reproducible-example) of the bug.
author: nstepien
maintainer_reply:
Browser mode doesn't have similar `console` buffer as Node side has (related to [`--disableConsoleIntercept`](https://vitest.dev/config/disableconsoleintercept.html#disableconsoleintercept)). But even if that was implemented, main thread could still be blocked by work all other test threads/processes/browsers cause. As all browser mode user events are in the end executed on the server side this will cause timing issues.

It would help if browser pool wrapped each browser instance around process/thread. But even then that would be shared by all parallel tests that the browser instance is running.

title: vitest should declare @vitest/coverage-v8 and @vitest/coverage-istanbul as optional peer dependencies
body:
`vitest@4.1.1` dynamically imports `@vitest/coverage-v8` when `coverage.provider` is set to `"v8"`:

```
Error: Cannot find package '@vitest/coverage-v8' imported from .../node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/coverage.CTzCuANN.js
```

This works in hoisted `node_modules` layouts (npm, yarn) because `@vitest/coverage-v8` is hoisted from the consuming project. In pnpm's strict isolation (default in pnpm 10), vitest can only resolve packages declared in its own dependency tree — and since `@vitest/coverage-v8` isn't listed as a peer, pnpm doesn't link it.

`vitest` already declares optional peers for `@vitest/browser-*` and `@vitest/ui`. Adding coverage providers would be consistent with that pattern.

**Temp workaround:**
```yaml
# pnpm-workspace.yaml
packageExtensions:
  "vitest@4":
    peerDependencies:
      "@vitest/coverage-v8": "*"
    peerDependenciesMeta:
      "@vitest/coverage-v8":
        optional: true
```

**Suggested proper fix:** 

Add `@vitest/coverage-v8` and `@vitest/coverage-istanbul` as optional peer dependencies in `vitest`'s `package.json`, matching the existing pattern for `@vitest/browser-*` and `@vitest/ui`.

**Why is it important?**

The import **failure happens in runtime**, so it can silently break things for people who adopting strict isolation (no hoisting).
author: baraknaveh
maintainer_reply:
Adding `@vitest/*` packages as `peerDependencies` is not correct solution. Coverage providers, reporters, runners, pools etc. can be built by community too. We cannot declare all community provided packages as `peerDependencies`.

Does this happen with `4.1.0` too? In `4.1.1` we introduced https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/9939.

Maybe external package resolving is broken. Minimal reproduction would help.

title: Reporting regression in V4: incorrect per-test duration + perceived serial execution slowdown
body:
### Describe the bug

After upgrading from Vitest v3 to v4, there are two issues:

1. Incorrect test duration reporting
- Tests that clearly run sequentially (~10s each) are reported as taking ~20s each.
- The total suite duration is correct, but per-test timings are inflated.
2. Perceived performance regression
- Our full test suite (~300 tests) increased from ~42s (v3) to ~166s (v4).
- This appears unrelated to the reporting issue, but may be connected to concurrency changes in v4.

### Expected:

- Each test should report its actual execution time (~10s in the example).
- Test runtime should remain roughly consistent with v3 under equivalent config.

### Actual:

- Each test reports the total elapsed time of the suite segment (~20s).
- Suite runtime is significantly slower in v4.

### Reproduction

```tsx
import { describe, it } from 'vitest';

const delay = (ms: number) => new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, ms));

describe.concurrent('Blah', () => {
  it('1', async () => {
    console.log('Started test 1');
    await delay(10000);
    console.log('Finished test 1');
  });

  it('2', async () => {
    console.log('Started test 2');
    await delay(10000);
    console.log('Finished test 2');
  });
});
```

Vitest config:
```tsx
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts'],
    maxConcurrency: 1,
    maxWorkers: 1,
  },
});
```

Observed output:

```
Started test 1
Finished test 1
Started test 2
Finished test 2

✓ 1  ~20s
✓ 2  ~20s
```

Even though each test only waits 10s.

title: maxConcurrency no longer bounds in-flight tests in describe.concurrent, causing per-test resource leaks (regression from v3?)
body:
### Describe the bug

### Summary

In vitest 3, `maxConcurrency` bounded the number of tests that were in flight at any moment - that is, the number of tests whose `beforeEach`/`body`/`afterEach` cycle had started but not yet completed. After #9653, the limiter was moved from runTest-level to leaf-level (individual hook/body function calls). This was done to fix #8367, where sibling `beforeAll` hooks weren't being throttled. But it removed a guarantee that resource-owning test suites were relying on: that resources allocated in `beforeEach` and freed in `afterEach` would only ever exist `maxConcurrency` at a time.

In v4, with `describe.concurrent` and an expensive `beforeEach`, the runtime now fires every test's `beforeEach` to completion before any test body runs, because the FIFO limiter releases between leaf calls and the queued bodies are appended after every queued `beforeEach`. The result is that all N concurrent tests own their per-test resources simultaneously, regardless of `maxConcurrency`.

### Impact
This affects test suites that:
* Use `describe.concurrent` (or `concurrent: true` via config)
* Allocate per-test resources in `beforeEach` (DB pools, app instances, file handles, network sockets, cloned databases)
* Free those resources in `afterEach`

Just to give an example scenario, inside each of our tests, we create and connect to a database. In v3, we would have max 5 of those connections active at any one time. In v4 we have 400 (we have 400 tests), even though only 5 tests happening at once. The 395 sit there connected, waiting for a test slot. Every concurrent test holds its a  DB conn for the entire duration of all sibling tests' beforeEach calls.

The new behaviour is internally consistent and the PR description (#9653) is reasonable: `maxConcurrency` now means "max user functions executing at any instant", which is a sensible interpretation of the option name. But it leaves no built-in way to express "max tests that own resources at any instant". These were the same number in v3 (as a side effect of where the limiter wrapped); they're decoupled in v4.

The available knobs in v4 don't fill the gap:

  - `maxConcurrency`: now leaf-level, doesn't bound resource ownership
  - `maxWorkers` / `fileParallelism`: worker-level, doesn't help inside a single concurrent file
  - `pool`/`isolate`: orthogonal
  - `singleFork`/`singleThread`: collapses parallelism entirely, defeats the purpose of `describe.concurrent`

The only fix I can see is to add a paired semaphore in user-space (acquire in `beforeEach`, release in `afterEach`) or implement a custom test runner that overrides `onBeforeRunTask`/`onAfterRunTask`. Both work, but they require users to know that the v4 behaviour exists, and effectively re-implement the v3 guarantee outside of vitest. Workaround I've got going atm (per-worker semaphore in the test setup file):
```tsx
import { limitConcurrency } from '@vitest/runner/utils'

const limiter = limitConcurrency(5)
const releases = new WeakMap<object, () => void>()

beforeEach(async (context) => {
  const release = await limiter.acquire()
  releases.set(context.task, release)
  // ... real setup that allocates resources
})

afterEach(async (context) => {
  try {
    // ... real teardown that frees resources
  } finally {
    releases.get(context.task)?.()
    releases.delete(context.task)
  }
})
```

### What I'd like to see:

1. A new option along the lines of `maxInFlightTests` (or `sequence.maxInFlightTests`) that re-exposes the v3 guarantee - wraps `runTest` end-to-end in a separate semaphore, sized independently of `maxConcurrency`. Defaults to Infinity so it's opt-in and doesn't change behaviour for anyone.
2. Or documentation on `maxConcurrency` that explicitly calls out the v3 to v4 behaviour change and points users at the workaround pattern (acquire/release in setup/teardown), so the next team that hits this knows what's happening before they spend a day debugging connection limits.
3. Or a first-class hook in the runner API for "around test" with paired acquire/release semantics, so user-side semaphores have somewhere natural to live.

I'd be happy to put up a PR for option 1 if there's interest - it's a small change (a second `limitConcurrency` instance, used at the same call site #9653 removed) and it's strictly additive.





### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitest-dev-vitest-munmai6p?file=test%2Fleak.test.ts

Here's a basic example showing that hooks can exceed maxConcurrency.

title: False uncovered lines, phantom "if" branches, and incorrect function mappings in Vue SFC
body:
### Describe the bug

`@vitest/coverage-v8` reports **false uncovered lines, phantom "if" branches, and incorrect function/statement mappings** in Vue Single File Components when the Vite transform pipeline involves multiple chained source maps (as happens with the Nuxt plugin chain). All tests pass and all code paths are exercised, yet coverage is reported below 100%.

### What's wrong

Given a Vue SFC (`MyForm.vue`) with `defineExpose`, `useTemplateRef`, and an `async function triggerFormSubmit` containing an `if` guard, the coverage report shows:

```
------------|---------|----------|---------|---------|-------------------
File        | % Stmts | % Branch | % Funcs | % Lines | Uncovered Line #s
------------|---------|----------|---------|---------|-------------------
 MyForm.vue |   92.85 |       50 |     100 |    92.3 | 30
------------|---------|----------|---------|---------|-------------------
```

**Three distinct errors in `coverage-final.json`:**

1. **Line 30 (`}` — closing brace of `triggerFormSubmit`) is reported as uncovered** (statement `s["6"]` has count `0`), despite the function being called and tested.

2. **Phantom "if" branch at line 29**: A `branchMap` entry with `"type": "if"` appears at line 29, column 2. But line 29 in the source is `await form.value.submit();` — there is **no `if` statement there**. The actual `if (!form.value)` is at line 26. The branch counts are `[0, 1]`, falsely indicating one path was never taken.

3. **Function mapping drift**: `fnMap` reports `onSubmit` at line 25 (actual: line 21) and `triggerFormSubmit` at line 28 (actual: line 25) — a consistent ~3-4 line drift.

### Root cause

The issue is a **source map position drift** accumulated through the multi-step Vite transform pipeline for Vue SFCs:

1. `@vitejs/plugin-vue` compiles the SFC (script setup + inline template) → source map `#1`
2. `esbuild` strips TypeScript type annotations → source map `#2` (chained with `#1`)
3. Nuxt's `unimport` plugin injects auto-import statements at the top of the compiled output → source map `#3` (chained with `#2`)
4. `@nuxt/ui` registers additional component auto-imports → more transform layers

When V8 coverage data is mapped back through the final chained source map, the accumulated position errors cause functions, branches, and statements to be attributed to wrong source positions, including creating phantom branches where none exist.

### Evidence from `coverage-final.json`

```json
{
  "branchMap": {
    "0": {
      "loc": { "start": { "line": 29, "column": 2 }, "end": { "line": 32 } },
      "type": "if",
      "locations": [
        { "start": { "line": 29, "column": 2 }, "end": { "line": 32 } },
        { "start": {}, "end": {} }
      ],
      "line": 29
    }
  },
  "b": { "0": [0, 1] }
}
```

Line 29 in the source is `await form.value.submit();`. The phantom `"if"` branch comes from the compiled template's cache conditional (`_cache[N] || (...)`) being incorrectly source-mapped back to this position.

The uncovered statement:
```json
{
  "s": { "6": 0 },
  "statementMap": {
    "6": { "start": { "line": 30, "column": 0 }, "end": { "line": 30 } }
  }
}
```

Line 30 is `}` (closing brace of `triggerFormSubmit`), which was executed.

### What does NOT trigger the bug

- Removing `defineExpose` + `useTemplateRef` + `triggerFormSubmit` while keeping the rest identical → coverage reports 100%.
- Compiling the same SFC with `@vue/compiler-sfc` + `esbuild` directly (outside the Nuxt plugin chain) → produces **correct source maps**.
- The bug only manifests when the full Nuxt Vite plugin chain runs with its additional transform layers that inject code and shift positions.

## Reproduction

A full reproduction is available with explicit README here : https://github.com/antoinezanardi/v8-mapping-nuxt-issue

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm run prepare   # generates .nuxt directory
pnpm run test:coverage
```

**Expected:** All 4 tests pass. Coverage is 100% across all metrics since every line, branch, function, and statement is exercised.

**Actual:** All 4 tests pass, but coverage reports 92.85% statements, 50% branches, 92.3% lines with line 30 falsely uncovered.

### Source file under test

`app/components/MyForm.vue`:
```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { reactive } from "vue";
import type { FormSubmitEvent } from "@nuxt/ui";
import { z } from "zod";

const schema = z.object({
  name: z.string().min(1),
  value: z.string().min(1),
});

type FormData = z.output<typeof schema>;

const emit = defineEmits<{
  (e: "submitData", data: FormData): void;
}>();

const form = useTemplateRef<InstanceType<typeof import("#ui/types").Form>>("form");

const formState = reactive<FormData>({ name: "", value: "" });

function onSubmit(event: FormSubmitEvent<FormData>): void {
  emit("submitData", event.data);
}

async function triggerFormSubmit(): Promise<void> {
  if (!form.value) {
    return;
  }
  await form.value.submit();
}

defineExpose({ triggerFormSubmit });
</script>

<template>
  <UForm ref="form" data-testid="my-form" :schema="schema" :state="formState" @submit="onSubmit">
    <UFormField data-testid="form-name-field" label="Name" name="name">
      <UInput v-model="formState.name" placeholder="Name" />
    </UFormField>
    <UFormField data-testid="form-value-field" label="Value" name="value">
      <UInput v-model="formState.value" placeholder="Value" />
    </UFormField>
  </UForm>
</template>
```

### Minimal trigger conditions

The bug requires **all** of these in the same SFC:
- `@nuxt/ui` module loaded (provides auto-imports + additional Vite transforms)
- `useTemplateRef` referencing a template element
- `defineExpose` exposing a function
- An async function with an `if` guard
- A template using Nuxt UI components (`UForm`, `UFormField`, `UInput`)

Removing any one of `defineExpose`, `useTemplateRef`, or the `triggerFormSubmit` function eliminates the bug.

### System Info

| Package | Version |
|---|---|
| vitest | 4.1.3 |
| @vitest/coverage-v8 | 4.1.3 |
| nuxt | 4.4.2 |
| @nuxt/ui | 3.3.7 |
| @vitejs/plugin-vue | 6.0.5 |
| vue | 3.5.32 |
| vite | 7.3.2 |
| Node.js | v25.9.0 |
| OS | macOS |

### Used Package Manager

pnpm

> // These are Vue's internal rendering optimizations and should not appear in coverage

You should file a bug report to Vue about this. Why does it leave generated code in source maps? This causes users' debuggers to stop at code that is not their source code, and they see unexpected results in code coverage.

We cannot accept this kind of changes in Vitest, as this is not public API of Vue compiler. If they change this compiler output in next patch/minor/major version, we'll need to update this logic in Vitest. Supporting all versions of Vue compiler's internal output is not maintainable.

title: Coverage chunk writes should ensure `reportsDirectory/.tmp` exists before writing `coverage-*.json`
body:
### Describe the bug

When coverage is enabled, Vitest writes per-suite coverage JSON files into a temp directory under `coverage.reportsDirectory`.

In the unpatched `vitest@4.1.3` coverage code path, `onAfterSuiteRun()` writes a coverage chunk without first ensuring that `reportsDirectory/.tmp` still exists:

```js
const filename = resolve(this.coverageFilesDirectory, `coverage-${uniqueId++}.json`);
const promise = promises.writeFile(filename, JSON.stringify(coverage), 'utf-8');
```

We have previously observed this class of failure in coverage-enabled workspace runs, where the temp directory was missing at the point a coverage file was opened or stat'ed, with errors like:

```text
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, open '/.../coverage/<project>/.tmp/coverage-0.json'
```

or:

```text
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, lstat '/.../coverage/<project>/.tmp'
```

Because `vitest@4.1.3` still has the same write-without-`mkdir` assumption in this code path, we are currently carrying a local defensive patch that recreates the temp directory immediately before each coverage chunk write:

```js
const promise = promises
  .mkdir(this.coverageFilesDirectory, { recursive: true })
  .then(() => promises.writeFile(filename, JSON.stringify(coverage), 'utf-8'));
```

This is a no-op when the directory already exists, but it makes the write robust if the temp directory is missing at write time.

The practical impact is that a test run that otherwise completed successfully can still fail at the coverage persistence step. From a user perspective, that is a high-friction failure mode because:

- tests may already be green
- the failure happens late, during coverage result flushing
- the error points at Vitest's internal `.tmp/coverage-*.json` files rather than at user test code
- it can make CI or task-runner integrations look flaky even when the tests themselves are stable


### Reproduction

I do not have a public minimal reproduction repo yet because the original workspace where this was first observed is private.

What I can state directly:

1. We observed coverage failures on the `.tmp/coverage-*.json` path family and on missing `.tmp` directories in real workspace runs.
2. The unpatched `vitest@4.1.3` code path still performs a bare `writeFile()` into that temp directory.
3. We added a local defensive patch to that `writeFile()` path.

The scenario where that patch is necessary is:

1. Run Vitest with coverage enabled and a concrete `coverage.reportsDirectory`.
2. Let Vitest create its temp coverage directory during `clean()`.
3. Later, when `onAfterSuiteRun()` tries to write `coverage-*.json`, the temp directory is no longer present.
4. The run fails with `ENOENT` on `reportsDirectory/.tmp/coverage-*.json` or on the missing `.tmp` directory itself.

From Vitest's perspective, the key condition is simply this: `onAfterSuiteRun()` currently assumes the temp directory created earlier still exists at write time.

I suspect this can show up more easily when Vitest is run through another task runner / wrapper that manages per-project coverage directories, cleans outputs between runs, or coordinates repeated isolated test runs, but I have not reduced that to a public minimal reproduction yet.

If needed, I can work on a standalone public reproduction. Right now the strongest directly-supported claim is that the write path is not defensive against a missing temp directory.

## Why this is worth fixing upstream

Even if the missing-directory condition is more likely to surface in orchestrated or wrapped executions, this still looks worth hardening in Vitest itself.

Reasons:

- the failure mode is expensive for users because it turns successful test execution into a failing overall command late in the run
- the error surface is confusing because it looks like an internal Vitest filesystem problem rather than an actionable user mistake
- coverage temp-file handling is Vitest-owned internal state, so making that write path defensive improves robustness at the correct boundary
- downstream users should not need to carry a patch for an idempotent directory-creation guard around an internal temporary file write

## Why this patch is needed

The current flow creates `coverageFilesDirectory` in `clean()`, but later writes in `onAfterSuiteRun()` do not re-check that the directory still exists.

That means the write path is only correct if the directory lifetime is guaranteed from the initial `clean()` call until every later coverage chunk write happens.

We have evidence that this guarantee did not hold in at least one real coverage-enabled execution, because the failing paths were exactly the temp coverage file locations under `.tmp`.

Recreating the directory directly before `writeFile()` makes the write idempotent and removes that assumption.

## Why the change is low risk

The proposed change is intentionally very small and local.

- it only touches the coverage temp-file write path
- it uses `mkdir(..., { recursive: true })`, which is already safe when the directory exists
- it does not change coverage file names, file contents, report formats, or aggregation logic
- it preserves the existing behavior in the normal case and only adds resilience in the missing-directory case

So the fix is effectively a defensive precondition check directly at the point of file output.

## Current workaround

We are currently working around this downstream by patching `vitest@4.1.3` locally.

Patch shape:

```diff
- const promise = promises.writeFile(filename, JSON.stringify(coverage), 'utf-8')
+ const promise = promises.mkdir(this.coverageFilesDirectory, { recursive: true }).then(
+   () => promises.writeFile(filename, JSON.stringify(coverage), 'utf-8')
+ )
```

In our environment, this is applied via the package manager's patch mechanism rather than by forking Vitest.

## Evidence from the workaround

This is not yet a public minimal reproduction, so I do not want to overstate the proof.

What I can say accurately is:

- without this defensive guard, we have observed coverage failures on Vitest temp paths such as `coverage/<project>/.tmp/coverage-*.json`
- with this patch applied, our current coverage-enabled workspace verification completes successfully on `vitest@4.1.3` / `@vitest/coverage-v8@4.1.3`
- the patch has not caused any observable change in coverage output shape or normal successful runs; it only hardens the temp-file write path

So while this is not a substitute for a standalone public reproduction, it is practical evidence that the change is safe and useful in a real coverage-enabled setup.

## Suggested solution

Make `onAfterSuiteRun()` ensure `coverageFilesDirectory` exists before writing the JSON file.

This looks like a good upstream tradeoff because the implementation cost is minimal, the change is narrowly scoped, and the upside is improved reliability for coverage-enabled runs across more execution environments.

Conceptually:

```js
const filename = resolve(this.coverageFilesDirectory, `coverage-${uniqueId++}.json`);
const promise = promises
  .mkdir(this.coverageFilesDirectory, { recursive: true })
  .then(() => promises.writeFile(filename, JSON.stringify(coverage), 'utf-8'));
this.pendingPromises.push(promise);
```

```shell
System:

    CPU: (16) x64 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-11900H @ 2.50GHz

```

Yes, please do. 🙏

This is not just coverage related - JSON, junit, html and other reporters that write to file system will run into this too.

If code coverage result writing did not crash here, you would see missing coverage results. Having this incorrect behaviour kicking in silently would be difficult to debug by users. Make sure you are not running multiple Vitests with same reportsDirectory at the same time`.

Try configuring different paths for [`coverage.reportsDirectory`](https://vitest.dev/config/coverage.html#coverage-reportsdirectory) for each Vitest runs that you do simultaneously.

title: Vite Vulnerable to Arbitrary File Read via Vite Dev Server WebSocket (CVE-2026-39363)
body:
### Describe the bug

going through some of our security notifications and this one popped up on a project using @vitest/coverage-v8 as a devDependancy (an older version).

Wondering if there's any plan in `vitest` to upgrade `vite` above 7.1.5 to fix this vuln?

### Reproduction

clone https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest.git, run `pnpm install`, run `pnpm why vite`, get 

```
vite@7.1.5
├─┬ @unocss/vite@66.6.6
│ └─┬ unocss@66.6.6
│   └── @vitest/ui@4.1.4 (devDependencies)
├─┬ @vitejs/plugin-vue@6.0.4
│ └── @vitest/ui@4.1.4 (devDependencies)
├── @vitest/mocker@4.1.4 (devDependencies)
```

title: `spyOn` is not possible on private or protected method
body:
### Describe the bug

TypeScript [allows accessing private and protected methods using bracket notation](https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/classes.html#caveats). This is useful for unit testing, if you want to check a private/protected method works as expected.

Vitest does not allow using `spyOn` on a private/protected method (e.g. you want to test a public method that uses a private method to load data) unless you cast to any. So `vi.spyOn(myObject, 'privateMethod')` does not work while  `vi.spyOn(myObject as any, 'privateMethod')` works as expected. But this comes with the caveat that Vitest does not know about the types this function returns.

author: JakobDev
maintainer_reply:
The typescript's behavior looks a bit crazy, but since they are saying this trick is literally meant for "unit test", maybe it's reasonable to make this possible.

I thought this is outright impossible as type utility but it seems somehow possible according to quick research below:

<details><summary>Research note</summary>

# TypeScript `private` Soft-Privacy Notes

Date: 2026-04-23

## Context

This note records findings on TypeScript's soft-private behavior for `private` class members, especially the bracket-notation escape hatch and whether that enables a generic "strip private" utility type.

Repo note: markdown is linted broadly in this repo, so this note lives under `.dev-notes/dist/`.

**Location:** `eslint.config.js#L107`

## Main finding

TypeScript `private` is soft-private.

- Value-level property access rejects `obj.privateName` outside the class.
- Value-level bracket access allows `obj["privateName"]`.
- Type-level indexed access also allows `T["privateName"]` if the private member name is already known.
- But `keyof T` does not include private members from outside the class.
- Mapped types over `keyof T` therefore only see the public surface.

This means the type system exposes enough to target a known private key, but not enough to generically enumerate private keys.

## Consequence for utility types

A fully generic utility such as `StripPrivate<T>`, `ExposePrivate<T>`, or `fieldof T` is not implementable in normal TypeScript today if it depends on discovering private keys from a class type.

What is possible is an explicit-key helper for test-only or escape-hatch usage:

```ts
type PublicClone<T> = { [P in keyof T]: T[P] }

type UnsafePick<T, K extends string> = {
  [P in K]: (T & Record<P, unknown>)[P]
}

type Expose<T, K extends string> = PublicClone<T> & UnsafePick<T, K>
```

This works for known keys like `Expose<MySafe, "secretKey">`, but it does not discover private keys automatically.

## Local verification

Checked locally with `pnpm exec tsc`:

- `keyof C` only included the public key `"y"`, not private `"x"`.
- `{ [P in keyof C]: C[P] }` produced a public-only clone.
- `type X = C["x"]` compiled.
- Intersecting the public clone with an explicit-key helper exposed `x` as a readable property in the resulting type.

Summary:

- discover private keys: no
- index a known private key: yes
- build a generic private-stripper: no
- build an explicit-key escape hatch: yes

## Vitest `vi.spyOn` note

This same TypeScript behavior is directly relevant to `vitest-dev/vitest#10172`, where `vi.spyOn(obj, 'privateMethod')` is rejected unless the object is cast to `any`.

Issue:

- <https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/10172>

### Current typing choke point

Vitest's `spyOn` overloads constrain the key through `Methods<Required<T>>`, `Classes<Required<T>>`, and `Properties<Required<T>>`:

- **Location:** `packages/spy/src/index.ts#L262`

Relevant excerpt:

```ts
export function spyOn<T extends object, S extends Properties<Required<T>>>(
  object: T,
  key: S,
  accessor: 'get',
): Mock<() => T[S]>

export function spyOn<T extends object, G extends Properties<Required<T>>>(
  object: T,
  key: G,
  accessor: 'set',
): Mock<(arg: T[G]) => void>

export function spyOn<T extends object, M extends Classes<Required<T>> | Methods<Required<T>>>(
  object: T,
  key: M,
): Required<T>[M] extends Constructable | Procedure
  ? Mock<Required<T>[M]>
  : never
```

Those helper types are defined here:

- **Location:** `packages/spy/src/types.ts#L187`

Relevant excerpt:

```ts
export type Methods<T> = keyof {
  [K in keyof T as T[K] extends Procedure ? K : never]: T[K];
}

export type Properties<T> = {
  [K in keyof T]: T[K] extends Procedure ? never : K;
}[keyof T] & (string | symbol)

export type Classes<T> = {
  [K in keyof T]: T[K] extends new (...args: any[]) => any ? K : never;
}[keyof T] & (string | symbol)
```

They are built from `keyof T`, which means:

- outside the class, `private` / `protected` members are not visible
- those keys are filtered out before `spyOn` overload resolution happens

### Why `spyOn` is a plausible exception

Unlike a generic utility type, `spyOn` already receives the key literal at the call site.

That matters because TypeScript allows:

- `obj["privateMethod"]`
- `T["privateMethod"]` if the key name is already known

But TypeScript still does not allow:

- generic discovery of all private keys through `keyof`

So this is the important distinction:

- not possible: "discover all private keys"
- possible: "given this exact key literal, determine whether it indexes a method"

Minimal example of the asymmetry:

```ts
class Example {
  private loadData(id: string) {
    return { id }
  }

  public run(id: string) {
    return this.loadData(id)
  }
}

type K = keyof Example
// "run"

type LoadData = Example['loadData']
// (id: string) => { id: string }
```

### Feasibility

This looks technically feasible.

In local `tsc` experiments, a fallback overload based on a known string key can:

- accept `spyOn(obj, 'privateMethod')`
- infer the private method's parameter and return types
- continue rejecting non-function keys
- continue rejecting nonexistent keys

Sketch of the kind of fallback overload that seems viable:

```ts
type KnownMethod<T extends object, K extends string>
  = (T & Record<K, unknown>)[K] extends Procedure | Constructable ? K : never

export function spyOn<T extends object, K extends string>(
  object: T,
  key: KnownMethod<T, K>,
): (T & Record<K, unknown>)[K] extends Constructable | Procedure
  ? Mock<(T & Record<K, unknown>)[K]>
  : never
```

The important property of this shape is that it does not try to discover private keys with `keyof`. It only asks whether the already-provided key literal indexes a callable member.

So the constraint here is not technical impossibility. It is whether Vitest wants to model TypeScript's documented soft-private testing escape hatch in its public typings.

## Relevant upstream issues

### TypeScript

- `microsoft/TypeScript#19335` "Class private members accessible from outside with brackets notation"
  - Canonical complaint about bracket notation bypassing `private`
  - Closed as working as intended
  - <https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/19335>

- `microsoft/TypeScript#46802` "[Feature Request] fieldof similar to keyof but include private and protected field"
  - Direct request for a `keyof`-like operator that includes private/protected members
  - <https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/46802>

- `microsoft/TypeScript#22677` "Removing `private` modifier from types"
  - Very close to the idea of a private-stripping mapped-type modifier
  - <https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/22677>

- `microsoft/TypeScript#18499` "Explain why private and protected members in a class affect their compatibility"
  - Includes testing/mocking pain from private members participating in compatibility
  - <https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/18499>

- `microsoft/TypeScript#44670` "Account for discrepancy between soft privacy of `private` vs hard privacy of `#`"
  - Documents user confusion around soft-private vs hard-private
  - <https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/44670>

- `microsoft/TypeScript#14186` "Private methods accessed using bracket notation are reported as 'unused'"
  - Shows secondary edge cases caused by bracket-notation access
  - <https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/14186>

### Utility libraries

- `sindresorhus/type-fest#20` "Proposal: ExcludeProps"
  - Not the same utility, but explicitly notes that private/protected props are not properly supported in a mapped-type-style helper
  - <https://github.com/sindresorhus/type-fest/issues/20>

I did not find a strong corresponding issue in `ts-toolbelt` or `utility-types` during a quick issue search. That should be treated as "not found yet", not as proof none exist.

## Docs / references

- TypeScript handbook class caveats
  - <https://www.typescriptlang.org/docs/handbook/2/classes.html#caveats>

- TypeScript FAQ
  - Mentions that `private` class members are visible at runtime
  - <https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/wiki/FAQ>

## Practical guidance

- If strict non-bypassable privacy matters, use ECMAScript `#private` fields.
- If tests need access to TypeScript-private members, use an explicit-key helper and keep it clearly test-scoped.
- Do not expect `keyof`, mapped types, or common utility libraries to surface class private members automatically.

</details>

title: merge-reports crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading importers)' when blob graph contains edges to file-less modules
body:
### Describe the bug

`vitest run --merge-reports` crashes when the serialized module graph in a blob report contains an edge whose target was filtered out of serialization.

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'importers')
 ❯ .../vitest/dist/chunks/index.DXMFO5MJ.js:3325:17
 ❯ deserializeEnvironmentModuleGraph .../vitest/dist/chunks/index.DXMFO5MJ.js:3318:21
 ❯ .../vitest/dist/chunks/index.DXMFO5MJ.js:3256:5
 ❯ .../vitest/dist/chunks/index.DXMFO5MJ.js:3254:50
 ❯ .../vitest/dist/chunks/index.DXMFO5MJ.js:3248:43
```

### Root cause

In `packages/vitest/src/node/reporters/blob.ts`:

```ts
// serialize — skips modules without `file`…
for (const [id, mod] of environment.moduleGraph.idToModuleMap.entries()) {
  if (!mod.file) continue
  const importedIds: number[] = []
  for (const importedNode of mod.importedModules) {
    if (importedNode.id) {
      importedIds.push(getIdIndex(importedNode.id))   // …but still records edges TO them
    }
  }
  modules.push([getIdIndex(id), getIdIndex(mod.file), getIdIndex(mod.url), importedIds])
}

// deserialize
serialized.modules.forEach(([id, _file, _url, importedIds]) => {
  const moduleId = serialized.idTable[id]
  const moduleNode = nodesById.get(moduleId)!
  importedIds.forEach((importedIdIndex) => {
    const importedId = serialized.idTable[importedIdIndex]
    const importedNode = nodesById.get(importedId)!   // undefined when target had no `file`
    moduleNode.importedModules.add(importedNode)
    importedNode.importers.add(moduleNode)            // 💥 TypeError
  })
})
```

`serializeEnvironmentModuleGraph` skips modules without `file`, but still records import edges whose target has an `id` even if that target has no `file`. On restore, `nodesById.get(importedId)` is `undefined` for those targets and the subsequent `.importers.add(...)` throws.

The non-null assertions on `nodesById.get(importedId)!` (and `nodesById.get(moduleId)!`) hide the invariant mismatch between serialize and deserialize.

### Introduced by

PR #9740 / commit 843554bf04aa325c9e28fc71d412660d170e87a5 (first shipped in 4.1.0-beta.6, still present on `main`).

### Trigger

Reproduces reliably with Vitest 4.1.0 + Vite 8 when sharded blob reports contain cross-module import edges that target virtual / file-less modules. Vite 8 exposes more modules that have an `id` but no `file` than Vite 6 does, which is likely why this latent bug now fires for us (our catalog bump from Vite 6 to Vite 8 is what turned green CI red).

The crash does not depend on browser mode, coverage, or UI — a plain sharded run followed by `vitest run --merge-reports=./.vitest-reports --reporter=default` is enough.

### Suggested fix

Guard against the missing node during restore:

```diff
         importedIds.forEach((importedIdIndex) => {
             const importedId = serialized.idTable[importedIdIndex]
-            const importedNode = nodesById.get(importedId)!
+            const importedNode = nodesById.get(importedId)
+            if (!importedNode) return
             moduleNode.importedModules.add(importedNode)
             importedNode.importers.add(moduleNode)
         })
```

Alternative (strictly more correct): filter `importedIds` at serialization time so only edges whose target was actually serialized are kept, then the deserializer invariant holds without a runtime guard.

### System Info

```
vitest: 4.1.0
vite:   8.0.5
node:   v22
pnpm:   10.30.1
```

### Related

- #10032 — also merge-reports + Vite 8 + Vitest 4.1, but a different symptom (v8 coverage native crash)
- #9685 — earlier merge-reports / module graph issue, closed

- [x] This is a concrete bug

title: birpc proxy in browser mode doesn't guard against toJSON, causing unhandled errors
body:
### Describe the bug

When using Vitest browser mode, the birpc RPC proxy created in `@vitest/browser/dist/client.js` intercepts all property accesses and converts them to RPC calls. The proxy has a special case for `"then"` (to avoid Promise-like behavior), but it does **not** guard against `"toJSON"`.

When any code calls `JSON.stringify()` on an object that references `globalThis.__vitest_worker__` (or any object in the prototype chain that includes the birpc proxy), the `toJSON` trap fires, sending an RPC request to the server. Since `"toJSON"` is not a registered RPC function, this produces:

```
[birpc] function "toJSON" not found
```

This manifests as unhandled errors in the test output, even though the tests themselves pass.

### Reproduction

1. Create a vitest browser mode test
2. In the test, access any object that transitively references `globalThis.__vitest_worker__.rpc`
3. Call `JSON.stringify()` on that object (or let a framework's change detection do it)
4. Observe `[birpc] function "toJSON" not found` error

### Expected behavior

The birpc proxy should handle `"toJSON"` the same way it handles `"then"` — by returning `undefined` to indicate the object is not JSON-serializable via a custom `toJSON` method.

### Suggested fix

In the birpc proxy handler (or `createBirpc` / `createSafeRpc`), add `"toJSON"` to the list of trapped methods that return `undefined`:

```js
// Current
if (method === 'then') return undefined;

// Suggested
if (method === 'then' || method === 'toJSON') return undefined;
```

### Environment

- Vitest: 4.0.18
- @vitest/browser: 4.0.18
- Browser: Chromium (via Playwright)
- OS: macOS / Linux
author: AlonMiz
maintainer_reply: please provide actual use case leading to an error instead of direct `JSON.stringify({ rpc: globalThis.__vitest_worker__.rpc })`.

title: "cannot find module" for path without file extensions for packages with incomplete ESM support
body:
### Describe the bug

I have created a minimal repro here: https://github.com/Pistonight/vitest-repros/tree/vitest_bug/cannot_find_file_without_extension

There are some packages like [@fluentui/react-icons](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@fluentui/react-icons) that have [improper ESM support](https://github.com/microsoft/fluentui-system-icons/issues/789). The package manifest claims an `"import"` field in `"exports"` but the actual file is not conformant to ESM because it tries to import a path without a file extension. But the package also doesn't have `"type": "module"`. 

`vitest` is able to resolve imports from packages like this if it's used directly in a project (i.e. running `vitest` in `my-project`, which has some `foo.ts` that imports from `@fluentui/react-icons`)

However, when I make a package that depends on @fluentui/react-icons (for example a shared react components package), The output bundle would contain something like `import { ... } from "@fluentui/react-icons"`. Since the code from my package is ESM, I put `"type": "module"` in my `package.json`.

Now if `my-project` imports `my-package`, vitest cannot resolve imports from @fluentui/react-icons. I feel like this is a bug because the behavior shouldn't be different if `my-project` imports the broken package directly or through `my-package`.

 Currently the workaround is to remove `"type": "module"` in my package (since there doesn't seem to be a plan for upstream to fix the issue)

title: Coverage deadlocks in per-file isolation on large React+jsdom suite (4308 tests / 255 files)
body:
## Summary

Vitest 4.1.4 with coverage enabled hangs deterministically on a 255-file / 4308-test React+jsdom suite. Without coverage the suite completes cleanly. Adding coverage makes vitest's module loader stall partway through the run; tests never start, no test timeout fires, vitest never prints a summary.

I don't have a minimal reproducer (sorry — happy to put one together if maintainers indicate it would help). But I've ruled out enough configuration variables that I think the cause is narrow enough to be useful as-is.

## Environment

- vitest \`4.1.4\`
- \`@vitest/coverage-v8\` \`4.1.2\` (also reproduced with \`@vitest/coverage-istanbul\` \`4.1.5\`)
- Node \`24.x\` on \`ubuntu-24.04\` (GitHub Actions \`ubuntu-latest\`)
- \`jsdom\` environment, React 18 + Testing Library, \`@vitejs/plugin-react\`
- \`pool: 'forks'\` (default; also reproduced with \`pool: 'threads'\`)
- Suite size: 255 test files, 4308 tests, ~39,800 source statements across the coverage \`include\` glob

## Symptom

With coverage enabled, vitest streams test results normally for ~50–60 seconds, files complete, then **total stdout silence**. The 30s \`testTimeout\` never fires. After 5+ minutes the run is still hung. Last successful test result is always at the same stop point, run after run.

When the wrapping run-tests script eventually force-kills the parent, GitHub Actions' orphan-process cleanup terminates 2 surviving \`MainThread\` workers (default 4 forks were spawned — 2 are missing, but no V8 \"heap out of memory\" stack trace appears anywhere in the log).

The 36 of 255 test files that complete are almost entirely **pure-TypeScript**: services, hooks, engine, store, utils, integration. The handful of completing component tests are the ones that mock all their imports. The moment a test file with real React component imports hits a fork, that fork goes silent.

## What was ruled out

| Change | Result |
|---|---|
| \`NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=6144\` | Same hang at same stop point. No V8 OOM ever logged. |
| Switch to \`@vitest/coverage-istanbul\` | Same hang at same stop point. |
| \`pool: 'threads'\` instead of \`forks\` | Same hang at same stop point. |
| Scope to \`__tests__/components\` only | Hangs after 3 files (deterministically the 3 that mock everything). |
| \`--isolate=false\` | **Hang disappears.** Vitest completes in seconds, runs all 256 files. (200+ failures from state pollution because suite isn't designed for shared context, and the coverage report still doesn't write before the wrapping process exits — but the loader hang is clearly gone.) |

## Hypothesis

The deadlock lives in the **per-file isolated module-load + instrumentation path**. Each test file in default isolation gets a fresh execution context; coverage instrumentation has to be applied to every imported source file in that context. For test files that pull in deep React+jsdom+component import graphs across many forks/threads doing the same work in parallel, something deadlocks.

Notable signals:
- The hang is in **module load**, not test execution (no test timeout fires).
- It's independent of pool architecture (forks vs threads).
- It's independent of coverage provider (v8 vs istanbul).
- It only manifests with coverage enabled.
- It only manifests with isolation enabled (default).
- Workaround: \`--isolate=false\` (with the obvious cost of breaking tests that rely on isolation).

## What would help me help you

- Should I produce a minimal reproducer? I can try, though shrinking a 4k-test React suite to a public repro is non-trivial. If a maintainer can suggest specific instrumentation to add (debug log points, vitest-internal flags, etc.) before I trim, that would save time.
- Are there known related upstream issues I should link?
- Any flags I haven't tried that might narrow it further?

Will keep watching the issue. Thanks for the work on vitest.

title: Allow passing `ReadonlyArray<T>`s to `expect.toBeOneOf`
body:
### Clear and concise description of the problem

Currently, the `expect.toBeOneOf` matcher does not allow passing in `ReadonlyArray`s or `ReadonlySet`s in TypeScript without giving type errors.

The actual implementation does not modify either argument type in any way, shape or form - this is purely a typing issue.

Moreover, this would also prevent the asymmetric matcher from accidentally mutating its passed-in arguments (which could easily corrupt shared global state inside `noIsolate` runs).

### Suggested solution

Change the typing to use `ReadonlyArray<T>` and `ReadonlySet<T>` instead of `Array<T>` and `Set<T>`.

### Alternative

Don't pass in readonly arrays or sets (though this isn't exactly desireable)

### Additional context

[TS Playground link](https://www.typescriptlang.org/play/?#code/JYWwDg9gTgLgBAbzsGAaOBTAHmDBjeAXzgDMoIQ4ByANxQwGcYqBuAWAChOB6b5EAIYBzYADsMcGAAtgDZHIGjMWGBiiiBAGzh4IopovgBXBhgAmmTaYDuUtRk6798AIIAZNwHkA6gFEAInAAvHAA2lQuVOhUAEJUALpwAnJOTOxcHCgAFFQMUhBGmhYARhIucNBwcehZAJTBAHyInHDKuAQ5kbUAdDAQMRhZ2O0wvf0YnuKeJFnuXn7+tbXphMucQA)

title: `concurrencyId` not exposed to custom reporters
body:
### Clear and concise description of the problem

Vitest runs tests in parallel across workers, but custom reporters have no way to know which worker / concurrency lane a given test ran on.

Knowing the concurrency lane is useful for diagnosing flakes that correlate with specific workers, e.g. resource contention, port collisions, or state leaked between tests sharing a worker.


### Suggested solution

It would be useful for the reporter API to expose a `concurrencyId` (or worker id) on each `TestCase` or test result. That's what Playwright Test do.

title: coverage-v8: rolldown fails to parse JSON files imported via ?import query
body:
### Describe the bug

- When `@vitest/coverage-v8` is enabled and the source code imports a `.json` file (e.g. via `import data from "./data.json"`), the V8 coverage remap phase invokes rolldown's AST parser on the file's bundled URL (which carries Vite's `?import` query string). 
- Rolldown only parses JS/TS, so it throws `RolldownError: Parse failed with 1 error: Expected a semicolon or an implicit semicolon after a statement` and excludes the file from coverage.

Although `coverage.include` is already restricted to JS/TS extensions (`src/**/*.{ts,tsx}`), JSON files still reach the remap step because the include filter is applied **after** the remap attempt, not before.

The error is non-fatal (file is excluded), but produces large amounts of stack-trace noise on every run and pollutes CI logs. JSON files aren't executable code so they wouldn't contribute meaningful coverage anyway, they should be filtered out before being handed to rolldown.

This is a regression from Vitest v3 (v8-to-istanbul) which silently handled non-JS files.

**Affected files in real projects:**
- Any module-level `import x from "./x.json"`

**Workaround** that currently silences the warnings:

```ts
coverage: {
  include: ["src/**/*.{ts,tsx}"],
  exclude: ["**/*.json"],
}
```

But this is not officially documented, and users naturally expect `include` alone to be sufficient.

### Reproduction

**Reproduction:** https://github.com/lyhoang-web-dev/vitest-dev-vitest

**Expected:** JSON files are silently skipped by the coverage remapper (matches v3 behaviour).
**Actual:** Rolldown parser throws and dumps a multi-line stack trace per JSON file.

title: Setting `window.innerWidth` doesn't actually set `innerWidth` on happy-dom's `window` object
body:
### Describe the bug

I was having unexpected test failures in some of my tests ran in happy-dom environment related to `window.matchMedia()`, after digging a bit and adding a few `console.log` statements in node_modules/happy-dom/ I discovered that the modifications to `window.innerWidth` in my tests were not reflected on the window object the window methods like `matchMedia()` were bound to. Here is the minimal reproduction to demonstrate the issue:

```typescript
test('window.matchMedia()', () => {
  window.innerWidth = 100;
  expect(window.matchMedia('(max-width: 100px)').matches).toBe(true);
});
```

adding the following at the top of this test file fixes the issue:
```typescript
import { Window } from 'happy-dom';

const window = new Window();
```
But obviously it would be desirable to not have to do this in every test file and not have to explain that it's only done due to a bug in comments.

author: arthur-cornfield
maintainer_reply:
From the rough reading, it looks to me that Vitest intentionally doesn’t write every `window` assignment through to the underlying happy-dom/jsdom `Window`; it keeps a facade so `window`, `self`, `global`, and `globalThis` share state consistently.

https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/d3c964bfcb5a47840e892e7ff4b1146dd4ca8b6d/packages/vitest/src/integrations/env/utils.ts#L69-L83

The obvious "fix" would be write through `win[key] = value`, but this would be likely too breaking change since some direct assignment such as `window.document = ...` or `window.location = ...` seems to cause hard errors, which is currently allowed since it just swaps out as global getter/setter level.

That said, happy-dom making assigned `innerWidth` visible to `matchMedia()` seems like useful behavior for Vitest to preserve even though in real window `window.innerWidth` isn't even writable. A reasonable Vitest-side direction could be a small explicit allowlist of mutable window state, e.g. viewport-related properties, that should write through to the backing DOM window.

---

While playing around with some, it might not be that breaking to always assign `window[key] = ...`.

title: `BaseReporter.logFailedTask` crashes when `onUserConsoleLog` is missing on the receiver; replayed logs are lost on `silent: 'passed-only'`
body:
### Describe the bug

`BaseReporter.logFailedTask` calls `this.onUserConsoleLog(log, "failed")` unguarded ([packages/vitest/src/node/reporters/base.ts](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/main/packages/vitest/src/node/reporters/base.ts), installed dist `index.UpGiHP7g.js:2238-2240`):
```
logFailedTask(task) {
    if (this.silent === "passed-only")
        for (const log of task.logs || [])
            this.onUserConsoleLog(log, "failed");
}
```

If anything has shadowed or removed `onUserConsoleLog` on the receiver, this throws `TypeError: this.onUserConsoleLog is not a function`. The reporter dispatcher catches it (`this.vitest.state.catchError(..., "Unhandled Reporter Error")` in `TestRun.updated`), so the run survives — but the failing test's captured logs that `passed-only` exists to surface are silently dropped, replaced with `Unhandled Reporter Error` noise on the summary.

We hit this in production via the VSCode Vitest extension (which deliberately mutates `e.onUserConsoleLog = void 0` on every non-own reporter — [separate report filed at `vitest-dev/vscode`](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vscode/issues/786)). But the underlying call site in vitest is fragile by itself: it assumes nothing in the rest of the reporter dispatch — including legitimate downstream consumers extending `BaseReporter` — has touched the method.

Suggested fix: route the replay through the existing event broadcast — `this.ctx.vitest.report("onUserConsoleLog", log)` or equivalent — so replay uses the same delivery path as every other log and doesn't depend on the receiver's prototype shape. A bare `?.` guard prevents the crash but silently drops the logs, which is worse than the current crash since the user loses diagnostic output with no warning.

Reproduced on `vitest@4.0.18`, `vitest@4.1.6`, and present on `main` (5.0.0-beta.2) at the same line.

Not submitting a PR for this — happy to if a maintainer confirms the preferred direction.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/rhwinter/vitest-loggingError

```
git clone https://github.com/rhwinter/vitest-loggingError
cd vitest-loggingError
npm install
npm run repro:forced
```

`broken-reporter.js` is a 5-line `DefaultReporter` subclass with one assignment that shadows `onUserConsoleLog` on the instance — the smallest change that exposes the unguarded call site. The forced repro produces this stack:

title: coverage-v8: Text reporter counts ~2x branches of JSON coverage file for nested ternaries (React/TypeScript)
body:
## Description

When using `@vitest/coverage-v8` in a React/TypeScript project, the **text reporter** counts approximately **2× more branches** than what is reported in `coverage-final.json` for the same codebase. This causes the text reporter to show ~94–95% branch coverage while the JSON canonical file shows 100% branch coverage.

## Environment

- **Vitest:** 4.1.6
- **@vitest/coverage-v8:** 4.1.6
- **ast-v8-to-istanbul:** 1.0.0 (latest — already includes fix from PR #138)
- **Node.js:** 22.x
- **Framework:** React 18 + TypeScript
- **Not Vue SFC** — plain React/TypeScript project

## Reproduction

The discrepancy appears on nested ternary chains such as:

```typescript
const normalizedQty = isCashDirectDeposit
  ? (direction === 'depot' ? Math.abs(form.quantity) : -Math.abs(form.quantity))
  : form.type === 'Frais'
    ? forfait ? -1 : -Math.abs(form.quantity)
    : form.type === 'Revenu'
    ? Math.abs(form.quantity)
    : form.quantity;
```

## Observed behavior

Text reporter output:
```
All files | % Stmts | % Branch | % Funcs | % Lines
          |   100   |  94.79   |   100   |   100

Branches: 94.79% ( 1348/1424 )
```

JSON coverage (`coverage-final.json`) analysis:
```
Total uncovered branches: 0/689 (100.00%)
```

**The text reporter counts 1424 branches, while the JSON counts 689 — roughly 2×.**

All 689 branches are covered (0 uncovered in JSON). The ~735 extra "branches" in the text reporter appear to come from nested ternary expressions being counted multiple times.

## Expected behavior

Text reporter branch count should match the JSON coverage file count, or at minimum produce the same covered/total ratio.

## Additional notes

- This is **not** the Vue SFC NaN issue from #9725 — that was fixed in ast-v8-to-istanbul v0.3.12/v1.0.0, which we already have installed
- This is **not** the missing branches issue from #140 or #145
- Switching to `provider: 'istanbul'` via `--coverage.provider=istanbul` CLI flag shows the **same 1424 branch count** in the text reporter, suggesting the bug is in the **text reporter logic**, not the v8/istanbul provider itself
- The JSON `coverage-final.json` correctly reports 100% branch coverage — only the text reporter is wrong

## Workaround

Currently setting the coverage threshold to 94% instead of 100% to accommodate the false count. The JSON canonical output confirms true 100% coverage.

title: @vitest/mocker: `vi.mock(` substring inside a comment triggers TLA hoist, deadlocks browser mode with cyclic imports
body:
With the comment:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/13987622-79b1-442a-ab36-cf7aba0e103c

Without the comment:

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/17bd2172-4b2b-4e63-b751-a31bcb409d05

---

### Summary

`@vitest/mocker`'s `hoistMocksPlugin` decides whether to hoist by running a raw-source regex against the file. The regex has no awareness of comments or string literals, so the substring `vi.mock(` appearing in a JSDoc comment is enough to flip hoisting on. When hoisting is on, every static `import` in the file is rewritten as a top-level `await wrapDynamicImport(...)`. Combined with a benign source-level import cycle, this deadlocks chromium's ESM loader in `vitest --project=browser` and the test sits in `[queued]` forever.

### Repro

https://github.com/shahmir-oscilar/vitest-mocker-hoist-comment-false-positive

```bash
git clone https://github.com/shahmir-oscilar/vitest-mocker-hoist-comment-false-positive
cd vitest-mocker-hoist-comment-false-positive
npm install
npx playwright install chromium
npm run test:browser
```

**Actual:** test hangs in `[queued]` indefinitely; only `RUN  v4.1.6 …` is printed.
**Expected:** test passes in ~2s.

To confirm: open `src/cycle-a.ts`, delete the line containing the literal `` `vi.mock('./cycle-b')` `` (it's inside a JSDoc comment — production code is untouched), and re-run. Now it passes in ~450ms.
author: shahmir-oscilar
maintainer_reply:
Cyclic import is already a smell, but Vitest shouldn't overmatch transform to avoid changing semantics when possible.

The cyclic dynamic import hits deadlock (and it doesn't with static import) because of a following structure:

```text
Original source graph

cycle.test.ts
   |
   | static import { fromA }
   v
cycle-a.ts  <----------------.
   |                          |
   | static import { fromB }  | static import { fromA }
   v                          |
cycle-b.ts  ------------------'

This is OK:
- ESM creates live bindings for the cycle.
- cycle-b does not call fromA during module initialization.
- test later calls fromA() -> fromB() + 1 -> 42.
```

```text
After false-positive hoist transform

cycle.test.ts
   |
   | static import { fromA }
   v
cycle-a.ts
   |
   | top-level await import("./cycle-b")
   | waits for cycle-b to evaluate
   v
cycle-b.ts
   |
   | static import { fromA } from "./cycle-a"
   | waits for cycle-a to evaluate
   v
cycle-a.ts

Deadlock:
cycle-a waits for cycle-b,
cycle-b waits for cycle-a.
```
