title: coverage-v8: uncovered .tsx files silently dropped because parseAstAsync defaults to lang: "js"
body:
### Describe the bug When `@vitest/coverage-v8` is enabled, every `.tsx` file matched by `coverage.include` that is NOT imported by any test is silently dropped from the report. The dropping is preceded by one `RolldownError: Parse failed` per file in stderr, but coverage exits successfully and produces a report, so the drop is easy to miss. Root cause: `V8CoverageProvider.getCoverageMapForUncoveredFiles` (in `packages/coverage-v8/src/provider.ts`) calls `this.remapCoverage(url, 0, sources, [])` for each uncovered file in the include set. `remapCoverage` does: ```ts ast = await parseAstAsync(result.code) ``` `parseAstAsync` is re-exported from rolldown, whose `defaultParserOptions` is `{ lang: "js", preserveParens: false }` (see `rolldown/dist/parse-ast-index.mjs:27`). The call does not pass a `lang` option or a filename, so rolldown parses every uncovered file as plain JavaScript. For `.tsx` files this fails at the first TypeScript or JSX construct, for example: - `interface Foo {` -> "Expected a semicolon or an implicit semicolon after a statement, but found none" - `import type { X } from "..."` -> "Expected `from` but found `{`" - `function F({ a }: Props) {}` -> "Expected `,` or `)` but found `:`" - `
...
` -> "Unexpected JSX expression" - `value as Foo` -> "Type assertion expressions can only be used in TypeScript files." The catch block in `remapCoverage` (`return {}` on parse failure) prevents the run from failing, so the user sees a coverage report that looks complete but has every uncovered `.tsx` file missing. In a Next.js project with ~20 untested components this means component coverage is entirely unmeasurable, with no indication beyond stderr noise. The covered (test-imported) path works because by the time `remapCoverage` sees those files their `result.code` has already been transformed to plain JS by Vite. The uncovered path goes through `createUncoveredFileTransformer`, which either returns a transform result (if Vite can handle the extension) or `getSources` falls back to `readFile` of the raw source. With no JSX-aware Vite plugin configured, that raw source reaches rolldown. This is similar in shape to #9972 (TS files importing virtual modules) and #10321 (JSON files imported with `?import`), both of which were workarounded with `exclude`. But this one affects every uncovered `.tsx` file in a normal include glob, with no per-file workaround unless the user adds a global `**/*.tsx` exclude or sets up render tests for every component (which is what the workaround section below describes). Suggested fixes: 1. Pass the filename and a derived `lang` to `parseAstAsync`, e.g. `parseAstAsync(result.code, { lang: getLangFromFilename(filename) }, filename)` where `getLangFromFilename` returns `"tsx"` / `"ts"` / `"jsx"` / `"js"` from the extension. The result variable already carries the URL, and the lang hint is what rolldown needs. 2. Filter `uncoveredFiles` by extension before parsing, so files that Vite did not transform are skipped instead of throwing. Today's catch already silently drops them, so an explicit pre-filter would just remove the noise and keep current behavior. ### Reproduction Minimal reproduction: 1. Create a Vitest project with `coverage.provider: "v8"` and `coverage.include: ["src/**/*.tsx"]`. 2. Add a `.tsx` file under `src/` containing at least one TypeScript or JSX construct. 3. Do not import that file from any test. 4. Run `vitest run --coverage`. A real reproduction: ```ts // vitest.config.ts import { defineConfig } from "vitest/config"; export default defineConfig({ test: { environment: "happy-dom", include: ["src/**/*.test.ts"], coverage: { provider: "v8", include: ["src/**/*.tsx"], }, }, }); ``` ```tsx // src/Hello.tsx interface Props { name: string } export function Hello({ name }: Props) { return
{name}
; } ``` ```ts // src/sanity.test.ts import { expect, it } from "vitest"; it("works", () => expect(1).toBe(1)); ``` Run `vitest run --coverage`. Observed: `Failed to parse file:///.../src/Hello.tsx. Excluding it from coverage.` printed to stderr, and `src/Hello.tsx` is missing from the coverage report. Tested on `@vitest/coverage-v8@4.1.7` and `@vitest/coverage-v8@5.0.0-beta.3`. Both reproduce. The relevant code in `provider.js` is unchanged between the two: `parseAstAsync(result.code)` at line 133 in v4 and line 150 in v5. ### Expected behavior Either: - `.tsx` files are parsed with the correct lang so they appear in the coverage report at their real (likely 0%) coverage, or - `.tsx` files that cannot be transformed by Vite are silently skipped, with no stderr noise. Today's behavior, "every uncovered `.tsx` produces a multiline RolldownError stack trace AND is silently dropped from the report", is the worst of both. ### Workaround Either of: ```ts // Option A: Exclude tsx from coverage if you do not have component tests yet. coverage: { include: ["src/**/*.ts", "src/**/*.tsx"], exclude: ["src/components/**/*.tsx"], } ``` ```ts // Option B: Add render tests so every .tsx becomes a "covered" file and bypasses // the uncovered-file parse path. Requires a JSX-aware setup (@vitejs/plugin-react) // and @testing-library/react. ``` ### System info ``` @vitest/coverage-v8: 4.1.7 and 5.0.0-beta.3 (both reproduce) vitest: 4.1.7 and 5.0.0-beta.3 (both reproduce) vite: via vitest defaults node: v20+ OS: Windows 11 / Ubuntu / macOS (not OS-specific, repro on Windows) ```

title: maxConcurrency is not enforced across sibling describe blocks: concurrent tests pile up between beforeEach and afterEach
body:
### Describe the bug

In vitest 4, `maxConcurrency` does not bound the number of concurrent tests that are mid-lifecycle (between `beforeEach` and `afterEach`) *when the tests are split across sibling `describe` blocks.* Setups run far ahead of teardowns, so resources created per-test in `beforeEach` (in our real suite: one Postgres database + app instance per test) accumulate far beyond `maxConcurrency`.

This is a follow-up to #10097, which was fixed by #10179 (v5) and backported in #10384 (v4.1.7) (thank you @hi-ogawa!). That fix restores the bound within a single suite: a flat `describe.concurrent` now behaves correctly (it did not in 4.1.6). However, the fix gives each task branch an independent limiter, so sibling concurrent suites each receive their own full `maxConcurrency` budget and the totals multiply. With 5 sibling groups and `maxConcurrency: 5`, up to 25 tests are mid-lifecycle simultaneously.

I've created a repro. Basically we have 20 tests in 5 sibling `describe` groups under `describe.concurrent`, with `maxConcurrency: 5`. Each test creates a fake db in `beforeEach` and drops it in `afterEach`. Every db operation costs more the more databases are live (mimicking how a real database degrades under load). An `afterAll` asserts the live-database high-water mark stayed at or below 6. This is a contrived example, so if anyone has a better approach lmk. The point though is that there's definitely a regression in V4 causing real world consequences.

**Results:**

| Version                    | Flat (1 suite) | Grouped (5 sibling suites) |
| -------------------------- | -------------- | -------------------------- |
| 3.2.4                      | max 5 live     | max 5 live                 |
| 4.1.6                      | 20 live        | 20 live                    |
| 4.1.7 (with #10384)        | max 5 live     | 20 live                    |
| 5.0.0-beta.2 (with #10179) | max 5 live     | 20 live                    |

On the failing versions the suite fails with:

`AssertionError: live databases should be bounded by maxConcurrency: expected 20 to be less than or equal to 6` and wall time roughly doubles (~3.1s to ~6.5s) because the fake database's load-scaled operations make the pile-up cost real time. Flattening the groups (all 20 tests directly under one `describe.concurrent`) makes 4.1.7 and 5.0.0-beta.2 pass, so the sibling suites are required to reproduce.

**Why this happens**

- In vitest 3, a single shared limiter wrapped the entire test: `limitMaxConcurrency(() => runTest(c, runner))`. A test acquired one slot before its `beforeEach` and released it after its `afterEach`, so at most `maxConcurrency` tests could be mid-lifecycle at once, regardless of suite structure.
- #9653 changed what the shared limiter wraps: it now wraps each individual hook and body invocation separately. A test no longer holds a slot between its phases. After its `beforeEach` finishes, it sits "open" (resources allocated) without counting against any limit while other tests' hooks run.
- #10179/#10384 added a second limiter, but per branch: `runSuite` now creates a fresh `limitConcurrency(runner.config.maxConcurrency)` for each suite's children. Within one suite this restores the bound, but every sibling suite gets its own independent budget.

These per-branch limiters do not compose into a global bound. With N concurrent sibling suites, the effective limit on mid-lifecycle tests is roughly `maxConcurrency * N`, not `maxConcurrency`, which is why the flat repro passes on 4.1.7 while the grouped one allocates all 20 dbs at once.

For certain test suites this is a large performance regression. For example, our server suite went from 38s on vitest 3 to 89s on vitest 4 with identical configuration and identical per-test timings, purely from the resource contention caused by the pile-up. A fix likely needs the per-branch limiters to share a global budget, or a test to hold one slot for its full setup and teardown lifecycle as in v3.

### Reproduction

https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitest-dev-vitest-ruovhudo?file=package.json

Change v3 to v3 and vice versa in the package.json to see failures

title: V8 coverage intermittently reports uncovered TypeScript ranges in full-suite runs
body:
### Describe the bug

A full-suite V8 coverage run intermittently reports remapped TypeScript statement/function ranges as uncovered even though the focused spec covering the file reports no uncovered ranges.

The bad ranges are written to `coverage-final.json`. With `coverage.thresholds` set to `100`, this fails the run; with thresholds set to `0`, the same false zero-hit ranges can still appear but the command exits successfully.

This is not the expected implicit-`else` branch coverage behavior discussed in issues like #9447 / #9979. The bad map includes statement and function ranges for code that is exercised by the focused test, for example `isoDateTimeFor`, `nextGeneratedId`, the `config` destructuring inside `createTodoTxtTaskSource`, and the `resolveOne` method body.

### Reproduction

Public repo/tag: https://github.com/ClipboardHealth/groundcrew/tree/groundcrew%404.34.3

That tag currently contains `/* v8 ignore ... @preserve */` comments that work around this issue. Remove only the workaround comments, then run coverage repeatedly:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/ClipboardHealth/groundcrew.git
cd groundcrew
git checkout groundcrew@4.34.3
npm ci

perl -0pi -e 's/^\h*\/\* v8 ignore (?:else|next).*?full-suite V8 coverage remaps.*?\*\/\n//mg' src/lib/adapters/todo-txt/source.ts

# Focused test: source.ts is fully covered.
npx vitest run --coverage src/lib/adapters/todo-txt/source.test.ts
node -e 'const c=require("./test-output/vitest/coverage/coverage-final.json"); const k=Object.keys(c).find(k=>k.endsWith("/src/lib/adapters/todo-txt/source.ts")); const f=c[k]; const z=o=>Object.values(o).filter(v=>Array.isArray(v)?v.some(n=>n===0):v===0).length; console.log({s:z(f.s), f:z(f.f), b:z(f.b)});'

# Full suite: coverage-final.json intermittently reports false uncovered ranges.
for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
  npx vitest run --coverage --coverage.reporter=json --coverage.thresholds.lines=0 --coverage.thresholds.functions=0 --coverage.thresholds.statements=0 --coverage.thresholds.branches=0 >/tmp/vitest-json-0-$i.log 2>&1
  rc=$?
  node -e 'const c=require("./test-output/vitest/coverage/coverage-final.json"); const k=Object.keys(c).find(k=>k.endsWith("/src/lib/adapters/todo-txt/source.ts")); const f=c[k]; const z=o=>Object.values(o).filter(v=>Array.isArray(v)?v.some(n=>n===0):v===0).length; console.log(process.argv[1], {rc:Number(process.argv[2]), s:z(f.s), f:z(f.f), b:z(f.b)});' "$i" "$rc"
done
```

### Observed output

Focused `source.test.ts` run after removing the workaround comments:

```txt
{ s: 0, f: 0, b: 0 }
```

Five full-suite JSON coverage runs with thresholds set to `0`:

```txt
THRESHOLD 0
1 { rc: 0, s: 7, f: 1, b: 23 }
2 { rc: 0, s: 0, f: 0, b: 0 }
3 { rc: 0, s: 7, f: 1, b: 23 }
4 { rc: 0, s: 0, f: 0, b: 0 }
5 { rc: 0, s: 7, f: 1, b: 23 }
```

Five full-suite JSON coverage runs with thresholds set to `100`:

```txt
THRESHOLD 100
1 { rc: 0, s: 0, f: 0, b: 0 }
2 { rc: 0, s: 0, f: 0, b: 0 }
3 { rc: 1, s: 7, f: 1, b: 23 }
4 { rc: 0, s: 0, f: 0, b: 0 }
5 { rc: 1, s: 7, f: 1, b: 23 }
```

One failing `coverage-final.json` for `src/lib/adapters/todo-txt/source.ts` contained zero-hit statement ranges at these source lines:

```txt
160, 181, 182, 349, 477-480
```

The corresponding zero-hit function was:

```txt
isoDateTimeFor, declared at line 159
```

The normal terminal report for a failing threshold run showed:

```txt
source.ts        | 96.55 | 73.33 | 97.87 | 96.42 | ...82,349,477-480
```

### Expected behavior

Coverage for the same full-suite run should be deterministic. A full-suite run should not intermittently mark executed TypeScript ranges as uncovered when the focused test run for the same file reports no uncovered statement/function/branch ranges.

### Environment

```txt
vitest/4.1.8 darwin-arm64 node-v24.14.1
@vitest/coverage-v8 4.1.8
vite/8.0.16 darwin-arm64 node-v24.14.1
npm 11.11.0
macOS 26.5.1 arm64
```

title: Add a native option to derive `test.projects` from package-manager workspaces
body:
### Clear and concise description of the problem

As a developer using Vitest in a monorepo, I want `test.projects` to natively consume my package manager's workspaces (e.g. `projects: 'workspaces'`) so that I have one source of truth instead of either hardcoding a glob list that duplicates `workspaces` and drifts, or importing `package.json` to map it by hand.

### Suggested solution

We could let `test.projects` take a sentinel like `'workspaces'` (or `true`):

```ts
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    projects: 'workspaces', // or projects: true
  },
});
```

At startup, Vitest reads the `workspaces` field from `package.json`, resolves each pattern to its package directories, and registers them as projects.

### Alternative

Two workarounds exist today, both with drawbacks:

- Hardcode the globs — `projects: ['applications/*', 'libraries/*', ...]`. Simple, but duplicates the workspaces field; the two drift out of sync as workspaces are added or removed.
- Import the manifest — read `package.json` in the config and map workspaces into projects by hand. Keeps one source of truth, but pulls the manifest into the config and leaves you maintaining glue code.

Neither is terrible, but both make the config carry plumbing that the tool could own — a built-in resolver would just be the ergonomic default.

### Additional context

_No response_

I was about to suggest `pnpm update vite`, but apparently this doesn't work for our pattern of auto peer dependency install of vite. For now, the workaround I suggest is something more elaborate `pnpm add -D vite@8.0.16 && pnpm remove vite`.

Ideally `pnpm update vite` should work and that's what I was expecting, but it doesn't, so we should either revisit peer dep strategy or explicitly call out the vite update gotcha in documentation.

(Btw, `pnpm update some-dep` does work for normal transitive dependencies, so not working for our peer dependency setup may be package manager issue)

That said, to be clear, narrowing Vite dependency version range whenever upstream patch or vulnerability won't be an ergonomic process, so I don't expect that should be the solution.

title: "$TITLE"
body:
## Bug report

### Describe the bug

When running a vitest test file that uses both `mongodb-memory-server` (or similar stateful integration setup) and `supertest`, vitest reports `Test Files <N> failed` and prints a `Failed Suites 1` entry for the file — **even though every individual test in the file passes**.

The suite-level error is reported as:

```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'method')
  at router.handle (node_modules/express/lib/router/index.js:139:34)
  at app.handle (node_modules/express/lib/application.js:181:10)
  at app (node_modules/express/lib/express.js:39:9)
```

`express@4.22.2` line 139: `debug('dispatching %s %s', req.method, req.url)`. So `req` is `undefined` at the moment vitest's reporter tries to walk the request through express.

### Reproduction

- vitest 4.1.9
- @vitest/runner 4.1.9
- express 4.22.2
- mongodb-memory-server 11.2.0
- supertest 7.2.2
- mongodb-memory-server-core 11.2.0

Any test file that:

1. boots `mongodb-memory-server` in `beforeAll`,
2. mounts a real Express app via `app.use(...)`,
3. drives it through `supertest`'s `request(app)`,

…will fail in the suite teardown phase after every test has passed.

The exit code is `1` despite `Tests 460 passed (460)`.

### Steps to reproduce

A minimal repro would be a single integration test file:

```ts
import { MongoMemoryServer } from 'mongodb-memory-server';
import mongoose from 'mongoose';
import express from 'express';
import request from 'supertest';

let mongo;

beforeAll(async () => {
  mongo = await MongoMemoryServer.create();
  await mongoose.connect(mongo.getUri());
  const app = express();
  app.get('/health', (_req, res) => res.json({ ok: true }));
  (globalThis as any).__app = app; // any way to keep the app alive
});

it('passes', async () => {
  await request((globalThis as any).__app).get('/health').expect(200);
});
// no afterAll — leaving the connection alive is intentional to
// surface the failure mode.
```

Run `npx vitest run` — the test passes, but vitest prints `Failed Suites 1` and exits non-zero with the stack trace above.

### Expected

`Test Files 1 passed (1)` and exit code `0`, even when mongoose / mongodb-memory-server are not torn down.

### Actual

```
Test Files  1 failed (1)
Tests  1 passed (1)
Process exited with code 1
```

with the `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'method')` stack.

### Workarounds attempted (none worked)

1. Binding the Express app to a single `http.Server` and using `request(server)` instead of `request(app)` — no change.
2. Setting `pool: 'forks'` (each test file in its own process) — `poolOptions` was removed in vitest 4 so this config is invalid; manually spawning workers via `pool: 'forks'` is broken.
3. Calling `server.closeAllConnections?.()` in `afterAll` — no change.
4. Letting the teardown be a no-op so the runner handles it on process exit — no change.

### Notes

- The failure only appears for files that use a real Express app (i.e. `app.handle` exists); pure unit tests with no Express never surface it.
- The error is reported by the vitest reporter, not by the test runtime — the tests themselves have already resolved successfully.
- The issue is **purely cosmetic** in the sense that no test correctness is affected, but it forces CI to fail (exit 1) on every integration-test run.

### Reproduction log

```
$ npx vitest run --no-coverage src/test/integration/auth.integration.test.ts

 ✓ src/test/integration/auth.integration.test.ts > POST /api/v1/auth/register > creates a new account and returns a JWT pair 244ms
 ✓ src/test/integration/auth.integration.test.ts > POST /api/v1/auth/register > 400 when email is missing 11ms
 ... (12 more passing tests) ...

 Test Files  1 failed (1)
      Tests  14 passed (14)
   Start at  20:55:13
   Duration  3.86s

⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯ Failed Suites 1 ⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯⎯
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'method')
 ❯ router.handle node_modules/.pnpm/express@4.22.2/.../lib/router/index.js:139:34
 ❯ app.handle    node_modules/.pnpm/express@4.22.2/.../lib/application.js:181:10
 ❯ app           node_modules/.pnpm/express@4.22.2/.../lib/express.js:39:9
```
author: demiryasin95
maintainer_reply: This is expected behavior. It doesn’t matter that the error didn’t happen in a hook or a test body. Any error surfaced during the test run is reported. Resolve every error to have a 0 exit code. This is your code failing, not a Vitest bug.

title: `getSnapshotData` swallows the parse error, making snapshot failures impossible to debug
body:
### Describe the bug

In browser mode, when the page is served with a CSP that blocks `eval` (no `'unsafe-eval'`), external `.snap` files silently fail to load. The snapshot data ends up empty, which produces 1 failed snapshot and 1 obsolete snapshot. 

The `.snap` file parses fine in Node. The actual cause is never reported.

**NOTE** This happens only when `CI=true` is set, which is the default in GitHub Actions. There is no error in non-CI mode, which makes this even more confusing to debug.

## Why

`getSnapshotData` parses `.snap` files with `new Function("exports", contents)`, which CSP blocks. The resulting error is thrown away:

```js
// @vitest/snapshot/dist/index.js
try {
  snapshotContents = content;
  const populate = new Function("exports", snapshotContents);
  populate(data);
} catch {} // <- error discarded, data stays empty
```

With the `catch {}` in place there's nothing in the logs pointing at CSP/eval. Adding a `console.log(err)` there immediately surfaces the real error.


## Proposed solution
The `catch {}` should be removed, or at least the error should be logged. This would make snapshot failures in browser mode much easier to debug.

https://github.com/vojty/vitest-browser-snapshot-error

title: Vitest 4 is ignoring "v8 ignore file" comment specifically
body:
### Describe the bug

Upgarding to vitest 8 + vite 4 revealed an issue: our files that has `/* v8 ignore file -- @preserve */` at the very top of the file are now included in the code coverage report. Reverting the upgrade resolves the issue.

Unlike a [similar closed issue](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues/9881), the following ignore hints **all work as expected**:

- `/* v8 ignore next -- @preserve */` ✅ 
- `/* v8 ignore start -- @preserve */` ✅ 
- `/* v8 ignore stop -- @preserve */` ✅ 
- `/* v8 ignore if -- @preserve */` ✅ 
- `/* v8 ignore else -- @preserve */` ✅ 

🔴 **It is only `/* v8 ignore file -- @preserve */` that stops working after upgrading to vitest 4.**

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Use of AI disclaimer: due to the need to understand the inner workings of vite/vitest in order to come up with a diagnosis, I have used Claude Code to help debug the issue on my behalf. It has verified its findings on our monorepo, and I have attached its full report in the reproduction step below.

### Reproduction

TL;DR: `/* v8 ignore file */` is ignored when the directive sits above a type-only import

**The minimal reproduction in the form of a GitHub repo is available here: https://github.com/terrymun/v8-ignore-file-diagnosis**

***

#### Summary

After upgrading to Vite 8, the file-level coverage directive `/* v8 ignore file -- @preserve */` stops working for any
file whose **first import is a type-only import** (`import type { … }` / `export type { … } from …`). The file is still
included in the V8 coverage report.

The line-range directives (`/* v8 ignore start */` … `/* v8 ignore stop */`) are **not** affected and continue to work
in the same files.

The root cause is an interaction between two things:

1. Vite 8 transforms TypeScript with **oxc**, which **elides type-only imports** during transform. When the
   `v8 ignore file` comment is the leading comment attached to an elided `import type` statement, the comment is dropped
   together with that statement.
2. `ast-v8-to-istanbul` (used by `@vitest/coverage-v8` v4) detects the **file**-level directive by scanning the
   **transformed** code, whereas it detects **start/stop** directives from the **original** source via the sourcemap. So
   once the comment is stripped from the transformed output, the file directive is silently lost — but start/stop keeps
   working.

#### Environment

| Package               | Version                                     |
| --------------------- | ------------------------------------------- |
| `vite`                | `8.0.16`                                    |
| `vitest`              | `4.1.9`                                     |
| `@vitest/coverage-v8` | `4.1.9`                                     |
| `ast-v8-to-istanbul`  | `1.0.4` (resolved by `@vitest/coverage-v8`) |
| `node`                | `v24.16.0`                                  |

#### Minimal reproduction

```
v8-ignore-file-repro/
├─ package.json
├─ vitest.config.ts
└─ src/
   ├─ broken.ts      # directive above a type-only import → STILL COUNTED (bug)
   ├─ works.ts       # directive above a value import     → excluded (correct)
   ├─ types.ts
   ├─ value.ts
   └─ repro.test.ts
```

**`package.json`**

```json
{
  "name": "v8-ignore-file-repro",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": { "test": "vitest run --coverage" },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@vitest/coverage-v8": "4.1.9",
    "vite": "8.0.16",
    "vitest": "4.1.9"
  }
}
```

**`vitest.config.ts`**

```ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config';

export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    coverage: {
      provider: 'v8',
      include: ['src/**/*.ts'],
      reporter: ['json', 'text'],
      all: true,
    },
  },
});
```

**`src/broken.ts`** — directive above a **type-only** import (bug):

```ts
/* v8 ignore file -- @preserve */
import type { Foo } from './types';
import { value } from './value';

export const broken = (x: number): Foo | string => (x > 0 ? value('a') : 'b');
```

**`src/works.ts`** — directive above a **value** import (works):

```ts
/* v8 ignore file -- @preserve */
import { value } from './value';
import type { Foo } from './types';

export const works = (x: number): Foo | string => (x > 0 ? value('a') : 'b');
```

**`src/types.ts`**

```ts
export type Foo = { a: number };
```

**`src/value.ts`**

```ts
export const value = (s: string) => s.toUpperCase();
```

**`src/repro.test.ts`**

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest';
import { broken } from './broken';
import { works } from './works';

test('both run', () => {
  expect(broken(1)).toBe('A');
  expect(works(1)).toBe('A');
});
```

#### Expected vs. actual

Both `broken.ts` and `works.ts` carry `/* v8 ignore file -- @preserve */`, so **neither** should appear in the coverage
report.

**Actual** — `broken.ts` is reported, `works.ts` is correctly excluded:

```
 % Coverage report from v8
-----------|---------|----------|---------|---------|-------------------
File       | % Stmts | % Branch | % Funcs | % Lines | Uncovered Line #s
-----------|---------|----------|---------|---------|-------------------
All files  |     100 |       50 |     100 |     100 |
 broken.ts |     100 |       50 |     100 |     100 | 5
-----------|---------|----------|---------|---------|-------------------
```

The only difference between the two files is the **order** of the type-only import relative to the value import.

#### Diagnosis

##### 1. Vite 8 / oxc strips the comment along with the elided `import type`

Inspecting the transform output that the coverage provider feeds to `ast-v8-to-istanbul`:

```js
import { createServer } from 'vite';

const server = await createServer({
  configFile: false,
  server: { middlewareMode: true },
  optimizeDeps: { noDiscovery: true },
});

for (const f of ['broken.ts', 'works.ts']) {
  const r = await server.transformRequest(`/src/${f}`, { ssr: true });
  console.log(`${f}:`);
  console.log('  comment in TRANSFORMED code:        ', r.code.includes('ignore file'));
  console.log('  comment in sourcemap.sourcesContent:', !!r.map?.sourcesContent?.[0]?.includes('ignore file'));
}

await server.close();
```

Output:

```
broken.ts:
  comment in TRANSFORMED code:         false   ← stripped
  comment in sourcemap.sourcesContent: true
works.ts:
  comment in TRANSFORMED code:         true
  comment in sourcemap.sourcesContent: true
```

In `broken.ts`, oxc elides `import type { Foo } from './types'` (its only purpose is types), and the leading
`/* v8 ignore file -- @preserve */` comment is attached to that statement, so it is removed with it. `@preserve` does
not help — the entire statement (and its leading comments) is gone before codegen. In `works.ts`, the leading comment is
attached to the surviving value import, so it stays.

##### 2. `ast-v8-to-istanbul` reads the file directive from transformed code, but start/stop from source

In `ast-v8-to-istanbul/dist/index.mjs`:

```js
// File-level directive — scans the TRANSFORMED code (`e.code`)
async function convert(e) {
  let t = getIgnoreHints(e.code);
  if (t.length === 1 && t[0].type === 'file') return {}; // whole-file skip
  // …
}
```

`getIgnoreHints()` tokenizes `e.code` (the transformed module) with `js-tokens` and looks for the `file` hint in the
comment tokens. Because the comment is no longer present in the transformed code, the hint is never found and the
whole-file skip never triggers.

By contrast, the start/stop path resolves ignored lines from the **original** source obtained via the sourcemap
(`sourceContentFor`) or the file on disk:

```js
// inside Locator.getLoc — start/stop path
f = getIgnoredLines(c(this.#n, d) ?? tryReadFileSync(d));
```

Since `sourcesContent` still contains the original comment (see output above), start/stop directives keep working
regardless of what the transform did to the emitted code. This asymmetry is why start/stop survives the Vite 8 upgrade
and `file` does not.

#### Why this is a regression in Vite 8 specifically

The comment survival depends on the transformer. A bare `transformWithOxc` / `transformWithEsbuild` call with default
options keeps the comment, but Vite 8's resolved config sets `esbuild.legalComments: "none"` and routes TS through the
`vite:oxc` plugin, under which the leading comment on an **elided** type-only import is dropped. The same source under
the previous esbuild-based pipeline retained the directive.

#### Suggested fix (for maintainers)

Make the file-level directive detection consistent with start/stop by reading from the **original source** (sourcemap
`sourcesContent` / on-disk file) instead of the transformed code. The original source reliably contains the comment in
all cases shown above. Alternatively, oxc could preserve leading comments when eliding a type-only import, but resolving
it in `ast-v8-to-istanbul` (where start/stop is already handled correctly from source) seems like the more targeted fix.

#### Workarounds (until fixed)

Any of these keep the comment in the transformed output:

- Place `/* v8 ignore file -- @preserve */` **below** the import block, directly above the first runtime statement.
- Ensure the **first** import after the directive is a value import, not `import type`.
- Use `/* v8 ignore start -- @preserve */` (with no `stop`, or wrapping the whole body) instead of `v8 ignore file`,
  since the start/stop path is unaffected.

title: expect(null | undefined).toHaveProperty() throws an internal TypeError instead of a clean matcher error
body:
### Description
When the received value is `null` or `undefined`, `toHaveProperty` crashes with a raw internal error rather than failing the assertion cleanly (or, for the negated form, passing). `.not.toHaveProperty` also crashes, when under vitest's chai-based semantics it should pass on a nullish subject.

### Steps to reproduce
```ts
expect(null).toHaveProperty('x')        // throws
expect(null).not.toHaveProperty('x')    // throws (should pass)
expect(undefined).toHaveProperty('x')   // throws
```
Observed: every call throws `TypeError: Cannot convert undefined or null to object`. Expected: a proper matcher error / assertion failure (jest emits a clean matcher error here).

### Root cause
`packages/expect/src/jest-expect.ts` -- the `getValue()` helper calls `Object.hasOwn(actual, propertyName)` unconditionally, before the null-safe `utils.getPathInfo(actual, propertyName)` fallback. `Object.hasOwn(null, ...)` throws; `actual` is never guarded for nullish.

### Suggested fix
Guard the subject before the own-property check: `const hasOwn = actual != null && Object.hasOwn(actual, propertyName)`, which lets the null-safe `getPathInfo` fallback run (fails cleanly, `.not` passes) — or throw a jest-style matcher error when `actual == null`.
author: tsushanth
maintainer_reply: I would expect it to throw something like `expected to receive a valid object, instead got null`. `expect(null).not.toHaveProperty('some')` doesn't make sense semanticaly, there should be `expect(null).toBeDefined()` before this call in my opinion.

title: Support filename extension that sorts after `.ts`
body:
### Clear and concise description of the problem

Currently vitest automatically treats the `.test.` and `.spec.` (infix) file-extensions as test files.
The unfortunate side effect is that this sorts test files *before* typescript (ts, tsx) files in practically all interfaces.
Such as with diffs (both git CLI and web-forges such as github, gitlab).

- my-component.test.tsx
- my-component.tsx
- module.test.ts
- module.ts

This has a real impact on the UX for authoring and reviewing code.
Code reviewers on online platforms by default see test suite files before seeing implementation files.
Meanwhile only in a TDD oriented workplace does such test-first mindset actually align with how teams operate in practice.

### Suggested solution

Besides `.spec.` and `.test.`, support another infix out of the box that will let the alphabetical file order place test files after modules.

### Alternative

Currently the primary workaround would be to use separate directories to organise the test files under, but this does not help with the file ordering because such a directory (`__tests__`) is put before modules.

title: `.css?raw` imports resolve to an empty string under the default `test.css: false`
body:
### Describe the bug

A `?raw` import of a CSS file resolves to an **empty string** under Vitest's default configuration, while the same file imported with a non-CSS extension returns its source text as expected:

```ts
import cssRaw from "./tokens.css?raw"; // ""  ← empty string
import txtRaw from "./tokens.txt?raw"; // ":root {\n  --brand: #315fc3;\n..." (same file, copied)
```

`?raw` asks for the file's source text, not a processed CSS module, so I'd expect it to bypass CSS handling entirely (Vite serves it fine at dev/build time — this only breaks inside Vitest).

This bites hardest in tests that *assert on* CSS source (design-token parity checks and the like): a set/regex extraction over an empty string yields an empty result, so equality-style assertions pass **vacuously** and the test silently stops guarding anything. That's how we found it — a supposedly green token-parity test in our app had been comparing two empty sets.

**Where it happens** (`packages/vitest/src/node/plugins/cssEnabler.ts`): `cssLangRE` is `\.(?:css|less|sass|scss|styl|stylus|pcss|postcss)(?:$|\?)`, which matches `tokens.css?raw`. With CSS processing disabled (the default), the `vitest:css-disable` pre-transform returns `{ code: "" }` and `vitest:css-empty-post` then emits `export default ""` — before Vite's built-in `?raw` handling can serve the source. The plugin already special-cases `?inline` (`cssInlineRE`) but has no `?raw` awareness; a `[?&]raw(?:&|$)` early-return in both transforms (or in `isCSS`) would let Vite's raw asset pipeline handle it.

**Workaround:** `test: { css: true }` restores correct `?raw` behavior (or read the file with `fs` instead).

Reproduced identically on vitest **3.2.4**, **4.1.9**, and **4.1.10**, so it's long-standing default-config behavior rather than a v4 regression.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/erenozen/vitest-css-raw-repro

```bash
npm install
npx vitest run
# ✓ ?raw returns the file source for .txt
# ✗ ?raw returns the file source for .css   (cssRaw === "")
```

Three files: a `tokens.css`, a byte-identical `tokens.txt` copy, and a two-assertion test. No config (node environment); adding `test: { css: true }` makes both pass.

### System Info

```
System:
  OS: Linux 6.6 Ubuntu 26.04 LTS (WSL2)
  CPU: (32) x64 AMD RYZEN AI MAX+ 395 w/ Radeon 8060S
Binaries:
  Node: 24.18.0
  npm: 11.16.0
  pnpm: 11.9.0
npmPackages:
  vitest: 4.1.10 (also reproduced on 3.2.4 and 4.1.9)
```

npm

title: jsdom: localStorage/sessionStorage dropped by getWindowKeys on Node 25+ (follow-up to #8757)
body:
Follow-up to #8757, which was closed with "This looks like a bug of Node 25 […]
non-LTS is not officially supported by Vitest". Two things have changed since,
and I think they justify a second look:

1. **The Node-side issue it pointed at, nodejs/node#60303, is now closed as
   completed** (2026-01-22) — and the Vitest symptom persists unchanged on
   Node 26.3.0. So "wait for Node" has played out and did not resolve it.
2. **Node 24 is LTS and 26 is current**, so the non-LTS argument has expired.
   Every project that moves to a supported modern Node hits this.

I also think the original attribution was incomplete. Node's behaviour here is
legitimate; the reason jsdom's `Storage` never reaches the test is a specific
choice in Vitest's own key-copying.

### Mechanism

`getWindowKeys` in `packages/vitest/src/integrations/env/utils.ts`:

```js
return new Set(keysArray.concat(Object.getOwnPropertyNames(win)).filter((k) => {
  if (skipKeys.includes(k)) return false;
  if (k in global) return keysArray.includes(k);   // <-- here
  return true;
}));
```

A key already present on `globalThis` is only copied if it is in the allowlist.
Node 25+ ships `localStorage`/`sessionStorage` as configurable accessors, so
`'localStorage' in globalThis` is `true` — and neither key is in `LIVING_KEYS`
or `OTHER_KEYS`. The jsdom window's `Storage` is therefore filtered out, and
`window.localStorage` ends up `undefined`.

Verified against the installed `vitest@4.1.10` bundle:

```
LIVING_KEYS | localStorage: false | sessionStorage: false
OTHER_KEYS  | localStorage: false | sessionStorage: false
skipKeys    | localStorage: false | sessionStorage: false
```

```
$ node -v
v26.3.0
$ node -e "console.log('in globalThis:', 'localStorage' in globalThis, '| typeof:', typeof globalThis.localStorage)"
in globalThis: true | typeof: undefined
```

jsdom itself is fine — a directly constructed window round-trips:

```
$ node --input-type=module -e "
import { JSDOM } from 'jsdom'
const d = new JSDOM('', { url: 'http://localhost:3000/' })
d.window.localStorage.setItem('a','b')
console.log(typeof d.window.localStorage, d.window.localStorage.getItem('a'))
"
object b
```

### Reproduction

```ts
// probe.test.ts
// @vitest-environment jsdom
import { expect, it } from 'vitest'

it('has localStorage', () => {
  expect(typeof window.localStorage).toBe('object') // "undefined"
})
```

### Suggested fix

Add both keys to `OTHER_KEYS`, so the `k in global` branch returns `true`:

```diff
   'length',
+  'localStorage',
+  'sessionStorage',
```

### Why this is worth fixing rather than documenting

There is no error and no warning from Vitest — only `undefined`. The failure
surfaces wherever a test first dereferences storage, which is usually a
`beforeEach`, so it reads as a broken test. In our case two suites were dead for
weeks and the resulting failures were written off as pre-existing before anyone
traced them here.

### Workaround, for anyone landing here

`--no-webstorage` drops Node's global so jsdom's copy lands normally. It has to
be version-guarded: Node 22 rejects the flag outright with `bad option`, and
does not need it (Web Storage is not enabled there).

```ts
// vite.config.ts / vitest.config.ts
test: {
  execArgv:
    Number(process.versions.node.split('.')[0]) >= 25
      ? ['--no-webstorage']
      : [],
}
```

### Version

vitest 4.1.10 · jsdom 30.0.1 · Node 26.3.0

title: Bare setupFiles specifiers resolve against the project root's PARENT directory (paths:[root] lacks trailing slash) -- wrong node_modules wins in git worktrees
body:
### Describe the bug

`resolvePath` in config resolution resolves bare `setupFiles` / `globalSetup` specifiers against the **parent directory** of the project root instead of the root itself, because it passes the root without a trailing slash as a URL base:

```js
// dist/chunks/coverage.*.js (vitest 3.2.7)
function resolvePath(path, root) {
	return normalize(resolveModule(path, { paths: [root] }) ?? resolve(root, path));
}
```

`resolveModule` (local-pkg) only uses `require.resolve` under Yarn PnP; on a plain npm install it falls through to mlly's `resolvePathSync(path, { url: options.paths })`. mlly/Node URL-base semantics treat `/path/to/project` (no trailing slash) as a *file* URL whose parent `/path/to/` is the resolution base, so `node_modules` lookup starts one level above the project and walks up from there.

Normally this is invisible because the walk-up still finds the project's own `node_modules`. It breaks whenever an **ancestor directory has its own `node_modules` containing the same package** -- the ancestor's copy wins. Concrete case: a git worktree checked out inside the main repo (e.g. `repo/.claude/worktrees/wt/`). With `@storybook/addon-vitest`'s injected bare setup file (`@storybook/addon-vitest/internal/setup-file`), the specifier resolves into the **main checkout's** `node_modules`, which is outside the worktree project root, so the browser server refuses to serve it and every browser-mode test file fails with:

```
Error: Failed to import test file /path/to/MAIN-CHECKOUT/node_modules/@storybook/addon-vitest/dist/vitest-plugin/setup-file.js
Caused by: TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: http://localhost:63315/...
```

### Reproduction

1. `repo/` with vitest 3.2.7 + `@storybook/addon-vitest` (browser mode project) installed, `npm install` run.
2. `git worktree add repo/.worktrees/wt && cd repo/.worktrees/wt && npm install` (worktree has its own complete `node_modules`).
3. `npx vitest run --project storybook` inside the worktree.
4. Every test file fails at import; the logged setup-file path points at `repo/node_modules/...`, not `repo/.worktrees/wt/node_modules/...`.

Minimal form without storybook: any `test.setupFiles: ['some-pkg/setup']` bare specifier in a project that has an ancestor directory with `node_modules` containing `some-pkg`.

### Expected behavior

Bare specifiers in `setupFiles`/`globalSetup` resolve against the project root's own `node_modules` first (standard Node resolution from `root`), regardless of what ancestor directories contain.

### Suggested fix

Pass the root with a trailing slash (or as a directory URL) so the root itself is the resolution base:

```js
resolveModule(path, { paths: [root.endsWith('/') ? root : root + '/'] })
```

Verified locally: with the trailing slash added in the dist chunk, the full storybook browser-mode project passes inside the worktree (84 story files / 849 tests, previously 84/84 failing at import).

### System Info

vitest 3.2.7, @storybook/addon-vitest 10.x, macOS (darwin 25.5), Node 22, npm (no PnP). Downstream workaround we ship: a post-enforce Vite plugin that rewrites bare `setupFiles` entries to absolute paths via `createRequire(import.meta.url).resolve(...)` before vitest's resolvePath sees them.

A promise that rejects and gets a handler one microtask later is reported as an unhandled rejection when tests run in the workers pool. Every test passes and the run still exits 1.

The same file under the default node pool exits 0 and reports nothing.

### Reproduction

`probe.test.ts`:

```ts

  const promise = Promise.reject(new Error('handled late'))
  queueMicrotask(() => {
    promise.catch(() => {})
```

author: rexxars
maintainer_reply:
I present to you some slop from Fable (I did read it, but didn't verify because I want to sleep):

This is a workerd bug (already fixed upstream behind a compatibility flag), not a Vitest one.

## What happens

Your repro rejects a promise and attaches `.catch` one microtask later, in the same macrotask turn. Whether that counts as "unhandled" depends on when the runtime checks:

- **Node** runs its pending-rejection check only after the current turn's microtask queue fully drains. The `.catch` inside `queueMicrotask` runs during that drain, so the promise is removed from the pending list before anything is emitted. Neither `unhandledRejection` nor `rejectionHandled` fires. That is why the default pool exits 0.
- **Browsers** behave the same way per the HTML spec: attaching a handler removes the promise from the "about-to-be-notified" list, so no event fires.
- **workerd** at compatibility dates before **2026-03-03** schedules its check as a microtask enqueued *at rejection time*, so it runs before your `queueMicrotask` callback. It fires `unhandledrejection`, and then `rejectionhandled` once the handler attaches. I verified this with a raw miniflare probe (plain `addEventListener`, no Vitest involved): the event order is `unhandledrejection` → catch attaches → `rejectionhandled`.

Workerd classified this eagerness as a bug ([cloudflare/workerd#6020](https://github.com/cloudflare/workerd/issues/6020)) and fixed it in [cloudflare/workerd#6049](https://github.com/cloudflare/workerd/pull/6049) (Feb 2026) by deferring the check until the microtask checkpoint completes. The fix is gated behind the `unhandled_rejection_after_microtask_checkpoint` compat flag, default-on from compat date `2026-03-03`. Your config pins `compatibilityDate: '2024-11-11'`, so you get the legacy timing even though the installed workerd binary already contains the fix.

Vitest itself has no rejection-timing heuristics: it subscribes to the runtime's `unhandledRejection` notification and reports it. There is no retraction on `rejectionHandled`, intentionally: in Node, an emitted `unhandledRejection` with a handler attached a turn later is a real finding (`--unhandled-rejections=strict` crashes on it), so retracting would silently weaken the check for the pools where the runtime's timing is correct.

## How to fix it on your side

Either of these makes your repro pass:

- Set `compatibilityDate` to `2026-03-03` or later, or keep your date and add the flag:

  ```ts
  cloudflareTest({
    miniflare: {
      compatibilityDate: '2024-11-11',
      compatibilityFlags: ['unhandled_rejection_after_microtask_checkpoint'],
    },
  })
  ```

- Or filter these reports with the [`onUnhandledError`](https://vitest.dev/config/onunhandlederror) config option (returning `false` suppresses both the banner and the exit code).

Closing as an upstream runtime behavior. If you hit rejections that stay unhandled under the new flag too, that would be worth reporting to [cloudflare/workers-sdk](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk) (see also cloudflare/workers-sdk#14736 for an adjacent known issue with DO RPC rejections).

title: Coverage: a file’s statement map depends on which project reports it, so merged reports show an uncoverable statement
body:
### Describe the bug

_Disclosure: Claim supported by Claude Opus_

### Summary

When two projects use different environments, `@vitest/coverage-v8` builds two
different statement maps for the same untested source file. A project with
`environment: "jsdom"` emits an extra statement for an `import` from a `node:`
builtin. A project with `environment: "node"` does not.

A single run hides this, because a real test covers the file and no map is
synthesised. `--merge-reports` exposes it. The merge unions a real map that has
no statement at line 1 against a synthetic map that has one at zero hits. The
result is a statement that no run can ever cover.

A file that is fully covered then reports 50% in the example below.

**This is not #9366.** That issue reports *duplicate* statements, where the
start positions agree and the end columns disagree. Here the *start* positions
disagree, and the end columns are `null` in both projects. The counts also move
in opposite directions: #9366 inflates the total, this deflates it. A maintainer
also noted that #9366 needs SWC to reproduce, and this reproduction uses plain
Vite and Vitest with no plugins. See "Relationship to existing issues" below.

### Impact

The effect is small per file but permanent. A file reported at 50% here is at
100%. In a larger codebase the pattern repeats on every source file that imports
a `node:` builtin and is not covered inside the jsdom project. Any per-file
coverage ratchet then compares a true figure against a depressed one, and the
figure never recovers, because no test can cover the added statement.

### What we have not determined

We report only what we measured. We did not inspect the transform output, so we
cannot say at which stage the extra statement is introduced. We also did not
test environments other than `jsdom` and `node`, or providers other than `v8`.

### Relationship to existing issues

We searched the tracker and the discussions before filing. The closest match is
**#9366**, which is open. This report is a different defect, and the two are
easy to tell apart by the `end.column` values.

**#9366** — one file is covered by *two* projects. The statement start positions
agree, but the end columns disagree (`null` against a number), so the merge
keeps both copies and the statement count is inflated.

**This report** — one file is covered by *one* project, and a second project
synthesises it because it never loads it. The two maps disagree on the *start*
positions, so the merge adds a statement that has no counterpart.



### Reproduction

### Repository

[dextermb/vitest-reproduction-coverage-statement-map](https://github.com/dextermb/vitest-reproduction-coverage-statement-map) contains a minimal reproduction environment.


### Commands

```bash
# 1. Baseline: one run, both projects.
vitest run --coverage

# 2. The same work, split per project, then merged.
vitest run --project client --coverage --reporter=blob --outputFile.blob=.vitest-reports/client.json
vitest run --project node   --coverage --reporter=blob --outputFile.blob=.vitest-reports/node.json
vitest run --merge-reports=.vitest-reports --coverage
```

### Evidence

#### Expected — step 1, a single run

```
Statements   : 100% ( 2/2 )
Lines        : 100% ( 2/2 )
```

The statement map for `src/uses-node-builtin.ts` holds one statement:

```
4:2 = 1 hit
```

#### Actual — step 2, the same tests, merged

```
Statements   : 66.66% ( 2/3 )
Lines        : 66.66% ( 2/3 )

File                  | % Stmts | % Lines | Uncovered Line #s
 ...ode-builtin.ts    |      50 |      50 | 1
```

The merged statement map holds two statements:

```
1:9 = 0 hits     <-- added by the merge, and not coverable
4:2 = 1 hit
```

No test changed between the two runs. The same tests ran, and the same code
executed.

#### The two maps, side by side

Each project was asked to report the file on its own. The maps disagree:

```
src/uses-node-builtin.ts, as each project reports it

  client (jsdom)   1:9  4:2      <-- the import is a statement
  node   (node)         4:2
```

Statement `1:9` is the `randomUUID` binding of
`import { randomUUID } from "node:crypto";`.

The `node` project is the project that actually covers the file, so its map is
the real one. The `client` project never loads the file, so its map is
synthesised from source. The merge keeps the union, and nothing can raise
`1:9` above zero.

maintainer_reply:
It's caused by this quite aggressive global override 😠 

https://github.com/lerna-lite/lerna-lite/blob/db2a8f3026d0b0f8d676d1452c1baca1675285b9/vitest/silence-logging.ts#L17-L19

Your override should handle the callback argument too so that it would not hang here:

https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/9e116fb52a9f6d438d7ba8e7adea4fb2d27e3a71/packages/vitest/src/runtime/workers/init.ts#L61-L64

```diff
// Aggressively silence all output at the process level
-process.stdout.write = (() => true) as any;
+process.stdout.write = ((text, callback) => { callback?.(); return true }) as any;
```

title: vm pools: `prewarmModuleGraph` transforms subtrees that `vi.mock(..., factory)` replaces
body:
### Describe the bug

Was benchmarking 5.0.0-rc.2 on a large, fairly mock-heavy suite and it came out noticeably slower cold than 4.1 despite #10744 (roughly 1.4× wall on a full cold run, ~2× on a single-process shard). Tracked it down to the prewarm from #10708/#10744: `prewarmModuleGraph` walks every `importedModules` edge server-side and transforms whatever it hits. It doesn't know about the test file's hoisted `vi.mock(specifier, factory)` calls, so a factory-mocked module's *real* implementation and its whole static subtree still get transformed — stuff the on-demand fetch in 4.x (and `forks`/`threads` in 5.0) never touches because the mock intercepts first.

It's purely wasted main-thread transform work + GC + fsModuleCache churn, and it scales with how much a suite mocks — for us it about doubled the number of modules transformed per run, and the main-thread profile is dominated by vite transform + GC accordingly.

Looking into pruning the factory-mocked edges when walking from a test file. Will send a PR if I can get it working.

### Reproduction

Excuse the LLM bash... Couldn't make a gist for some reason (github having issues)

```sh
mkdir prewarm-repro && cd prewarm-repro && npm init -y >/dev/null && npm pkg set type=module && npm i -D vitest@5.0.0-rc.2
mkdir -p heavy && for i in $(seq 50); do echo "export const v$i = $i" > heavy/leaf$i.js; done
seq 50 | sed 's/.*/export * from ".\/leaf&.js"/' > heavy/index.js
echo 'import * as heavy from "./heavy/index.js"; export const count = () => Object.keys(heavy).length' > consumer.js
cat > consumer.test.js <<'JS'
import { expect, test, vi } from 'vitest'
import { count } from './consumer.js'

// the real ./heavy subtree (51 modules) is never loaded: the factory replaces it
vi.mock('./heavy/index.js', () => ({ a: 1 }))

test('uses the mock', () => {
  expect(count()).toBe(1)
})
JS
for pool in forks vmThreads vmForks; do
  rm -rf .cache
  npx vitest run --pool=$pool --fsModuleCache --fsModuleCachePath=.cache > /dev/null
  echo "$pool: $(ls .cache | wc -l) modules transformed"
done
```

```
forks: 3 modules transformed
vmThreads: 69 modules transformed
vmForks: 69 modules transformed
```

`forks` transforms the test, `consumer.js` and the mocked `heavy/index.js` entry. The vm pools additionally transform all 50 `heavy/leaf*.js` (plus ~15 of vitest's own inlined runtime chunks, which is expected for vm pools) — the leaves are pure overhead, nothing ever evaluates them. 4.1.10 transforms 2–3 modules here on every pool.

title: coverage-v8: RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded when merged coverage contains duplicate identical ranges
body:
### Describe the bug

Vitest v8 coverage report generation crashes with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` when the collected V8 coverage of a file contains a function whose ranges include **two identical ranges plus a zero-length range**, e.g.:

```js
ranges: [
  { startOffset: 0,  endOffset: 10, count: 1 },
  { startOffset: 0,  endOffset: 10, count: 1 }, // identical duplicate
  { startOffset: 10, endOffset: 10, count: 0 }, // zero-length range
]
```

`@vitest/coverage-v8` merges per-worker coverages with `mergeProcessCovs()` from `@bcoe/v8-coverage@1.0.2`. With such an entry present twice (i.e. ≥2 test files loading the same module), `mergeRangeTreeChildren` recurses without bound:

<details><summary>Stack trace</summary>

```
⎯⎯⎯⎯ Unhandled Error ⎯⎯⎯⎯
RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded.
 ❯ mergeRangeTreeChildren node_modules/@bcoe/v8-coverage/src/lib/merge.js:278:42
 ❯ mergeRangeTrees node_modules/@bcoe/v8-coverage/src/lib/merge.js:177:19
 ❯ nextChild node_modules/@bcoe/v8-coverage/src/lib/merge.js:346:9
 ❯ mergeRangeTreeChildren node_modules/@bcoe/v8-coverage/src/lib/merge.js:314:16
 ❯ mergeRangeTrees node_modules/@bcoe/v8-coverage/src/lib/merge.js:177:19
 ...
 ❯ readCoverageFiles node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/coverage.*.js:762:18
 ❯ generateCoverage node_modules/@vitest/coverage-v8/dist/provider.js:32:13
```

</details>

Minimal standalone reproduction (no Vitest involved, crashes on plain Node):

```js
import { mergeProcessCovs } from '@bcoe/v8-coverage'

const makeScriptCov = () => ({
  scriptId: '0',
  url: 'file:///src/relations.ts',
  functions: [{
    functionName: '',
    isBlockCoverage: true,
    ranges: [
      { startOffset: 0, endOffset: 10, count: 1 },
      { startOffset: 0, endOffset: 10, count: 1 },
      { startOffset: 10, endOffset: 10, count: 0 },
    ],
  }],
})

mergeProcessCovs([{ result: [makeScriptCov()] }, { result: [makeScriptCov()] }])
// RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded
```

Removing either the duplicate range or the zero-length range makes the merge succeed, so both are required to trigger it.

**Real-world trigger:** a project using drizzle-orm `defineRelations` (`drizzle-orm@1.0.0-rc.4`) where two test files import the relations module — the per-worker V8 entries for that file contain exactly the duplicate + zero-length pattern above, and `vitest run --coverage` crashes during report generation.

**Runtime note:** whether the *end-to-end* Vitest crash triggers depends on the engine's stack limit — it reproduces reliably under Bun (JavaScriptCore), while Node's larger default stack happens to absorb the deep recursion for this input. The underlying merge-algorithm bug is deterministic and always crashes via the standalone snippet above.

If it helps, I'm happy to open a PR against `@bcoe/v8-coverage` (de-duplicating equal ranges before building/merging the range trees seems sufficient).

### Reproduction

https://github.com/ninjin-sirisiri/v8-coverage-duplicate-ranges-crash

```sh
# standalone library-level repro (crashes everywhere)
node merge-repro.mjs

# full vitest repro (crashes under Bun runtime)
bun install
bunx --bun vitest run --coverage
```

title: Worker RPC timeout (birpc DEFAULT_TIMEOUT 60s) is not configurable — green runs exit 1 on loaded CI runners
body:
### Clear and concise description of the problem

The worker→host birpc channel is created with birpc's `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` of 60 s, and there is no configuration path to change it: `createRuntimeRpc` builds the client without a `timeout` option, and none of the `poolOptions`/runner options map to it.

On a loaded CI runner (4 vCPU, a monorepo test job running many packages concurrently), the host process that answers `onTaskUpdate` can be starved past 60 s for a single ACK. The result is a run where **every test file passes** and the process still exits 1:

```
Error: [vitest-worker]: Timeout calling "onTaskUpdate"
 Test Files  161 passed (161)
      Tests  3624 passed | 3 skipped (3627)
     Errors  1 error
```

We saw this repeatedly on GitHub-hosted runners (vitest 3.2.7, forks pool, coverage on). Capping `maxWorkers` reduced the load but did not eliminate the timeout — the bottleneck is the host loop, not the worker count. Related (browser-mode flavour of the same constant): #4497.

### Suggested solution

Expose the worker RPC timeout as a configuration option (e.g. under `poolOptions` or a top-level `workerRpcTimeout`), so CI environments can trade patience for reliability. A timeout that is configurable cannot mask a failing test — results still travel the same channel and a red still reports red; test execution stays bounded by `testTimeout`.

### Alternative

We currently carry a two-line `pnpm patch` on `vitest@3.2.7` adding `timeout: 300000` to the worker-side birpc client options in `createRuntimeRpc`. It works, but it is pinned to a content-hashed dist chunk and has to be re-derived on every upgrade.

### Additional context

Happy to send a PR if a maintainer confirms the preferred config surface.

title: 5.0.0: shipped .d.ts files (config.d.ts `@vitest/expect`, browser `MarkOptions`) fail type-checking without skipLibCheck
body:
## Bug Description

In 5.0.0, importing from `vitest/config` and running `tsc` with `skipLibCheck: false` fails with
two errors that come from **vitest's own bundled `.d.ts` files**, not from user code:

```
node_modules/vitest/config.d.ts(2,21): error TS2307: Cannot find module '@vitest/expect' or its corresponding type declarations.
node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/plugin.d.BbcoZhuj.d.ts(11,39): error TS2305: Module '"vitest/browser"' has no exported member 'MarkOptions'.
```

Both are dangling references to things a consumer never has:

1. **`@vitest/expect`** — `vitest/config.d.ts` line 2 does `import type {} from '@vitest/expect'`,
   but `@vitest/expect` is declared only in vitest's **devDependencies** (not `dependencies` or
   `peerDependencies`), so it is never installed in a consumer's tree. `npm ls @vitest/expect` in a
   fresh `npm i vitest@5` project prints `(empty)`. The 5.0 migration inlined `@vitest/expect`
   at runtime — this looks like a type-side import that was missed.

2. **`MarkOptions`** — `vitest/dist/chunks/plugin.d.*.d.ts` does
   `import { CDPSession, BrowserCommands, MarkOptions } from 'vitest/browser'`, but `vitest/browser`
   does not export `MarkOptions`. This is the same class of problem as #8662 (`BrowserCommands` from
   `vitest/browser`), fixed by #8666 — so `MarkOptions` looks like a **regression / missed member**
   of that fix.

**Expected:** vitest's published types type-check standalone (as on 4.x), so no errors.
**Actual:** the two errors above. `skipLibCheck: true` makes them disappear, confirming both come
from vitest's declaration files. Reproduces under both `moduleResolution: "bundler"` and `"nodenext"`,
and with TypeScript 5.x and 6.x.

Suggested fix:
1. Remove the leftover `import type {} from '@vitest/expect'` from `vitest/config.d.ts` (or move
   `@vitest/expect` to `dependencies`).
2. Export `MarkOptions` from `vitest/browser` (as #8666 did for `BrowserCommands`).

title: Coverage `text` reporter prints an empty table frame under agent detection when every file is 100% covered
body:
## Description

When vitest detects it is running under an AI agent, it forces `skipFull: true` onto the coverage `text` reporter and appends a `text-summary` reporter.

`skipFull` makes istanbul's text reporter omit any row whose metrics are all 100%. In a project where *every* file is fully covered, that removes every row — but the table header and rules are still emitted, so the output is a frame with no body:

```
 % Coverage report from v8
----------|---------|----------|---------|---------|-------------------
File      | % Stmts | % Branch | % Funcs | % Lines | Uncovered Line #s
----------|---------|----------|---------|---------|-------------------
----------|---------|----------|---------|---------|-------------------

=============================== Coverage summary ===============================
Statements   : 100% ( 1/1 )
Branches     : 100% ( 0/0 )
Functions    : 100% ( 1/1 )
Lines        : 100% ( 1/1 )
================================================================================
```

Forcing `skipFull` under an agent is reasonable on its own terms — hiding fully-covered rows is exactly the noise reduction it is going for, and `text-summary` compensates for what is lost. The empty frame looks like an unhandled edge of that, rather than intended output: it spends tokens to communicate nothing, which is the opposite of the goal. It is also mildly alarming to read, since an empty coverage table is what a broken `include` glob or a wrong working directory looks like.

This is cosmetic — `lcov.info` is byte-identical between an agent run and a non-agent run, and thresholds are still enforced.

## Steps to Reproduce

Minimal project — one source file, one spec, full coverage:

```ts
// src/a.ts
export function add(a: number, b: number) { return a + b }
```

```ts
// src/a.spec.ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest'
import { add } from './a.js'
test('add', () => { expect(add(1, 2)).toBe(3) })
```

```ts
// vitest.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from 'vitest/config'
export default defineConfig({
  test: {
    coverage: { provider: 'v8', include: ['src/**'], reporter: ['text', 'lcov'] }
  }
})
```

Then:

```sh
# empty frame
CLAUDECODE=1 vitest run --coverage

# rows render
env -u AI_AGENT -u CLAUDECODE vitest run --coverage
```

Toggling only the agent env var flips the behaviour in both directions. Any variable `std-env` treats as agent detection reproduces it; `CLAUDECODE=1` alone is sufficient.

## Expected Behavior

When `skipFull` eliminates every row, do not print the table at all — the `text-summary` block already carries the totals. Keeping the `All files` summary row would also be an improvement over the current output.

## Actual Behavior

The table header and both horizontal rules are printed with no rows between them.

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS (Noble Numbat), WSL2, kernel 6.18.33.2-microsoft-standard-WSL2
- Architecture: x86_64
- Runtime: Node v26.7.0
- Package manager: npm 12.0.2

IIRC, the documentation and code are written as intended. `toFake` and `toNotFake` aren't clean compliment unfortunately. While faking `nextTick` breaks vitest folks, faking `queueMicrotask` can still work depending on the use case (iirc it was node `fetch` API becomes broken).

That said, the current behavior may not be so ergonomic and documentation is vague about the intended behavior. I think forcing both `nextTick` and `queueMicrotask` in `toNotFake` when using `toNotFake` API is good.

- https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/7505

title: v5 browser mode no longer serves /mockServiceWorker.js (undocumented)
body:
### Describe the bug

Vitest 4.1 browser mode served MSW's worker at `/mockServiceWorker.js` via the `vitest:browser:resolve-virtual` plugin. `setupWorker().start()` worked with no `public/` file.

That plugin is gone in 5.0.0. Same `start()` now 404s:

```
[MSW] Failed to register a Service Worker for scope ('http://localhost:…/') with script ('http://localhost:…/mockServiceWorker.js'): Service Worker script does not exist at the given path.

Did you forget to run "npx msw init <PUBLIC_DIR>"?
```

The [v5 migration guide](https://vitest.dev/guide/migration/) does not mention this. I only found it by reading the plugin source after the tests failed.

This looks like leftover fallout from #7556 / #7576 (stop bundling MSW, mock modules with `page.route`). Fair change. The resolve was still in 4.1.10 though, so anyone who relied on it hits a wall on 5.0 with no note in the guide.

4.1.10 still has the virtual resolve:

https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/v4.1.10/packages/browser/src/node/plugin.ts#L313-L320

```ts
{
  name: 'vitest:browser:resolve-virtual',
  async resolveId(rawId) {
    if (rawId === '/mockServiceWorker.js') {
      return this.resolve('msw/mockServiceWorker.js', distRoot, {
        skipSelf: true,
      })
    }
  },
},
```

5.0.0's plugin list does not.

I am not asking to bring MSW back as a Vitest dependency. Either restore a tiny resolve that maps `/mockServiceWorker.js` to the project's `msw` package, or say in the migration guide that browser-mode `setupWorker()` now needs `msw init public`.

### Reproduction

1. Vitest 4.1 browser project with `setupWorker()` from `msw/browser` in a setup file. No `public/mockServiceWorker.js`.
2. `worker.start()` succeeds.
3. Upgrade to 5.0.0. Do not add a public worker file.
4. `worker.start()` throws the MSW "script does not exist" error.

Workaround that unblocked us: `msw init public --save` and commit the generated file.

### System Info

```
vitest: 5.0.0 (broke)
vitest: 4.1.10 (worked)
@vitest/browser-playwright: 5.0.0
msw: 2.15.0 (unchanged across the upgrade)
```

### Used Package Manager

pnpm

title: `typecheck`: Custom DOM matchers (`toHaveTextContent`, `toHaveAttribute`) missing from `Assertion` types in v5.0.0
body:
### Describe the bug

After upgrading to `vitest@5.0.0`, `tsc --noEmit` fails with type errors on standard DOM matchers provided by `@testing-library/jest-dom` (such as `toHaveTextContent` and `toHaveAttribute`), even though tests execute and pass successfully at runtime.

The type error indicates that `Assertion<void, HTMLElement>` no longer includes these extended properties:

```text
error TS2339: Property 'toHaveTextContent' does not exist on type 'Assertion<void, HTMLElement>'.
error TS2339: Property 'toHaveAttribute' does not exist on type 'Assertion<void, HTMLElement>'.

```

This appears to stem from a regression or breaking change in how `vitest` exports its internal assertion namespace or interface boundaries in v5, preventing ambient module declarations from properly augmenting `Assertion<R, T>` or `Matchers<R, T>`.


### Reproduction

1. Setup a minimal project with `vitest@5.0.0` and `@testing-library/jest-dom`.

2. Add a setup file importing `@testing-library/jest-dom` 
3. Create a test asserting on a DOM element:```ts
import { test, expect } from 'vitest';

```ts
test('DOM assertions', () => {
  const el = document.createElement('div');
  el.textContent = 'Hello World';
  el.setAttribute('data-testid', 'custom-el');

  expect(el).toHaveTextContent('Hello World');
  expect(el).toHaveAttribute('data-testid', 'custom-el');
});

```


4. Run `pnpm tsc --noEmit`.

**Expected:** Type checking passes without errors when ambient matchers are imported.

**Actual:** `TS2339: Property 'toHaveTextContent' does not exist on type 'Assertion<void, HTMLElement>'`.

The import `@testing-library/jest-dom` doesn't give type anymore likely related to this breaking change about jest global types

title: Worker catchError can loop forever on dead IPC channel (OOM → SIGABRT) — onError guard doesn't cover it
body:
## Summary

A `forks`-pool worker orphaned by a main process that dies **without pool teardown** can enter an unbounded `catchError → rpc.onUnhandledError → process.send` loop on the dead IPC channel and OOM (~3.5 GB observed in a core dump, then a fatal ~1 GB allocation in `FormatStackTraceToString` → SIGABRT). The existing `onError` guard in `init-forks` only covers the process `'error'` event, not this re-entrant report path.

## Observed incident

- Command shape: `npx vitest run <file> 2>&1 | head -120`. `head` exits early → EPIPE on the main's stdout → main dies mid-report with no final summary and **no pool teardown**.
- The orphaned worker (mid-file, event loop held by jsdom/react-query timers) survived with a dead IPC channel. A timer callback later threw an out-of-test assertion (`listOnTimeout` frames in the core).
- The worker's error reporter (`catchError → rpc.onUnhandledError → process.send`) failed on the closed channel as a floating rejection → `unhandledRejection` → `catchError`… Core dump: **873,759 iterations × ~4 KB ≈ 3.5 GB**, then a fatal ~1 GB alloc in `FormatStackTraceToString` → SIGABRT.

## Code path (vitest 4.1.11)

- `catchError` (`dist/chunks/init.*.js`, installed by `listenForErrors`) fire-and-forgets the report: `state().rpc.onUnhandledError(error, type)` — the returned promise is never handled.
- RPC is birpc with `timeout: -1`, `post: (v) => process.send(v)`.
- `init-forks` installs `process.on("error", onError)` → `processExit(1)` on `ERR_IPC_CHANNEL_CLOSED`/`EPIPE`, with the comment "Prevent leaving worker in loops where it tries to send message to closed main thread, errors, and tries to send the error." That covers sends that surface as a process `'error'`, but not the floating-rejection re-entry above.

## One data point that needs your characterization

In a bare-child probe (`child_process.fork`, `process.send` 2 s after the parent's SIGKILL), `send()` returned `false` plus an async `ERR_IPC_CHANNEL_CLOSED` process error — which `onError` would catch. So the exact condition under which the report promise *rejects* (looping via `unhandledRejection`) instead of the process error being delivered first is unclear to us; a tight enough re-entry loop would also starve the async delivery. The core dump is ground truth that the loop happened (~874k iterations).

## Suggested directions

- Check channel liveness (e.g. `process.connected`) in `catchError` before reporting, and exit the worker instead when the channel is known-dead.
- Attach a rejection handler to the fire-and-forget `rpc.onUnhandledError(...)` call that exits the worker (it currently floats).
- Optionally exit a forks worker on `disconnect` (the pool tears workers down via SIGTERM→SIGKILL and never `.disconnect()`s, so `disconnect` implies a dead parent).

## Repro sketch (not yet a minimal deterministic repro — being upfront)

Single file, `--pool=forks`, with a test that prints its pid, settles a few seconds, then throws uncaught ~10 s in; SIGKILL the main once settled; cap the heap (`NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=512`) and watch worker RSS. Our attempts so far exited via `onError` or idled without looping — the incident needed a later throw plus (presumably) the reject-instead-of-emit timing. Happy to help narrow this down.

## Environment

- vitest 4.1.11, node v24.19.0, linux x64, `pool: 'forks'`

## Our local mitigation (context only, not proposed as the upstream fix)

- `globalSetup`: swallow EPIPE on the main's stdout/stderr (truncated pipe no longer kills the main; exit code stays the tests').
- `setupFiles`: `process.once('disconnect', () => process.exit(1))` — verified the orphan now exits ~100 ms after the parent's death instead of surviving.

title: `process.env.NODE_ENV` define breaks JSX in browser mode in Vitest 5, worked in Vitest 4
body:
### Describe the bug A `define` for `process.env.NODE_ENV` breaks JSX in browser mode on Vitest 5. Every JSX expression throws `TypeError: _jsxDEV is not a function`. The same config works on Vitest 4. The two halves of the run end up disagreeing about `NODE_ENV`: - Vite computes `isProduction` from the Node process. Vitest sets `process.env.NODE_ENV ??= 'test'`, so `isProduction` is `false` and JSX is compiled against `react/jsx-dev-runtime`. - In the page, `process.env.NODE_ENV` is `'production'`. Vite's dev client materializes every `define` entry as a global (`vite/dist/client/env.mjs` walks the dotted key), so the page gets `process = { env: { NODE_ENV: 'production' } }`. Pre-bundled deps are not `define`-substituted, so they read that global. The optimized `react/jsx-dev-runtime` still contains a literal `process.env.NODE_ENV === "production"` check, takes the production branch, and that build exports `jsxDEV` as `undefined` (`exports.jsxDEV = void 0`). So the compiled call site and the module it calls come from different worlds. On Vitest 4 this worked because `deleteDefineConfig` ran unconditionally from a `config()` hook and hoisted `process.env.*` defines into the real Node environment. That happens before Vite computes `isProduction`, so Vite saw `production` and compiled JSX to `react/jsx-runtime`'s `jsx`/`jsxs`. Vitest 5 added a browser-mode branch in `TestConfigPlugin` that skips the hoist and leaves the entry on `config.define`: ```js else if (isBrowserEnabled) { resolvedTestConfig.defines = config.define || {} } ``` #11198 later changed that branch to `resolvedTestConfig.defines = {}`, which fixes #11164 but does not change this: `config.define` still stays on the Vite config, so the page global is still created and the Node process still says `test`. `react/jsx-dev-runtime` is the loudest symptom, not the only one. Any pre-bundled dependency that branches on `process.env.NODE_ENV` now takes a different branch than the one Vite compiled for, and `isProduction` also drives Vite's `production`/`development` resolve conditions. ### Reproduction The Playwright provider doesn't work in StackBlitz, so the reproduction needs to run locally. https://stackblitz.com/edit/vitejs-vite-z6tevmn7 On `vitest@5.0.0` / `@vitest/browser-playwright@5.0.0`: ``` FAIL |chromium| src/repro.test.tsx > creates an element TypeError: _jsxDEV is not a function ❯ src/repro.test.tsx:4:19 3| test('creates an element', () => { 4| const element =
hello
; | ^ ``` Downgrade both to `4.1.11` (and add `@vitest/browser@4.1.11`), delete `node_modules/.vite`, and the same files pass: ``` RUN v4.1.11 Test Files 1 passed (1) Tests 1 passed (1) ``` To see the disagreement directly, read the global through a key `define` cannot rewrite: ```ts const p = (globalThis as any)[['pro', 'cess'].join('')]; console.log(p.env); // { NODE_ENV: 'production' } — while Vite compiled for development ``` ### System Info ```shell System: OS: macOS 26.6.2 CPU: (12) arm64 Apple M4 Pro Memory: 1.30 GB / 48.00 GB Shell: 5.9 - /bin/zsh Binaries: Node: 22.23.2 npm: 10.9.8 pnpm: 10.34.4 Browsers: Chrome: 152.0.7977.83 Safari: 26.6.2 npmPackages: @vitejs/plugin-react: 6.1.1 => 6.1.1 @vitest/browser-playwright: ^5.0.0 => 5.0.0 react: 19.2.8 => 19.2.8 vitest: ^5.0.0 => 5.0.0 ``` ### Used Package Manager npm ### Validations - [x] Follow our [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) - [x] Read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). - [x] Read the [docs](https://vitest.dev/guide/). - [x] Check that there isn't [already an issue](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/issues) that reports the same bug to avoid creating a duplicate. - [x] Check that this is a concrete bug.
