title: `--silent` is ignored when the `minimal` (agent) reporter is active
body:
### Describe the bug

When Vitest detects an AI coding agent environment, the default reporter becomes `minimal` (`reporters: [isAgent ? 'minimal' : 'default']`). `MinimalReporter` hardcodes `silent` in its constructor:

```ts
// packages/vitest/src/node/reporters/minimal.ts
constructor(options: DefaultReporterOptions = {}) {
  super({ silent: 'passed-only', ...options, summary: false })
}
```

`DefaultReporter` only falls back to the user's config in `onInit` (`this.silent ??= this.ctx.config.silent`), so with the minimal reporter `this.silent` is already set and an explicit `--silent=true` / `--silent=false` on the CLI (or `silent` in the config) is silently ignored. The behavior stays `passed-only` no matter what the user passes.

This is confusing to debug: the CLI parses the flag fine (`--silent=bogus` even throws the expected `TypeError`), `BaseReporter.shouldLog` looks correct, yet the value never takes effect — until you notice the reporter never reads `config.silent`.

The [Minimal Reporter docs](https://vitest.dev/guide/reporters#minimal-reporter) describe the reduced output ("Console logs from passing tests and the summary section are also suppressed"), but do not mention that an explicitly provided `silent` setting is overridden.

Expected: an explicit `silent` (CLI flag or config) should win over the minimal reporter's default — e.g. only default to `'passed-only'` when the user did not set one. Alternatively, document the override.

Workaround: passing it as a reporter option does work, because options are spread after the hardcoded default: `reporters: [['minimal', { silent: true }]]`.

### Reproduction

https://github.com/ossan-engineer/vitest-silent-repro

Two files (plus the pnpm lockfile):

```json
// package.json
{
  "name": "vitest-silent-repro",
  "private": true,
  "type": "module",
  "scripts": {
    "test": "vitest run"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "vitest": "5.0.0"
  }
}
```

```js
// silent.test.js
import { describe, expect, it } from 'vitest'

describe('silent repro', () => {
  it('passes', () => {
    console.log('MARKER_PASS_LOG')
    expect(1).toBe(1)
  })
  it('fails', () => {
    console.log('MARKER_FAIL_LOG')
    expect(1).toBe(2)
  })
})
```

Run `pnpm install`, then run each command piped (non-TTY) and check which `MARKER_*` logs appear:

| command | MARKER_PASS_LOG | MARKER_FAIL_LOG |
|---|---|---|
| `pnpm vitest run` | shown | shown |
| `pnpm vitest run --silent=true` | hidden | hidden |
| `pnpm vitest run --silent=passed-only` | hidden | shown |
| `AI_AGENT=1 pnpm vitest run` | hidden | shown |
| `AI_AGENT=1 pnpm vitest run --silent=true` | hidden | **shown (bug — expected hidden)** |
| `AI_AGENT=1 pnpm vitest run --silent=passed-only` | hidden | shown |

With `AI_AGENT=1` (or any other agent marker std-env detects, e.g. `CLAUDECODE`), the output is identical for all three `silent` values — the flag has no effect.

body:
### Describe the bug

Under `environment: 'jsdom'`, a `Blob` or `File` used as a request body arrives as the literal string `undefined`. Nothing throws, so a test uploading a file passes while sending nine bytes of ASCII instead of its content.

```ts
const blob = new Blob(['hello world'], { type: 'text/plain' })
const text = await new Request('http://x.test/', { method: 'POST', body: blob }).text()
```

| environment | `text` |
| --- | --- |
| node | `"hello world"` |
| happy-dom | `"hello world"` |
| jsdom | `"undefined"` |

Same for a `File` inside `FormData`: the multipart part body is `undefined`, and `fetch(URL.createObjectURL(blob))` returns `undefined` too.

### Cause

`makeCompatBlob` in `packages/vitest/src/integrations/env/jsdom.ts` bridges jsdom's `Blob` to Node's `fetch` by reading a private field:

```ts
const buffer = (blob as any)[implSymbol]._buffer
return new NodeBlob_([buffer], { type: blob.type })
```

jsdom 28.0.0 renamed that field to `_bytes`, so the read is `undefined` and `new Blob([undefined])` stringifies it.

| jsdom | impl keys |
| --- | --- |
| 24.1.3 – 27.4.0 | `_buffer,_globalObject,type` |
| 28.1.0 – 29.1.1 | `_globalObject,type,_bytes` |

Vitest's own devDependency is `jsdom: ^29.1.1`, so the default combination is the broken one. The existing tests in `test/unit/test/environments/jsdom.spec.ts` use an empty `new Blob()` and only assert `toBeInstanceOf`, which is why CI stays green.

### Reproduction

The snippet above, in any project with `vitest@5.0.1` and `jsdom@29`, run once per `environment`. A single test file:

```ts
import { expect, test } from 'vitest'

test('blob bytes survive a Request body', async () => {
  const blob = new Blob(['hello world'], { type: 'text/plain' })
  const text = await new Request('http://x.test/', { method: 'POST', body: blob }).text()
  expect(text).toBe('hello world')
})
```

Passes with `--environment=node` and `--environment=happy-dom`, fails with `--environment=jsdom`.

### System Info

```
vitest 5.0.1
jsdom 29.1.1
node 22.18.0
win32 x64
```

### Used Package Manager

npm

### Validations

- [x] Follow our Code of Conduct
- [x] Read the Contributing Guidelines
- [x] Read the docs
- [x] Check that there isn't already an issue that reports the same bug
- [x] Check that this is a concrete bug
- [x] The provided reproduction is a minimal reproducible example of the bug

I used Claude to help investigate this. I ran the reproduction myself across the three environments and the six jsdom versions above.

title: Regression in Vitest 5: spying on Set.prototype.add causes a stack overflow
body:
### Describe the bug

Spying on `Set.prototype.add` causes infinite recursion in Vitest `5.0.1` when the method is called:

```js
import { expect, it, vi } from 'vitest'

it('can spy on Set.prototype.add', () => {
  const spy = vi.spyOn(Set.prototype, 'add')
  try {
    new Set([1])
    expect(spy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(1)
  } finally {
    spy.mockRestore()
  }
})
```

Expected: the test passes and the spy records the call, as it does on Vitest `4.1.10` and `4.1.11`.

Actual: the test fails with `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded`. The stack repeatedly enters `Set.add` in `@vitest/spy/dist/index.js`.

This also reproduces with `@vitest/spy` alone in plain Node, without the Vitest runner or Vite. Each mock invocation in [5.0.1's spy implementation](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/v5.0.1/packages/spy/src/index.ts#L503) calls `DIRTY_MOCK_STATES.add(...)`, which calls the spied method again. This bookkeeping was added in [#11092](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/pull/11092).

### Reproduction

[Minimal reproduction repository](https://github.com/why-reproductions-are-required/vitest-set-add-spy-recursion)

```sh
git clone https://github.com/why-reproductions-are-required/vitest-set-add-spy-recursion.git
cd vitest-set-add-spy-recursion
npm ci
npm test
```

For the smaller Node-only reproduction:

```sh
npm run repro:spy
```

Both commands exit with code 1 and a stack overflow on `5.0.1`, which was the latest stable release when checked on 2026-09-17. Both pass on `4.1.10` and `4.1.11`. The README contains the comparison commands. Vite remains pinned to `8.3.0` in all cases.

### System Info

```text
System:
  OS: macOS 26.2
  CPU: (16) arm64 Apple M4 Max
Binaries:
  Node: 24.21.0
  npm: 11.19.0
npmPackages:
  @vitest/spy: 5.0.1
  vite: 8.3.0
  vitest: 5.0.1
```

### Used Package Manager

npm

author: fengmk2
maintainer_reply:
This specifically hit `Set.prototype` but technically other primitive like `Map/Array.prorotype` are used internally of course, so likely those mocking will crash Vitest. I'm not sure how far we should guard against this in general, but fixing this specific regression of `Set.prorotype.add` seems reasonable to fix.

If we were to be completely free from primitive mocking effect, then it would require some primordial utility like Node does internally and stash all relevant prototype methods, which is too tedious to deal with, so it's likely out of scope:

```js
const setAdd = Set.prototype.add.call.bind(Set.prototype.add)
const mapSet = Map.prototype.set.call.bind(Map.prototype.set)
...
```

title: `vitest.config.config` is `undefined` in v5 when the config file is auto-detected
body:
### Describe the bug

Reporters rely on `vitest.config.config` to know which config a run used.

- In Vitest 4, `vitest.config.config` held the absolute path of the config file Vitest loaded, even when the file was found automatically.
- In Vitest 5.0.0 it is `undefined` unless `--config` is passed. When `--config` is passed, it holds the raw CLI string (e.g. `vitest.config.ts`) instead of a resolved path.


### Reproduction

A project with two files:

`vitest.config.mjs`:

```js
export default {}
```

`repro.mjs`:

```js
import { createVitest } from 'vitest/node'
const vitest = await createVitest('test', {})
console.log(vitest.version, vitest.config.config)
await vitest.close()
```

Run:

```sh
npm i -D vitest@5
node repro.mjs
```

Output:

- **4.1.10:** `4.1.10 /abs/path/repro/vitest.config.mjs`
- **5.0.0:** `5.0.0 undefined`

With no config file at all, both versions print `undefined`, so the regression only affects config files that Vitest finds automatically.

### Workaround

`vitest.vite.config.configFile` still has the resolved absolute path.


### System Info

```shell
System:
    OS: macOS 26.6.2
    CPU: (10) arm64 Apple M1 Max
    Memory: 258.22 MB / 32.00 GB
    Shell: 3.2.57 - /bin/bash

    npm: 11.17.0 - /Users/aslushnikov/.local/share/mise/installs/node/latest/bin/npm

```

pnpm

title: A dynamic import() inside a vi.hoisted factory silently drops the file's vi.mock registrations (5.0 regression, all pools)
body:
### Describe the bug

> **AI disclosure** (per [CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/vitest-dev/vitest/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)): the investigation and the text of this report were assisted by Claude. This is not an automated filing — the bug was hit while migrating a real 677-file suite from Vitest 4 to 5, and I will respond personally to any questions here.

When a `vi.hoisted()` factory **starts a dynamic `import()`**, the `vi.mock()` calls in that same file are intermittently never applied. The subject gets the *real* module, with no error and no warning — the only symptom is an assertion failure that looks like broken test logic.

It is load-dependent: a single file always passes, and a **different subset** of files fails on every run. In our real suite (677 files) this showed up as 1–4 files failing to collect per run, never the same ones, because the dropped mock was `server-only` — a module that throws on import:

```
Error: This module cannot be imported from a Client Component module. It should only be used from a Server Component.
 ❯ Object.<anonymous> node_modules/server-only/index.js:1:7
```

That made it look like an app bug rather than a mocking bug. The reduced repro below uses a plain value instead, so the silent-drop is visible directly.

**This is a v5 regression.** The same files are green on 4.1.11 and fail on 5.0.1.

It is **not** pool-specific, so I believe it is distinct from #11284 and #11289, which are both `vmThreads`-only (and #11284 explicitly reports itself as not a v5 regression). This reproduces on `forks`, `threads`, `vmThreads` and `vmForks`, with default isolation and no `deps.optimizer`.

### Reproduction

No config file, no plugins, default pool, default isolation.

```sh
mkdir vt5-hoisted-repro && cd vt5-hoisted-repro
npm init -y >/dev/null && npm pkg set type=module
npm i -D vitest@5.0.1

cat > dep.js <<'JS'
export const value = "real";
JS

cat > helper.js <<'JS'
export function makeHelper() {
  return { tag: "helper" };
}
JS

# 20 identical files; the bug needs a few files in flight to show up
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
cat > "a$i.test.js" <<'JS'
import { expect, it, vi } from "vitest";

const helper = vi.hoisted(async () => {
  const { makeHelper } = await import("./helper.js");
  return makeHelper();
});

vi.mock("./dep.js", () => ({ value: "mocked" }));

import { value } from "./dep.js";

it("applies the mock registered in this file", async () => {
  expect(await helper).toEqual({ tag: "helper" });
  expect(value).toBe("mocked");
});
JS
done

npx vitest run
```

Result on 5.0.1 — roughly half the files fail, a different set each run:

```
 FAIL  a1.test.js > applies the mock registered in this file
AssertionError: expected 'real' to be 'mocked' // Object.is equality

Expected: "mocked"
Received: "real"

 Test Files  11 failed | 9 passed (20)
```

On 4.1.11, the identical files are `20 passed (20)`.

### What isolates the trigger

Same 20 files, 5.0.1, default pool. Only the hoisted block changes.

| # | hoisted block | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | `vi.hoisted(async () => { await import(...) })` — baseline | **11 failed / 9 passed** |
| B | `vi.hoisted(() => ({ tag: "helper" }))` — sync, no import | 20 passed |
| C | `vi.hoisted(async () => ({ tag: "helper" }))` — async, no import | 20 passed |
| D | `vi.hoisted(() => import(...).then(...))` — sync, starts import, no `await` | **16 failed / 4 passed** |
| E | baseline, but `vi.mock` moved *above* the hoisted block | **14 failed / 6 passed** |
| F | memoised loader, import deferred to first `await` | 20 passed |

So it is the **initiation** of the dynamic import during the hoisted phase that matters, not the `await` (D fails, C passes), and source order of `vi.mock` relative to the hoist does not help (E). Deferring the import until after registration is the only thing that fixes it (F):

```js
const helper = vi.hoisted(() => {
  const load = () => import("./helper.js").then((m) => m.makeHelper());
  let pending;
  return () => (pending ??= load());
});

vi.mock("./dep.js", () => ({ value: "mocked" }));
```

### Pools and versions

20 files, same source.

| vitest | forks | threads | vmThreads | vmForks |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 5.0.1 | 14 failed | 15 failed | 17 failed | 13 failed |
| 4.1.11 | 20 passed | 20 passed | — | — |

File count matters only in that it needs a few files in flight: `N=1/2/4` passed, `N=10` failed 3, `N=20` failed 13, `N=50` failed 42.

### Expected behaviour

A `vi.hoisted()` factory that performs a dynamic `import()` should not affect whether the file's own `vi.mock()` registrations are applied. Either it keeps working as it did in v4, or — if starting a module load during hoisting is no longer supported — it should be a documented breaking change and ideally throw, rather than silently serve the real module.

The silence is the costly part: a dropped mock surfaces as an ordinary assertion failure or an unrelated import-time crash, in a different file on each run, with nothing pointing back at mocking.

### Vitest version

`vitest@5.0.1` (regression from `4.1.11`)

### System Info

```
System:
  OS: Linux 6.6 Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS (Noble Numbat) (WSL2)
  CPU: (12) x64 Intel(R) Core(TM) i5-10600KF CPU @ 4.10GHz
  Memory: 23.09 GB / 31.31 GB
Binaries:
  Node: 24.19.0
  npm: 11.13.0
npmPackages:
  vitest: 5.0.1
```

### Used Package Manager

npm
